a.title: Cyient DLM sees 25-30% growth in electronics design and manufacturing
a.content:
Cyient DLM expects its electronics design and manufacturing business to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 25-30% over the next three to five years, driven by rising demand for safety-critical electronics and products designed and developed in India.
The business includes contract manufacturing of electronics as well as the development of products where the company owns the underlying intellectual property (IP).
The company has an order book of around $1 billion for its own-designed electronic products over the seven-year period from FY27 to FY34, Kaushal Jadia, CTO, Cyient DLM said in an interaction with Fe. The figure is about five times the unit’s current revenue, even as it keeps more than 90% of that design-led business export-oriented.
“Over 90% is export. That’s been our legacy from an engineering services side, we have been working with the likes of Boeing and Airbus in commercial aviation, similarly in medical and automotive. Previously we were only doing engineering services, but now we are doing the whole bit, whenever there’s a custom need,” Jadia said, referring to the share of the company’s design business currently sold overseas. The company works with customers across Europe and the US on product design, certification and qualification.
A key focus for Cyient DLM is to develop safety-critical electronics for sectors such as commercial aviation, defence, automotive and railways. Its product portfolio includes power electronics, communication systems, radio-frequency (RF) and microwave systems, and displays. The company is increasingly focusing on products where it owns the design and IP. Jadia said the complete design cycle, from system design and hardware to software and certification is undertaken in-house in India.
For semiconductor fab equipment, however, the company operates as a contract manufacturer. It assembles electronic cards, wire harnesses and boxes used in semiconductor manufacturing equipment, purchasing components such as semiconductors and PCB blanks before assembling, testing and delivering the finished systems.
Cyient DLM currently has manufacturing operations in Mysore, Hyderabad, Bengaluru and the US, while its engineering operations are primarily based in Bengaluru.
While artificial intelligence and machine learning can help automate parts of verification and certification, Jadia said the underlying safety and certification requirements cannot be bypassed.
India’s cost structure also provides an advantage for developing such products. “Engineering costs in India are about 50% lower than in Western countries, while manufacturing costs can be around 15-20% lower even when semiconductors are imported,” Jadia said. He added that this combination of domestic engineering, product ownership and manufacturing could allow Indian firms to develop globally competitive electronics products rather than remaining limited to contract manufacturing.

a.title: TNPCB tells NGT Sun Pharma did not implement proposed expansion in Chengalpattu
a.content:
The Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board (TNPCB) has told the National Green Tribunal (NGT) that Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd.’s unit at Sathammai village in Chengalpattu district is currently operating within its existing permitted production capacity and has not undertaken the proposed expansion.
The submission was made in a recent report filed before the southern bench of the NGT following an appeal filed by K.R. Selvaraj Kumar of Meenavar Nala Sangam, challenging the environmental clearance granted to the company for expansion.
Consent to establish
According to the TNPCB report, the unit had originally obtained the Board’s consent to establish in 2005 and consent to operate in 2006 for manufacturing pharmaceutical products with a total production capacity of 25.5 tonnes a month. Subsequent consent orders permitted changes in sewage generation, trade effluent disposal and air pollution control measures, without an increase in the permitted product quantity.
The company later obtained environmental clearance from the Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change on March 31, 2022, for increasing its production capacity from 25.5 tonnes per month to 134.082 tonnes per month for active pharmaceutical ingredients within the existing plant. However, the TNPCB said the company had not obtained the Board’s consent to establish or consent to operate for the expansion.
A TNPCB inspection conducted on September 12, 2026, found that the unit was in operation but its production was within the existing consented capacity of 25.5 tonnes a month. The Board also recorded that no expansion activity had been carried out.
The dispute also relates to an earlier NGT order in an original application filed in 2020. The Tribunal had noted violations relating to the unit’s operation without environmental clearance for an earlier expansion and had confirmed an environmental compensation of ₹58.20 lakh for contamination of groundwater and soil. It had also directed payment of an interim compensation of ₹10 crore and asked the TNPCB to assess any additional compensation for operation beyond the permitted pollution load.
The TNPCB report said the company subsequently obtained the 2022 environmental clearance for the proposed expansion and renewed consent from the Board valid up to March 31, 2028, but had not obtained consent specifically for carrying out the expansion.

a.title: Sun Pharma Recalls Lidocaine Ointment, Nystatin Cream in US Over Quality Issues
a.content:
Sun Pharma Recalls Lidocaine Ointment, Nystatin Cream in US Over Quality Issues
New Delhi: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries has initiated voluntary recalls of Lidocaine Ointment USP, 5%, and Nystatin Cream USP in the United States following quality-related issues identified during testing, according to the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) recall information.
The company is recalling 65,328 jars of Lidocaine Ointment USP, 5%, Spearmint Flavor, supplied in 50 g jars as a prescription-only product. The ointment is manufactured by Taro Pharmaceuticals Inc., Brampton, Ontario, Canada, and distributed in the US by Taro Pharmaceuticals U.S.A. Inc., Hawthorne, New York.
The affected product carries NDC 51672-3008-5 and belongs to Lot AD48154, with an expiration date of April 30, 2027.
The Lidocaine recall was initiated after the product failed to meet content uniformity specifications. According to the FDA recall information, the product was found to be out of specification for assay during analysis at the 24-month long-term stability station under storage conditions of 25°C and 60% relative humidity.
The recall is listed under D-0848-2026 and Event ID 99794 and has been classified as a Class II recall. The voluntary recall was initiated by the firm on August 31, 2026, while the FDA centre classification date was September 15, 2026. The recall covers nationwide distribution across the US.
A Class II recall refers to a situation in which use of, or exposure to, a violative product may cause temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences, while the probability of serious adverse health consequences is considered remote.
Separately, Sun Pharma is recalling an undisclosed quantity of Nystatin Cream USP, a prescription-only antifungal product supplied in 15 g tubes, after the product failed to meet stability specifications.
The Nystatin Cream is manufactured by Taro Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd., Haifa Bay, Israel, and distributed in the US by Taro Pharmaceuticals U.S.A. Inc., Hawthorne, New York. The product carries NDC 51672-1289-1.
The recall involves Lot AD49605 and Lot AD49606, both carrying an expiration date of May 31, 2027. The recall is identified as D-0872-2026 under Event ID 99876 and has an updated Class II classification.
The Nystatin recall was voluntarily initiated by the firm on September 14, 2026, while the FDA centre classification date was September 25, 2026. The distribution pattern covers the US nationwide.
The two recalls involve different Taro manufacturing facilities and separate recall numbers. The Lidocaine Ointment recall concerns an assay and content uniformity issue, while the Nystatin Cream recall relates to a failure of stability specifications. ETPharma also reported the recalls based on the FDA's latest enforcement report.
Lidocaine is a local anaesthetic used to temporarily numb an area and reduce pain by blocking pain signals from nerves, while Nystatin is an antifungal medicine used to treat fungal infections. Both products are prescription-only drugs.

a.title: Nykaa raises the stakes, becomes brand incubator
a.content:
Nykaa is no longer content with being the platform where beauty brands are sold. With its latest partnership with L’Oréal’s corporate venture capital arm BOLD, India’s largest beauty retailer is moving further upstream — identifying, nurturing, and investing in brands that could shape the next phase of the beauty market.
The two companies will jointly take minority stakes in high-growth Indian beauty, personal care, and wellness companies, while founders retain ownership and operational control. The investment corpus and size of individual investments have not been disclosed. Beyond capital, the partners will offer mentorship, beauty expertise, and access to their networks.
For Nykaa, the move builds on a strategy that began well before the L’Oréal deal.
In 2022, Nykaa partnered with Estée Lauder Companies’ New Incubation Ventures to launch BEAUTY&YOU India, an entrepreneurship programme aimed at discovering and supporting Indian beauty brands, according to executives at the firm. The programme offered financial support, mentorship, industry access and distribution support through Nykaa. Its inaugural winners included Skinvest, Bahut Beauty and Yaan Man. The programme has since become a recurring platform. In its fifth edition in 2026, Estée Lauder described Nykaa as a “launch partner” bringing consumer understanding, market expertise & distribution at scale.
Nykaa has also extended the incubation idea beyond products. In 2025, it partnered with Snapchat to launch the Nykaa Snap Star Beauty Incubator Programme, targeting Gen Z beauty creators and giving them access to Nykaa launches, creative formats and Snapchat technology.
The BOLD partnership is different, however. Unlike an awards or creator programme, it brings equity capital into the equation. “India is one of the most exciting beauty markets in the world,” said Jacques Lebel, managing director, L’Oréal India. He said the partnership would back founders with capital, mentorship and L’Oréal’s beauty expertise while allowing them to build independently.
Anchit Nayar, executive director and chief executive officer, Nykaa Beauty, said the ober-a-decade-long relationship between Nykaa and L’Oréal had given both companies an in-depth understanding of the Indian market. It has “allowed us to understand what it takes to build promising brands into an enduring one,” Nayar added.
The logic is straightforward: Nykaa brings consumer discovery, retail reach and distribution, while L’Oréal brings global beauty expertise. For a young brand, that combination potentially offers both capital and an accelerated route to market.
That is increasingly important as the Indian beauty and personal care market expands. The market is estimated at about $23 billion and is expected to reach roughly $40 billion by 2030, with premiumisation, digital adoption and younger consumers among the growth drivers, according to consultancy firm Redseer.
Analysts have already highlighted Nykaa’s owned brands and ecosystem as an important part of its growth proposition. Nomura, for instance, has said Nykaa’s platform, content ecosystem and owned brands could help it capture a disproportionate share of premium lifestyle spending. Jefferies has similarly pointed to the company’s expanding brand portfolio and premium assortment as drivers of longer-term margin expansion.
That makes the startup strategy strategically adjacent to Nykaa’s existing business rather than a complete departure from it. The company has been building its own portfolio, including Dot & Key, Nykaa Cosmetics, and Kay Beauty, while its retail platform gives emerging brands access to consumers and its content ecosystem helps drive discovery.

The pair will jointly invest in fast-growing Indian beauty brands, taking minority stakes that leave founders with full control over the business.
Tickets are now available for the 25th anniversary of the Pure Beauty Awards, taking place on 15 October 2026 at the Grosvenor House Hotel in London, UK. Join the beauty industry for an evening of recognition and celebration as this year’s winners are revealed. Click here to secure your place.
Beyond the financial backing, L’Oréal BOLD and Nykaa will also offer mentorship, guidance and the opportunity to benefit from each company’s expertise – L’Oréal’s global reach, and Nykaa’s retail network.
The partnership is designed to help scale Indian beauty brands faster, including their global reach.
“India is one of the most exciting beauty markets in the world, and its energy comes both from an expanding base of demanding consumers with rapidly evolving needs and from its ecosystem of tremendous entrepreneurs,” said Jacques Lebel, Managing Director, L'Oréal India.
“Through L’Oréal BOLD and this partnership with Nykaa, we want to stand behind that talent, backing founders with capital, mentorship, and L'Oréal's beauty expertise, while leaving them free to build their brands their way.
“Our commitment to India is stronger than ever, and this is the next major milestone in a journey of partnership and growth that we began over three decades ago.”
L’Oréal has already invested in India’s growing beauty ecosystem in recent years.
In January, the beauty giant announced it is investing €350m over the next five years to create its first global Beauty Tech Hub, which will be located in the city of Hyderabad, India.
L’Oréal’s Big Bang Beauty Tech Innovation Programme, which supports start-ups on commercial pilots in South Asia Pacific, Middle East and North Africa (SAPMENA), has entered its third year.
India has become a sought-after beauty market in 2026, amid a boom in investment and attention from global businesses.
Premium Indian brand RAS Luxury Skincare received a minority investment from conglomerate Dabur, and beauty retailer Nykaa confirmed talks on a potential acquisition of Indian skin care brand 82°E.
Unilever invested in perfume brand Secret Alchemist and skin care brand SkinInspired in January, and Estée Lauder Companies acquired skin care business Forest Essentials in March as part of a “long-term commitment to India”.
L’Oréal India is also allegedly in talks to take a majority stake in beauty company Innovist.
Anchit Nayar, Executive Director and CEO, Nykaa Beauty, said: “Nykaa and L'Oréal have been partners in India for over a decade, working together on our shared vision of making India into one of the world's largest and fastest-growing beauty markets.
“The experience and lessons we have learned along the way have allowed us to understand what it takes to build a promising brand into an enduring one.
“Combining our strong consumer ecosystem, deep retail network and wide distribution, along with L’Oréal’s global beauty expertise will be an incredibly valuable asset to the next generation of founders as they look to build consumer brands that India can be proud of.”

a.title: Nykaa partners with L’Oréal’s BOLD and completes 51% acquisition of Aminu Wellness
a.content:
The company popularly known as Nykaa, is an Indian consumer technology company operating across beauty, personal care, fashion and related categories. The company began as a digital-first beauty platform and has expanded into omnichannel retail, owned brands, fashion and B2B distribution.
The shares of Nykaa are currently trading atRs. 332.00, down by 0.91%. The company has a market capitalization of 95,094.59 crore. The stock’s 52 week high is Rs. 349.55 and its 52 week high is Rs. 227.90. In the past 6 months the stock has delivered a return of 36.05%.
What’s The News
FSN E-Commerce Ventures Limited, also known as Nykaa, and BOLD, a corporate venture capital fund of L'Oreal, are partnering to nurture the future crop of Indian beauty and personal care brands.
The two organizations would be making investments into promising Indian startups in the beauty, personal care and wellness space, which have good consumer acceptance and unique product offerings, by taking minority equity stakes.
The partnership will combine Nykaa’s consumer ecosystem, omnichannel retail network and understanding of the Indian market with L’Oréal’s global beauty expertise, network and mentoring capabilities. The companies said the objective is to help promising Indian beauty businesses scale while allowing founders to continue running their brands independently.
Neither Nykaa nor L’Oréal has disclosed the names of the startups that will receive investment under the new collaboration or the timeline for the first investments.
Nykaa Completes 51% Acquisition of Aminu Wellness
Additionally, Nykaa has successfully completed the acquisition of 51% stakeholding in Aminu Wellness Private Limited on a fully diluted basis post the approval by the Board of Directors in the month of August 2026.
The acquisition has been completed on 24th September 2026, once all transaction documents have been signed and the shareholding has been allotted to the demat account of Nykaa. The acquisition has made Aminu Wellness a subsidiary of Nykaa.
The acquisition of 51% stake has been approved by Nykaa at an amount of Rs. 32 crores. Aminu Wellness is in the beauty and personal care product industry with a specialization in skincare products. The company was incorporated in June 2019. It has manufacturing expertise in cosmetic products.
Strategic Significance
Both the two initiatives add value to Nykaa as a beauty retailer since it is able to not only access emerging consumer brands but also scale the businesses through its retail and distribution network via the BOLD program.
The Aminu Wellness acquisition means that Nykaa is now in control of a majority-owned beauty and personal care business which specializes in skincare.
By June 30, 2026, Nykaa had reportedly provided services to over 60 million customers using its online platforms and run 324 offline beauty destinations. Some of the owned brands from the company include Nykaa Cosmetics, Dot & Key, Kay Beauty, Nykaa Collections and Earth Rhythm.
Financial Performance
Looking at the quarterly results of FSN E-Commerce Ventures Limited (Nykaa), the company’s consolidated revenue from operations increased by 29.10 percent YoY, from Rs. 2,154.94 crore in Q1 FY26 to Rs. 2,782.00 crore in Q1 FY27, and grew by 5.05 percent QoQ from Rs. 2,648.17 crore in Q4 FY26. The company’s consolidated total income stood at Rs. 2,791.31 crore in Q1 FY27, compared with Rs. 2,164.27 crore in Q1 FY26 and Rs. 2,657.32 crore in Q4 FY26.
In Q1 FY27, Nykaa’s consolidated net profit increased by 225.95 percent YoY, reaching Rs. 79.76 crore, compared with Rs. 24.47 crore in Q1 FY26. On a sequential basis, consolidated net profit increased by 1.28 percent from Rs. 78.75 crore in Q4 FY26. The profit attributable to equity shareholders of the parent stood at Rs. 80.01 crore, compared with Rs. 23.32 crore in Q1 FY26 and Rs. 78.38 crore in Q4 FY26.
The company’s basic and diluted earnings per share stood at Rs. 0.28 in Q1 FY27, compared with Rs. 0.08 in Q1 FY26, registering an increase of 250 percent YoY. On a sequential basis, EPS increased from Rs. 0.27 in Q4 FY26 to Rs. 0.28 in Q1 FY27.
Investor Perspective
Collaboration with L'Oréal's BOLD unit and acquisition of Aminu Wellness can be seen as two different paths to extend Nykaa's beauty ecosystem. Whereas the partnership with BOLD will revolve around minority investments in emerging companies, the acquisition of Aminu Wellness means Nykaa owning a majority stake in an already established skincare-focused company.
In future, investors may keep a tab on the number of investments done through the BOLD-Nykaa partnership, performance and integration of Aminu Wellness, number of brands being developed internally by Nykaa and their contribution to its revenues.
Company Overview
FSN E-Commerce Ventures Limited, better known as Nykaa, is an India-based consumer technology company that operates within the beauty and personal care, fashion, and other segments. It started out as a beauty platform that leverages technology but has since diversified to include omni-channel retailing, owned brands, and fashion and B2B distribution.
The company has also been diversifying its owned brands by leveraging its e-commerce platforms and physical store network to give access to beauty brands in the domestic and international markets. Nykaa has also extended its operations into the beauty segment in the Middle East region through its Nysaa platform.

a.title: Yahoo Finance
a.content:
French cosmetics giant L'Oréal and Indian retail company Nykaa have entered a partnership to jointly back emerging beauty and personal care brands in India.
Under the alliance, L'Oréal's corporate venture capital arm, Business Opportunities for L'Oréal Development (BOLD), will work alongside Nykaa to acquire minority stakes in Indian beauty and wellness companies that have "strong consumer traction and distinctive propositions".
The two companies clarified that the funding will be strictly financial and minority in scope, leaving founders with complete ownership and control over their operations, teams, culture and creative direction.
L'Oréal India managing director Jacques Lebel said: "Through BOLD and this partnership with Nykaa, we want to stand behind that talent—backing founders with capital, mentorship, and L'Oréal's beauty expertise, while leaving them free to build their brands their way."
Alongside funding, the backed brands will receive mentorship and guidance from BOLD and Nykaa, as well as access to L'Oréal's international expertise in beauty and Nykaa's omnichannel retail infrastructure and knowledge of consumer behaviour.
The companies said their goal is to "help ambitious Indian beauty founders scale faster and build enduring brands for India and the world".
BOLD was set up in 2018 and backs companies across the beauty value chain, focusing on two areas: beauty and wellness brands, and science and technology for beauty.
Nykaa was established in 2012 by Falguni Nayar and has since evolved from an online beauty retailer into a broader group covering beauty, fashion and B2B operations, with brands such as Nykaa Fashion, Nykaa Man and Nykaa Superstore under its umbrella.
Nykaa Beauty executive director and CEO Anchit Nayar said: "Combining our strong consumer ecosystem, deep retail network and wide distribution, along with L'Oréal's global beauty expertise will be an incredibly valuable asset to the next generation of founders as they look to build consumer brands that India can be proud of."
Earlier this week, the Competition Commission of India approved L'Oréal India's acquisition of Onesto Labs, the entity that operates the Innovist personal care platform.

Nykaa (NYKAA): Inks investment deal with Loreal’s BOLD fund to invest in Indian beauty brands
Nykaa has inked an agreement with BOLD i.e. Business Opportunities for L’Oréal Development to invest in the coming generation of high growth Indian beauty & personal care brands. In addition to capital, Nykaa and BOLD will provide mentorship to their portfolio brands leveraging L’Oréal’s beauty experience and Nykaa’s panell distribution network. While L’Oréal India MD Jacques Lebel said that India is one of the most dynamic beauty markets in the world. No details on cheque size and corpus amount were shared.
Waaree Energies (WAAREEENER): Subsidiary to enter specialty gases business
Waaree Energies’ wholly owned subsidiary Waaree Clean Energy Solutions has decided to enter into the Specialty Gases business in India. The company aims to be a one stop shop for Specialty Gases for all Semiconductor and Solar cell manufacturing companies in India. Specialty Gases like Silane, Ammonia and Nitrogen Trifluoride are some of the examples which are used during etching and cleaning and deposition processes while manufacturing chips and solar cells. India imports most of these specialty gases from few international players. This is yet another step by Waaree to move up in the Electronics and Solar Value Chain. Earlier last month the company inked an MoU with WPPL and SGL to manufacture semiconductors in Gujarat. Alongside the company is already manufacturing Solar Cells, Modules and Green Hydrogen. Company didn’t mention any capex outlay but this is a lucrative segment that is expected to see significant growth.
Dr Lal PathLabs (LALPATHLAB): Board approves acquisition of 70% equity shareholding in SN Genelab
Board of Directors of Dr Lal PathLabs has approved to acquire 70% of the shares held by the shareholders of SN Genelab at a cash consideration of upto Rs 168 Crore. SN Genelab will become a subsidiary of Dr Lal Pathlabs once the transaction is completed. This will further add to the list of acquisitions done by the company in the space of diagnostics and pathology. The transaction is expected to complete by 30th Nov 2026 subject to certain terms and conditions.
Sterlite Technologies (STLTECH): Upsizes its Neuralis Data Center Portfolio to include 6,912 Fibers
Sterlite Technologies has expanded its Neuralis Data Center portfolio to include Pre Terminated Fiber Trunk Assemblies ranging from 48F to 6912F. These trunks will help provide connectivity between the data center servers in High Density applications typically seen in AI and Hyperscale data centers. These are assembled and tested at the factory using MTP/MPO Connectors in both Singlemode and Multimode. This eliminates the time taken to terminate each individual fiber in the data center. This follows the company’s recent launch of US certified Plenum rated Fiber Trunk Assemblies. Sterlite has been riding on the back of its growing data center business and reported its highest open orders of over Rs 18,600 Cr along with a healthy growth in QoQ profits in its latest quarter. The company will now offer all fiber counts from 48 to 6912 in their portfolio.
L&T Technology Services (LTTS): Joins hands with Cognite for Industrial AI Solutions
L&T Technology Services has partnered with Cognite a global leader in Industrial AI to provide joint offerings of Industrial AI and Data solutions to asset intensive industries. This partnership will help augment LTTS’ Engineering Intelligence portfolio with Cognitive’s offering in Industrial AI. Cognite uses a combination of its Data Platform and knowledge graphs to understand and create context for complex assets. This is an extension of several other partnerships the company has made in the space of Engineering Intelligence over the past year. This will allow asset intensive clients to benefit from data generated from their operations and engineering to make informed decisions on assets.

a.title: Beauty retailer Nykaa partners with L’Oréal’s BOLD to invest in emerging Indian beauty brands
a.content:
Beauty and fashion retailer Nykaa has partnered with BOLD, the corporate venture capital fund of L’Oréal, to jointly invest in emerging Indian beauty and personal care brands.
The two companies will take minority stakes in high-growth beauty and wellness brands that have established consumer traction and differentiated offerings, according to a regulatory filing by Nykaa.
The investments will be financial and minority in nature, with founders retaining operational and creative control of their businesses. The brands will continue to operate independently with their existing teams, culture and creative direction.
Beyond providing capital, Nykaa and BOLD will offer mentorship and guidance to the companies they back. The partnership will bring together L’Oréal’s global beauty expertise and Nykaa’s omnichannel retail network and understanding of Indian consumers.
The companies said the aim was to help Indian beauty founders scale their businesses and build brands for domestic and international markets.
Nykaa and L’Oréal deepen partnership
Jacques Lebel, Managing Director of L’Oréal India, said India was “one of the most exciting beauty markets in the world”, pointing to changing consumer needs and the country’s growing community of entrepreneurs.
He said BOLD and Nykaa will support founders with capital, mentorship and L’Oréal’s beauty expertise while allowing them to retain control over how their businesses develop.
Anchit Nayar, Executive Director and CEO of Nykaa Beauty, said: “Nykaa and L'Oreal have been partners in India for over a decade.”
Nayar said the experience gained from that relationship had helped Nykaa understand the challenges involved in building a promising brand into an enduring business.
He said Nykaa’s consumer ecosystem, retail network and distribution capabilities, combined with L’Oréal’s global beauty expertise, could support the next generation of Indian consumer brands.
What is BOLD?
BOLD, short for Business Opportunities for L’Oréal Development, was launched in 2018 as L’Oréal’s corporate venture capital fund.
It makes minority investments in innovative, high-growth businesses across the beauty value chain. Its investments include beauty and wellness brands as well as companies working in science and technology for beauty.
Alongside funding, BOLD provides portfolio companies with access to L’Oréal’s beauty expertise, global network and mentoring while preserving their independence.
L’Oréal launched BOLD as part of its wider strategy of working with startups and emerging businesses. The French beauty group has a portfolio of 40 international brands and employs more than 95,000 people.
L’Oréal recorded sales of €44.05 billion in 2025, up 4% on a like-for-like basis and 1.3% on a reported basis.
Nykaa expands its beauty ecosystem
Nykaa began in 2012 as a digital-first beauty company and has since expanded into physical retail, fashion and B2B commerce.
Its businesses include Nykaa Fashion, Nykaa Man and Nykaa Superstore. The company has also entered the Middle East through Nysaa, its omnichannel beauty retail offering in the region.
Nykaa has built its own portfolio of consumer brands, including Nykaa Cosmetics, Dot & Key, Kay Beauty, Nykaa Collections, Nykaa Wanderlust, Nykaa Perfumes and Earth Rhythm. Its fashion labels include Nykd by Nykaa, KICA, 20 Dresses, RSVP and Gajra Gang.
As of 30 June 2026, Nykaa said it had served more than 60 million customers through its online platforms and had 324 offline beauty destinations.
The partnership with BOLD gives Nykaa and L’Oréal a joint investment route into emerging Indian beauty businesses while allowing the founders of the companies they back to continue running their brands independently.

Nykaa said it has more than 60 million customers across its online platforms and 324 offline beauty destinations as of June 30, 2026.

MUMBAI, India and BRAMPTON, ON, Sept. 24, 2026 /CNW/ -- Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited (Reuters: SUN.BO, Bloomberg: SUNP IN, NSE: SUNPHARMA, BSE: 524715, together with its subsidiaries and/or affiliated companies, "Sun Pharma") today announced the commercial availability of Taro-Methylphenidate ER for Canadian patients in Ontario and Quebec.
Taro-Methylphenidate ER is the first and only bioequivalent to Concerta® with an osmotic delivery system indicated for the treatment of Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in patients six years of age and older.
"Finding the right treatment for someone with ADHD can be complicated," said Dr. Angelo Fallu, psychiatrist. "For the first time, we have not only a bioequivalent option but a molecule that uses the osmotic delivery system our patients have relied on for over 20 years to control their symptoms from morning to evening. This treatment option represents the only alternative with an osmotic delivery system available for our patients taking Concerta®."
ADHD is one of the most common neurodevelopmental disorders and is often diagnosed in childhood. ADHD presents as persistent inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity that lead to significant functional impairments. It is estimated that 5.4% of Canadians have ADHD.i
"The osmotic delivery system in Taro-Methylphenidate ER maintains a stable and effective concentration of treatment throughout the day," said Dr. Martin Katzman, Psychiatrist and Clinic Director. "The osmotic delivery system acts to minimize the peaks, troughs, and variability sometimes seen in other formulations that can compromise real-world functioning and patient outcomes in ADHD."
"Taro-Methylphenidate ER is the only generic with data from two rigorous randomized crossover studies to demonstrate patient stability across normal days when switching from the brand name product," said Joel Lamoure, community and hospital pharmacist. "Maintaining restorative functionality in the patient can be achieved through consistent osmotic-based medication delivery systems. The patient's body cannot tell the difference between Taro-Methylphenidate ER and the branded product, and that is huge for ADHD patients and their stability."
"Sun Pharma is excited to launch this much-anticipated, osmotic delivery formulation of methylphenidate as a lower-cost alternative to Concerta® for the over 2 million Canadians affected by ADHD," said Raffaele Spadafora, Head of Specialty Generics.
Taro-Methylphenidate ER is currently reimbursed by Régie de l'assurance maladie du Québec (RAMQ) in Quebec and the Ontario Public Drug Program (OPDP).
"We continue to work with public and private formularies to support patient access in every province across the country" said Barb Pimentel, General Manager Generics and Consumer Healthcare, Sun Pharma.
About Taro-Methylphenidate ER Taro-Methylphenidate ER is indicated for the treatment of Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in:
• children (6-12 years of age) • adolescents (13-18 years of age) • adults (>18 years of age)
- Should not be taken by children under 6 years of age - No data available in patients over 65 years of age - The effectiveness of Taro-Methylphenidate ER for more than 4 weeks in children and adolescents or 7 weeks in adults has not been systematically evaluated. If used for extended periods, physician should periodically re-evaluate.
Contraindications: Taro-Methylphenidate ER is contraindicated in: • Patients who are hypersensitive to methylphenidate or to any ingredients in the formulation or component of the container, thyrotoxicosis, advanced arteriosclerosis, symptomatic cardiovascular disease, moderate to severe hypertension, glaucoma, during treatment with monoamine oxidase inhibitors, and also within a minimum of 14 days following discontinuation of a monoamine oxidase inhibitor (hypertensive crises may result)
Most serious warning and precautions: • Drug dependence
Other relevant warnings and precautions: • General (oral use only), Fatigue, Information for patients, Carcinogenesis and Mutagenesis, hypertension and other cardiovascular conditions, pre-existing cardiovascular and cerebral vascular conditions, Sudden death and pre-existing structural cardiac abnormalities or other serious heart problems, Peripheral vasculopathy, including Raynaud's phenomenon, Drug dependence, Driving and operating machinery, Thyrotoxicosis, Long-term suppression of growth, Potential for gastrointestinal obstruction, monitoring and laboratory tests, cerebrovascular disorders, Motor and verbal tics, and worsening of Tourette's, Serotonin toxicity/serotonin syndrome, Increased intraocular pressure and glaucoma, Aggression, anxiety and agitation, Emergence of new psychotic or manic symptoms, Pre-existing psychosis, Screening patients for bipolar disorder, Suicidal behaviour and ideation, Priapism, Teratogenicity, Pregnancy women, Breast-feeding, Geriatrics, Pediatrics
For more information: • For important information on conditions of clinical use, contraindications, warnings, precautions, adverse reactions, drug interactions and dosing, please consult the product monograph at https://health-products.canada.ca/dpd-bdpp/index-eng.jsp. The product monograph is available by calling Sun Pharma Inc at 1-800-268-1975.
About Sun Pharma in Canada Sun Pharma combines the power of a global network with localized research and care to address the unmet needs of Canadian patients, and health care providers, consistent with the Company's vision of Reaching People. Touching Lives.
Sun Pharma offers a wide range of affordable medicines for the Canadian population in specialty and niche segments coupled with a presence in the top 15 Canadian generic products.
About Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited (CIN - L24230GJ1993PLC019050) Sun Pharma is a leading global pharmaceutical company with a presence in Innovative Medicines, Generics and Consumer Healthcare products. It is the largest pharmaceutical company in India and is a leading generic company in the US as well as Global Emerging Markets. Sun's high growth Global Innovative Medicines portfolio spans innovative products in dermatology, ophthalmology, and oncodermatology and accounts for about 22% of company sales. The company's vertically integrated operations deliver high-quality medicines, trusted by physicians and consumers in over 100 countries. Its manufacturing facilities are spread across five continents. Sun Pharma is proud of its multi-cultural workforce drawn from over 50 nations.

a.title: Nykaa brings haircare brand Oribe to India
a.content:
Nykaa brings haircare brand Oribe to India
                                Multi-brand beauty and lifestyle giant Nykaa has brought global premium haircare brand Oribe to the Indian market with an exclusive, omni-channel retail arrangement.
 
A selection of Oribe’s products are now available on Nykaa’s e-commerce store, on its shopping app, and at select Nykaa stores across India, the business announced in a press release. Oribe debuts with five products from its best-selling ‘Gold Lust’ collection: its Gold Lust Repair & Restore Shampoo, Gold Lust Repair & Restore Conditioner, Gold Lust Transformative Masque, Gold Lust Nourishing Hair Oil, and Gold Lust Dry Heat Protection Spray.
 
Nykaa’s continued expansion of its global premium haircare offering reflects the country's trend towards consumers increasingly investing in high-performance, luxury haircare products. The segment is one of the fastest-growing segments within beauty, according to Nykaa.
“We’re excited to share the Oribe story and expand our footprint by launching with Nykaa in India,” said Oribe Hair Care’s vice president, commercial growth salon Asia Eddie Wan in a press release. “We look forward to enhancing the consumer experience across all touchpoints by providing a new destination for consumers to discover Oribe.”
 
Founded by hairstylist Oribe Canales alongside beauty industry veteran Daniel Kaner, Oribe follows a fragrance and design-led approach to beauty, according to the brand. Known for its signature ‘Côte d’Azur’ fragrance, Oribe was launched in 2008 and is headquartered in New York.

Every one of these e-commerce and app based aggregator stocks trades at a valuation that looks extreme by traditional standards, reflecting the market's continued willingness to price in future growth over current profitability across India's new-age internet sector. FSN E-Commerce Ventures and One97 Communications at least post positive return on equity, while Eternal, Swiggy and Delhivery are all still working toward consistent profitability. a.title: Lenskart subsidiary NESO raises stake in French brand LPL to 34.34%
a.content:
Lenskart subsidiary NESO raises stake in French brand LPL to 34.34%
- NESO Brands acquired additional 2.52% stake in Le Petit Lunetier Paris SAS
- Total holding in French eyewear brand rises to 34.34% of fully diluted capital
- Transaction value stood at EUR 0.248 million or approx. ₹2.71 crore
- Investment aims to strengthen distribution access via Lenskart's retail network
*this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only.
Lenskart Solutions Limited subsidiary NESO Brands Pte Ltd acquired an additional 2.52% stake in French eyewear brand Le Petit Lunetier Paris SAS for EUR 0.248 million (approx. ₹2.71 crore) on September 23, 2026.
This primary subscription increases NESO's aggregate shareholding in the associate entity to 34.34% of fully diluted share capital, up from 31.82% following an earlier acquisition in April 2026.
Strategic Rationale and Portfolio Expansion
The acquisition aligns with Lenskart's brand portfolio strategy, which involves selectively investing in eyewear brands to scale their products across its omnichannel retail network in India and other markets. The company clarified that this investment strengthens access to the "Le Petit Lunetier" brand for distribution through Lenskart's stores but does not represent an expansion into LPL's existing wholesale and retail operations in Europe.
NESO Brands is a wholly owned subsidiary of Lenskart Solutions. LPL is considered a related party under applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, and SEBI Listing Regulations. The transaction was conducted on an arm's length basis.
Financial Details of Acquisition
The transaction involved a cash consideration by way of subscription to newly issued equity shares. This follows a previous investment made on April 30, 2026, where NESO acquired an additional 2.77% stake for EUR 0.25 million (approx. ₹2.77 crore).
What the Numbers Show
Lenskart has steadily consolidated its interest in Le Petit Lunetier over the last five months. Starting from a 29.05% holding at the time of Lenskart's listing in November 2025, NESO increased its stake to 31.82% in April 2026, and now to 34.34%. The aggregate increase of 5.30% over this period was achieved through two tranches totaling EUR 0.498 million (approx. ₹5.48 crore).
LPL reported a turnover of EUR 7.70 million for FY26, showing a slight contraction from EUR 7.90 million in FY25, though it remains significantly higher than the EUR 6.20 million recorded in FY24. The paid-up capital of LPL stands at EUR 1,546.

a.title: Nykaa adds luxury haircare brand Oribe to India portfolio
a.content:
New Delhi: Nykaa has launched luxury haircare brand Oribe in India, adding the brand to its premium beauty portfolio.
Oribe, founded by hairstylist Oribe Canales and beauty industry executive Daniel Kaner, will initially enter the Indian market with five products from its Gold Lust collection.
The range includes the Gold Lust Repair & Restore Shampoo, Repair & Restore Conditioner, Transformative Masque, Nourishing Hair Oil and Dry Heat Protection Spray.
The brand’s India entry comes as premium and high-performance haircare products gain wider adoption among consumers looking for specialised formulations and salon-led beauty routines.
Commenting on the launch, Eddie Wan, Vice President, Commercial Growth Salon Asia for Oribe Hair Care, said, “We’re excited to share the Oribe story and expand our footprint by launching with Nykaa in India. We look forward to enhancing the consumer experience across all touchpoints by providing a new destination for consumers to discover Oribe.”
Oribe’s products combine haircare formulations with fragrance and design-led packaging. The brand’s Gold Lust range is positioned around repair, hydration, heat protection and frizz control.
The products are now available on Nykaa.com, the Nykaa app and at select Nykaa stores across India.

Clinical Trial Data
The opinion follows results from the pivotal REPLENISH Phase III trial, published in the New England Journal of Medicine and presented at the 2026 European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) Congress. a.title: Block deals: New-age stock worth over Rs 67,000 crore sold in 2026, Lenskart accounts for over 25%
a.content:
Block and bulk deals in listed new-age companies have crossed Rs 67,000 crore so far in 2026, as venture capital funds, private equity investors and other early shareholders step up stake sales following the expiry of post-IPO lock-ins.
A total of 153 sell-side transactions worth roughly Rs 67,170 crore were recorded between January 1 and September 18, according to Prime Database data for the new-age company universe.
The activity has accelerated sharply since May. Nearly Rs 61,640 crore, or about 92 percent of the total, has changed between May and September, compared with just around Rs 5,530 crore during the first four months of the year, the data showed.
The selling has also been concentrated among a handful of large listed startups. Lenskart, Groww and Paytm together accounted for over Rs 35,000 crore, or about 53 percent of the total sell-side value during the period.
Lenskart leads selling
Lenskart has seen the highest value of secondary-market selling this year, with almost Rs 18,500 crore worth of shares changing hands across multiple transactions.
The largest wave came after the company's first post-listing lock-in expiry in May. Alpha Wave Ventures sold shares worth about Rs 1,762 crore on May 8, while other investors including Birdseye View Holdings sold additional shares the same day.
SoftBank Vision Fund II then sold shares worth Rs 2,873 crore on June 3 and another Rs 2,888 crore on August 24. Alpha Wave also sold another Rs 1,276 crore worth of shares on August 28.
The company saw another large round of selling on August 31, with Societe Generale, Integrated Core Strategies and BNP Paribas Financial Markets selling shares worth about Rs 2,679 crore collectively.
The transactions have made Lenskart the single largest source of new-age secondary-market supply this year, accounting for about 27 percent of the over Rs 67,000 crore total.
Groww, Paytm follow
Groww has seen the second-highest selling, with almost Rs 10,950 crore worth of shares sold so far this year.
A large part of the activity followed the expiry of its pre-IPO lock-in in May. Peak XV Partners, Ribbit Capital and Y Combinator-linked entities sold shares worth roughly Rs 5,326 crore on May 12, with the transactions executed at discounts of around 6-7 percent to the prevailing price.
The selling continued through the year. Y Combinator-linked entities sold another Rs 1,435 crore of Groww shares on August 18, while Ribbit Capital-linked entities sold around Rs 2,217 crore in August. Peak XV Partners sold another Rs 1,756 crore on September 16.
Paytm ranks third, with Rs 5,951 crore of sell-side transactions during the period. The largest transaction was Resilient Asset Management's sale of about Rs 2,949 crore on August 18, while SAIF (Elevation Capital)-linked entities sold around Rs 1,333 crore on August 4.
Meesho adds to supply
Meesho is the fourth-largest contributor, with Rs 5,557 crore of shares sold during the period.
The company saw its largest transaction on September 3, when SoftBank Vision Fund II sold shares worth about Rs 1,650 crore. That followed two transactions in August, including sales of around Rs 1,949 crore by Elevation Capital and Peak XV Partners and another Rs 970 crore by Y Combinator-linked entities.
Despite the series of large block deals, the supply has been being absorbed without necessarily causing sustained weakness in stock price across the board.
While companies like Groww and PB Fintech had seen intraday declines of around 7-8 percent during such large sales, firms like Meesho, Lenskart, Eternal and Delhivery saw relatively limited disruption or recovery despite sizeable blocks changing hands, Moneycontrol’s analysis revealed.
Policybazaar has seen another Rs 3,798 crore of sell-side transactions, while Pine Labs has recorded Rs 3,069 crore and Shadowfax about Rs 3,001 crore, as first reported by Moneycontrol, a story that led to share prices falling around 7 percent during the next day’s trade session.
The top five companies, Lenskart, Groww, Paytm, Meesho and Policybazaar, together account for nearly Rs 45,000 crore, or about two-thirds of the total value of new-age block and bulk deals this year.
May marks inflection point
The sharp increase in selling coincides with the first major wave of post-IPO lock-in expiries for India's new-age companies.
Moneycontrol had estimated in May that nearly Rs 2.3 lakh crore worth of shares across 11 newly listed new-age companies would become eligible for trading between May and August as pre-IPO lock-ins expired. Groww, Lenskart and Pine Labs accounted for about Rs 1.43 lakh crore of that potential supply, while Meesho accounted for more than Rs 59,000 crore.
At the time, market participants expected only a fraction of the unlocked shares to come into the market, with estimates that around 15-20 percent of the eligible supply could be sold over six months.
The subsequent transaction data shows that selling has accelerated materially as those lock-ins have expired.
VCs turn to exits
The selling has provided a major liquidity window for investors that backed these companies before they entered the public markets.
SoftBank, Alpha Wave, Elevation Capital, Peak XV Partners, Ribbit Capital, Y Combinator-linked entities and other venture and growth investors have been among the most active sellers.
Some investors have also used the public market to make complete exits. Lightspeed Venture Partners sold its entire 1.61 percent holding in PhysicsWallah for about Rs 550 crore in August, while Alpha Wave India exited Aye Finance through the sale of its entire holding for about Rs 323 crore.
The emergence of complete exits alongside partial stake sales suggests that the current cycle is not merely about investors trimming positions. For funds that have held these investments through the private-market and IPO stages, the expiry of lock-ins has opened a much broader route to return capital to limited partners.

Beauty and lifestyle retailer Nykaa has expanded its premium beauty portfolio with the exclusive introduction of Oribe, the luxury haircare brand founded by renowned hairstylist Oribe Canales and beauty industry veteran Daniel Kaner. The launch marks Oribe’s entry into the Indian market, with the brand debuting exclusively through Nykaa across online and select offline channels.
The move comes as India’s premium beauty and luxury haircare segments continue to witness strong growth, driven by increasing consumer interest in performance-led products and elevated beauty routines. Nykaa said the partnership reinforces its strategy of bringing globally recognized beauty brands to Indian consumers while strengthening its position in the luxury beauty category.
Known for its high-performance formulations, signature Côte d’Azur fragrance, and design-led aesthetic, Oribe has built a global reputation for combining salon-quality results with a luxury beauty experience. The brand’s products are developed using advanced formulations and skincare-inspired ingredients designed to cater to a wide range of hair types and textures.
As part of its India debut, Oribe is introducing five products from its best-selling Gold Lust collection, a range focused on repairing, nourishing, and protecting hair.
The collection includes the Gold Lust Repair & Restore Shampoo, designed to cleanse while helping strengthen damaged hair, and the Gold Lust Repair & Restore Conditioner, formulated to restore moisture, smoothness and manageability. Consumers will also have access to the Gold Lust Transformative Masque, an intensive treatment developed to replenish dry and damaged hair and improve softness and shine.
The range is further complemented by the Gold Lust Nourishing Hair Oil, which aims to smooth frizz and enhance shine without weighing hair down, and the Gold Lust Dry Heat Protection Spray, a styling product that offers heat protection up to 450°F while helping reduce frizz and improve softness.
Gaurs Group has sold out the entire available inventory of its newly launched premium residential project, Gaur Alaris, during a two-day allotment event held for homebuyers. Located in Sector 22D on the Yamuna Expressway near the upcoming Noida International Airport, the project offered 3 BHK and 4 BHK apartments and recorded strong demand shortly after bookings opened.
Launched in August 2026, Gaur Alaris is expected to generate sales realisation of approximately Rs 1,900 crore. The development follows the company's earlier luxury housing project, Gaur NYC Residences, which was sold out within 60 hours before its official launch.
The latest sell-out highlights growing demand for residential real estate along the Yamuna Expressway corridor, which has witnessed increased buyer interest due to infrastructure development, improved connectivity, and the upcoming Noida International Airport. The region has emerged as a key destination for both end-users and property investors.
Manoj Gaur, CMD, Gaurs Group said, “The response to Gaur Alaris is a strong endorsement of the evolving potential of the Yamuna Expressway as a residential destination. The complete sell-out reflects the confidence buyers have in the corridor as well as in the quality, planning and execution that Gaurs Group brings to its developments. It is also a testament to the trust and belief our customers have in us, the legacy that has been built over 3 decades by timely delivery of all our projects.”
The project has been designed around a peacock-inspired concept and features Art Deco architecture by Hafeez Contractor. Landscape planning has been undertaken by Site Concepts International, while interior design has been developed by Studio Designscape. Gaur Alaris includes a clubhouse spread across more than 1 lakh sq ft, nearly eight acres of landscaped open spaces, and over 65 amenities across the residential development.
Sarthak Gaur, Director, Gaursons India Pvt Ltd said, “The Allotment Day of Gaur Alaris was a big success and is an endorsement of the trust of our buyers and the credibility of Gaurs Group. The complete sell-out of Gaur Alaris reflects the strong momentum that the Yamuna Expressway is currently witnessing. The Noida International Airport has added a significant new dimension to the region, while the overall infrastructure ecosystem continues to improve. Also, to our advantage, we already had a strong footprint in this region as we have already delivered a 250-acre integrated township – Gaur Yamuna City on Yamuna Expressway which is today home to almost 15000 residents.”
The project adds to Gaurs Group's premium and luxury housing portfolio, which includes developments such as The Islands by Gaurs, Legacy by Gaurs, Trecento Residences by Gaurs, Gaur NYC Residences, and Gaur Chrysalis. The company said it plans to launch two additional residential projects on the Yamuna Expressway in the near future as demand in the region continues to grow.
Nykaa reported strong growth across its beauty and fashion businesses for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, supported by store expansion, customer acquisition, omnichannel growth, and brand additions. The beauty and lifestyle retailer said its Beauty vertical is expected to record net sales value (NSV) growth and net revenue growth in the late twenties on a year-on-year basis during the second quarter.
The performance was driven by continued omnichannel expansion, growth in new customers, higher repeat purchases, and improved offline retail performance. Nykaa's physical retail business also recorded like-for-like (LFL) store sales growth in the early twenties, marking the highest LFL growth rate for its store network in the last six quarters.
As part of its retail expansion strategy, Nykaa added 14 net new stores during the quarter, taking its total offline store count to 338 as of September 30, 2026. The expansion further strengthens the company's omnichannel retail presence across India's beauty and personal care market.
The company's owned brand portfolio, House of Nykaa, continued to outperform the broader Beauty business during the quarter. Growth was supported by established brands within the portfolio as well as emerging beauty labels across skincare, cosmetics, and personal care categories. Nykaa's Fashion business also maintained strong momentum as it continued to scale operations. The company expects Fashion NSV growth in the late forties and net revenue growth in the early forties year-on-year, increasing the segment's contribution to overall revenue.
Product assortment expansion remained a key focus area during the quarter. Across its beauty and fashion platforms, Nykaa onboarded more than 250 brands in Q2 FY27, broadening consumer choice across categories. The company also reported early consumer interest following its exclusive partnership with Nike, which was announced during the period.
Nykaa noted that the timing of India's festive season affected quarterly demand patterns. A significant share of festive shopping activity shifted into the third quarter of FY27 rather than the September quarter. As a result, the company expects the December quarter to witness the bulk of festive demand and sales volumes. Despite the timing shift, Nykaa said its long-term growth drivers across beauty retail, fashion e-commerce, omnichannel retail, and owned brands remain unchanged.
The update highlights continued momentum in India's beauty retail and fashion retail sectors, with store expansion, premium brand partnerships, and omnichannel growth supporting Nykaa's business performance.
Ahead of the festive season, Amazon India has announced the expansion of its Ashray network with 50 new centres across the country, taking the total number of operational centres to 200. The company said it remains on track to reach 250 Ashray centres by the end of 2026 as it continues to strengthen support infrastructure for delivery drivers.
Amazon India also expanded its mobile Ashray van initiative to Bengaluru, making it the fourth city after Delhi NCR, Mumbai, and Hyderabad to receive the service. Two mobile Ashray vans were flagged off in Bengaluru in the presence of Sandy Gordon, Vice President, Employee Experience and Relations, Amazon, and Brendan Branon, Vice President of North America (NA) Employee Relations (ER).
The move comes ahead of the festive shopping season, a period that typically sees a significant rise in e-commerce orders and last-mile deliveries across India.
Salim R. Memon, Director – Operations, Amazon India said, "With the festive season driving a sharp increase in deliveries, it's more important than ever that drivers across the industry have access to rest on their routes. Ashray was built on a simple idea — that every delivery driver, whether they deliver for Amazon or not, deserves a clean, cool place to rest during their workday. Expanding to 200 centres and bringing mobile vans to more cities means we can reach more drivers in more cities, right when they need it most. This expansion is part of Amazon India's broader investment of over INR 2,800 crore (~USD 300 million) in 2026 to strengthen associate safety, health, and financial well-being across its operations network."
Launched in 2024, the Ashray initiative has grown into one of India's largest delivery driver welfare programmes. The centres are open to all delivery drivers, including those not associated with Amazon. The facilities provide air-conditioned seating, drinking water, mobile charging points, clean washrooms, first-aid support, and designated rest areas. Each centre can accommodate 10 to 15 people at a time and allows free access for up to 30 minutes per visit. The centres operate throughout the year from 9 a.m. to 7 p.m. and are located at high-footfall areas such as petrol pumps and commercial hubs. Their locations are also listed on Google Maps to improve accessibility.
To complement the fixed centres, Amazon's mobile Ashray vans provide similar amenities directly on high-density delivery routes. The fully air-conditioned vans offer seating, drinking water, free Wi-Fi connectivity, and mobile charging facilities, allowing delivery personnel to take short breaks during work hours.
Ashray Expansion Timeline
- 2024: Pilot launched with Ashray centres across Delhi NCR, Bengaluru, and Mumbai.
- 2025: Expanded to 100 centres across 16 cities.
- May 2026: Added 50 new centres, taking the total to 150; mobile Ashray vans launched in Delhi NCR.
- September 2026: Announced 50 additional centres, increasing the total to 200; mobile Ashray vans now operational in Delhi NCR, Mumbai, Hyderabad, and Bengaluru.
- End of 2026 Target: 250 Ashray centres across India.
The latest expansion is part of Amazon India's broader investment in delivery associate welfare, logistics infrastructure, and last-mile operations as e-commerce demand continues to grow across the country.
Canon India plans to expand its consumer printing retail network to more than 10,000 active retailers across 700 cities by the end of 2027, doubling its current reach as it looks to deepen its presence in Tier II, Tier III and Tier IV markets. The expansion follows sustained double-digit year-on-year growth in Canon India’s Consumer Printing business. The company is looking to improve access to printing products and services while growing its presence across consumer, SME, education, enterprise and institutional segments in India.
Demand for printing solutions is evolving across homes, schools, small businesses and enterprises, particularly in smaller cities where entrepreneurship, digital adoption and education-related requirements are increasing. Canon aims to use its wider retail network to improve product availability, strengthen local distribution and provide customers with access to product consultation and after-sales support.
The company is also investing in product development, digital commerce and partner capabilities as part of its wider India growth strategy. Building on the Canon Passport Program, which supports more than 5,000 active reseller partners through a digital rewards and engagement platform, Canon India is introducing BizBee for its B2B partner network.
BizBee will cater to System Integrators, Value-Added Resellers and other partners by providing access to incentives, product and solution training, technical certifications, business resources and digital tools. The initiative is intended to strengthen Canon’s B2B channel ecosystem across enterprise, education and institutional markets.
Toshiaki Nomura, President and CEO, Canon India said, “India is central to Canon’s long-term growth ambitions, underpinned by the resilience of its economy and the emergence of new centres of enterprise and consumption. As education, digitisation and infrastructure reshape demand across Tier lll and Tier IV markets, we see a significant opportunity to unlock the next phase of growth for our printing business. Our ambition to build a network of over 10,000 active retailers across 700 cities by 2027 reflects our commitment to invest ahead of the curve and bring Canon closer to customers through trusted touchpoints that combine first-hand product experience with expert guidance. By combining scale with customer-led innovation and strong channel partnerships, we are positioning Canon to lead and shape the future of printing in India.”
To support the expansion, Canon India is strengthening its omnichannel distribution network across traditional resellers, large-format retail chains, e-commerce, quick commerce and enterprise-focused partners. The company currently operates more than 400 active PIXMA Zones across India and plans to add over 500 PIXMA Zone Lite stores this year. Its Canon eSHOP platform also allows authorised resellers to showcase and sell Canon products digitally.
The wider channel strategy is aimed at giving customers flexibility to research and purchase products across online and offline retail formats while enabling Canon to extend its presence beyond major metropolitan markets. Canon is also increasing investment in retailer engagement and frontline sales capabilities. Its Retail Display Incentive Program currently covers over 1,000 partners and focuses on strengthening product visibility at physical retail outlets.
At the same time, the company plans to scale its RetailChamp Initiative from 400 to more than 1,000 retail sales personnel. The programme focuses on improving product knowledge and customer consultation across the company's retail network. Beyond consumer retail, Canon India intends to expand its System Integrator network to more than 500 partners nationwide. The move is expected to increase its reach across enterprise, education and government segments.
C Sukumaran, Vice President, Canon India said, “Our channel ecosystem will be central to translating Canon’s growth ambition into business impact. As we expand our reach, our focus is on building the capabilities of our partners and frontline teams to understand local needs, create demand and deliver trusted customer experience. Through initiatives such as Canon Passport, RetailChamp and BizBee, we are strengthening partner engagement, knowledge and enablement across the ecosystem. BizBee, in particular, will equip our B2B partners and System Integrators with the training, certifications and business tools needed to unlock opportunities across enterprise, education and government segments. Together, these efforts will help us build a more capable partner network and drive solution-led growth across consumer, SME and institutional markets.”
Canon’s expansion strategy brings together physical retail, digital commerce, reseller engagement and B2B channel development as the company increases its reach across India. The planned addition of retailers, PIXMA Zone Lite stores, System Integrators and trained frontline personnel is expected to support Canon’s consumer printing business across smaller cities while strengthening its ability to serve education, SME, enterprise and institutional customers.
Carlsberg India has received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for its confidential pre-filing of documents for a proposed initial public offering (IPO). The company had submitted its draft IPO papers to SEBI through the confidential route in July 2026. This process allows companies to keep their draft offer documents private during the initial review, before deciding when to make the filing public.
The approval marks a key milestone in Carlsberg India’s proposed initial public offering (IPO). Details regarding the issue size, timeline, and other terms are expected to be disclosed in the offer documents, subject to the necessary regulatory and corporate approvals.
The proposed listing comes amid growing interest among multinational companies in India’s equity markets, as businesses look to unlock value from their investments in the country. The potential IPO would add to the activity in India’s primary market, with anticipated offerings from companies such as Jio Platforms drawing investor attention.
Carlsberg India commenced commercial operations in June 2007 with the launch of Carlsberg Green, entering India’s premium beer segment. Since then, the company has expanded its presence in the domestic beer market through a portfolio of brands, including Carlsberg and Tuborg.
The parent company has also reported positive volume growth across key markets. In its earnings guidance for the six months ended June 30, 2026, Danish brewer Carlsberg reported overall volume growth of 2.8%, while organic volume growth stood at 1.7%. Europe recorded volume growth of 0.1%, while the Central and Eastern Europe and India region registered growth of 6.2%.
The performance highlights the contribution of the Central and Eastern Europe and India region to the group's volume growth during the first half of 2026. With SEBI approval secured, Carlsberg India has taken another step toward its proposed public listing, with further details expected to emerge following the release of the relevant offer documents.
Global apparel retailer UNIQLO has reopened its expanded store at Ambience Mall, Gurugram, strengthening its retail presence in North India and offering customers a larger shopping destination featuring the brand’s latest seasonal collections and customer engagement initiatives.
The reopening was marked by a traditional Taiko drum performance, creating a festive atmosphere that attracted a large number of shoppers to the store. Customers visiting the revamped outlet were introduced to the expanded retail space and a wider assortment of products across key categories.
The enlarged store features UNIQLO’s latest Fall/Winter collection, including seasonal essentials such as Fleece, Knitwear, HEATTECH and PUFFTECH. The expansion is aimed at improving the overall shopping experience while providing consumers with greater access to the brand’s apparel and technology-driven clothing solutions.
In addition to the product showcase, UNIQLO introduced a series of customer-focused experiences designed to encourage participation and community engagement. One of the highlights was the UNIQLO Share Wall, an interactive installation where visitors could share personal stories and experiences about what they appreciate most about the brand.
The company also promoted sustainability through its RE: UNIQLO initiative. A dedicated donation box was installed at the store, encouraging customers to contribute pre-loved clothing that can be redirected to individuals and communities in need. The initiative forms part of UNIQLO’s broader efforts to support responsible consumption and extend the lifecycle of garments.
To celebrate the reopening, UNIQLO has announced a range of special promotional offers, available from October 2 to October 8. The limited-period deals are intended to drive footfall to the newly expanded outlet while giving customers an opportunity to explore the retailer’s latest collections and in-store experiences.
The Ambience Mall store expansion reflects UNIQLO’s continued focus on strengthening its retail footprint in India. By combining a larger retail format, seasonal product innovations, and community-driven initiatives, the brand aims to deepen its engagement with consumers while reinforcing its position in the country’s growing fashion and apparel market.
Reliance-backed online healthcare platform Netmeds reported steady financial performance for FY26, maintaining profitability despite recording only moderate growth in revenue.
Revenue from operations increased 2.3 percent to Rs 44.7 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 43.7 crore in FY25. The digital healthcare and online pharmacy platform posted a profit of Rs 5.5 crore during the fiscal year, continuing its profitable run despite a relatively stable topline.
Netmeds operates across multiple healthcare segments, including online pharmacy, diagnostics, teleconsultation services, and healthcare product sales. In addition to product transactions, the company derives income from healthcare-related services and marketing activities.
Services remained the primary contributor to the company’s business during the year. Gross service income stood at Rs 46.3 crore, largely unchanged from Rs 46.2 crore reported in the previous fiscal. Revenue generated from the sale of goods, however, registered stronger growth, rising 24 percent to Rs 6.03 crore from Rs 4.86 crore in FY25.
Netmeds reported operating revenue of Rs 44.7 crore. The company also earned Rs 3.24 crore from non-operating income, taking its total income to Rs 47.94 crore for FY26.
The company significantly increased spending on brand visibility and customer outreach initiatives during the year. Advertising and promotional expenses jumped 76 percent to Rs 2.9 crore, compared to Rs 1.65 crore in FY25. Additional overhead expenses, including legal, professional, and rental costs, amounted to Rs 12.24 crore.
Overall expenditure increased to Rs 42.4 crore from Rs 41.6 crore in the previous fiscal year. Despite the rise in costs, Netmeds remained in the black, although its profit declined by around 5 percent year-on-year.
The company reported a return on capital employed (ROCE) of 4.5 percent and an EBITDA margin of 5.66 percent. Operational efficiency remained largely stable, with Netmeds spending approximately Rs 0.95 to generate every Re 1 of operating revenue, in line with FY25 levels.
Reliance Industries, through Reliance Retail Ventures Ltd. (RRVL), acquired a majority stake in Netmeds for approximately Rs 620 crore in August 2020 as part of its expansion into the digital healthcare and e-pharmacy sector.
Netmeds competes with major players in India’s online healthcare market, including Tata 1mg, PharmEasy and Apollo 24/7. During FY26, Tata 1mg reported Rs 2,936 crore in revenue while posting a consolidated loss of Rs 287 crore, whereas API Holdings, the parent company of PharmEasy, reported Rs 6,869 crore in revenue.
Cinema exhibitor Cinépolis India has strengthened its presence in Haryana with the launch of a new four-screen multiplex at Amolik’s City Life Mall in Sector 28, Faridabad.
With the latest opening, the company has doubled its footprint in the city to eight screens, less than a year after inaugurating its first Faridabad property at Pacific Mall.
The newly launched multiplex houses 549 seats across four screens and offers recliner seating, Dolby sound technology and the brand’s food and beverage services. The opening comes ahead of the Gandhi Jayanti holiday weekend and the release of Drishyam: The Conclusion on October 2.
The expansion is part of Cinépolis India’s broader growth strategy across the Delhi-NCR cinema market. In recent months, the multiplex chain has added new properties at IREO Grand High Street in Gurugram and Dwarka, taking its regional network to 16 cinemas and 78 screens.
Devang Sampat, Managing Director, Cinépolis India said, "For us, growth is really a catchment question. Sector 28, has settled residential neighbourhoods on every side, and Faridabad is a big city, so there's room here for more than one Cinépolis. The choice of mall matters just as much. Amolik has built City Life as a place where families already come to eat and shop, and a good cinema gives them one more reason to spend the evening there. When a cinema runs well, the businesses around it do well too."
Located in the residential hub of Sector 28, City Life Mall has been developed by Amolik, whose portfolio in Faridabad also includes projects such as Amolik Heights and Amolik Residency.

Milky Mist Dairy Food Limited has commissioned a new 10 MW solar power plant at Arasanoor, further strengthening its renewable energy infrastructure and sustainability initiatives. The latest addition comes alongside the 15 MW solar facility already operational at the same location, taking the company’s total investment in the 25 MW Arasanoor solar project to Rs 109.60 crore.
With the commissioning of the new facility, Milky Mist’s renewable energy portfolio has grown to 41 MW. The company’s renewable assets now include 5 MW at Chithode, 9 MW at Kavilipalayam, 25 MW at Arasanoor, and 2 MW of wind power at Kayathar. According to the company, renewable energy sources now meet its entire power requirement across operations.
The solar installations have been developed on arid and open land that is not suitable for agricultural use, allowing the company to utilize such areas for renewable energy generation while supporting its sustainability goals.
The newly operational 25 MW solar facility is expected to generate around 20 million units of renewable electricity annually and supply power to Milky Mist’s integrated manufacturing facility in Perundurai as well as its milk chilling centers. The additional capacity is also projected to reduce dependence on conventional energy sources and help avoid nearly 16,000 tonnes of carbon emissions every year.
Beyond solar and wind energy, the company has invested in steam turbine technology and a methane gas purification plant that generates approximately 15,000 units of electricity daily. Methane produced through effluent treatment processes is purified and converted into compressed natural gas (CNG), while biomass is also used in boiler operations to further reduce reliance on conventional energy sources.
T Sathish Kumar, Chairman and Managing Director, Milky Mist Dairy Food Limited said, “At Milky Mist, our approach to growth has always been guided by a long-term vision of building a business that is responsible in its use of resources and conscious of its impact on the environment. We believe that sustainability must be embedded in the way an enterprise is built, operated and scaled, rather than viewed as a standalone initiative. Our investments in renewable energy, resource-efficient technologies and alternative sources of power are a reflection of this philosophy. The commissioning of our new 10 MW solar power plant is another significant step in this journey, taking renewable sources to over 90% of our total power requirements. As we continue to expand our operations, our endeavour is to strengthen energy self-sufficiency, advance more sustainable manufacturing practices and create enduring value for our business, our stakeholders and the environment.”
The latest investment aligns with Milky Mist’s broader strategy of building a technology-driven and resource-efficient manufacturing ecosystem, while continuing to explore opportunities to enhance energy efficiency and expand the use of renewable power across its operations.
Amazon India has expanded its ultra-fast delivery service, Amazon Now, to more than 120 cities across the country, doubling the service’s reach within two weeks. The expansion brings the quick-commerce offering to several new markets, including Amritsar, Abohar, Jalandhar, Ambala, Mangalore, Manipal, Visakhapatnam, Kochi, Changanassery, Bhubaneswar, and Karwar.
Amazon Now enables customers to receive deliveries within minutes and offers access to a broad assortment of daily essentials. The service covers categories such as groceries, including fresh fruits and vegetables, frozen foods, personal care products, beauty items, fashion, small appliances, home essentials, and kitchen products.
To support the growing network, Amazon is leveraging nearly 800 micro-fulfilment and urban fulfilment centres across India. The infrastructure is designed to facilitate rapid deliveries while expanding product availability in both metropolitan and emerging markets.
Harsh Goyal, Vice President – Everyday Essentials, Amazon India said, "We are delighted to take ultra-fast deliveries with Amazon Now to India’s hinterland – from Amritsar & Abohar in the north to Kochi & Changanassery in the south – ahead of the Amazon Great Indian Festival. Amazon Now continues to be the fastest-growing ecommerce business unit in Amazon India's history with orders doubling every quarter. This accelerated rollout underscores our commitment to making fast & reliable delivery accessible to customers across the country. We look forward to continue scaling up and offering the widest selection of products at the fastest delivery speeds this festive season.”
The announcement follows Amazon’s recent disclosure that Amazon Now achieved an annualized gross sales run rate of $1 billion in India over the past three-month period. The company plans to further scale the service to more than 300 cities as it works toward building one of the country’s largest delivery-in-minutes networks.
