Pricing starts at Rs 599 for menswear shirts and T-shirts, Rs 899 for womenswear dresses, skirts, and shirts, and Rs 999 for Indian wear categories including fusion dresses, fusion blazers, culottes, and kurta sets. Prices across the collection go up to Rs 1,999.
Da Milano Group has appointed Piyush Singh as its Group CEO as the company looks to accelerate growth and strengthen its presence across markets. Singh brings more than 18 years of experience across consumer businesses, retail, business strategy, transformation and leadership. Over the course of his career, he has worked on business growth initiatives, consumer-focused strategies and operational transformation across competitive markets.
The appointment comes as Da Milano Group continues to focus on expanding its business, strengthening its brand portfolio and enhancing customer engagement across channels. The company said Singh will play a key role in shaping and executing its growth strategy during the next phase of development.
Piyush Singh, Group CEO, Da Milano Group said, “I am delighted to join Da Milano Group at an exciting stage in its journey. The Group has built a strong presence in the luxury lifestyle space, and I look forward to working closely with the team to build on this foundation and unlock the next phase of growth. Our focus will be on strengthening our brands, deepening our customer connect, building operational excellence and creating sustainable value as we scale the business across markets and channels.”
In his new role, Singh will oversee initiatives focused on strengthening the company’s brand portfolio, improving operational efficiency across the value chain and driving business performance across retail and emerging channels. He will also be responsible for supporting the company’s long-term growth objectives and expanding its presence across multiple consumer touchpoints.
The leadership appointment reflects Da Milano Group’s ongoing efforts to build a stronger management structure as it expands its operations. The company is also exploring opportunities across retail, direct-to-consumer (D2C) platforms and emerging distribution channels as part of its broader business strategy. With Singh taking over as Group CEO, Da Milano Group aims to build on its existing market presence while pursuing new growth opportunities across the luxury accessories, lifestyle and fashion retail sectors.
India is assured to emerge as a global hub for gems and jewellery in the coming years, Union Home Minister Amit Shah said on Sunday, urging the industry to take the lead in building a complete, India-owned value chain for the emerging lab-grown diamond market.
India’s rich jewellery heritage
The Home Minister highlighted the contribution of Indian artisans and craftsmen to the development of the country's jewellery traditions over centuries.
He noted that royal patronage during the medieval period helped jewellery craftsmanship reach new heights, while regions such as Rajasthan and Kolkata developed distinctive traditions, including Kundan and Meenakari.
Jaipur, Shah said, continues to be renowned globally for its coloured gemstones.
Lab-Grown diamonds present new opportunity
According to Shah, changing consumer preferences and the emergence of lab-grown diamonds present a significant opportunity for India's gems and jewellery sector.
He said the era of lab-grown diamonds is set to emerge, with the market expected to grow to nearly 50 times the size of the current diamond market.
Shah stressed that the entire ecosystem and manufacturing value chain should be under Indian ownership, spanning the manufacture of machinery, production of lab-grown diamonds, jewellery manufacturing, branding and global retail.
“From manufacturing the machines to the showroom where the jewellery ultimately reaches a woman’s hand, India must have ownership of the entire ecosystem,” Shah said.
India Jewellery Park to drive investment
Shah said the India Jewellery Park is a landmark project expected to attract investments of around INR 50,000 crore and generate direct and indirect employment for one lakh people.
The project is expected to strengthen India's jewellery manufacturing ecosystem while creating opportunities across manufacturing, processing, design, branding and retail.
India’s growing global jewellery footprint
In his speech, the Union Home Minister also highlighted India's growing position in the global jewellery trade. He said India has emerged as a major source of jewellery imports for markets including the United States, the Middle East, Hong Kong and Europe.
Conclusion
India's gems and jewellery industry is at an important inflection point, with its traditional craftsmanship now intersecting with new-age opportunities such as lab-grown diamonds. Building an India-owned value chain could help the country move beyond its established strengths in manufacturing and craftsmanship towards greater control over technology, branding and global retail. With large-scale investments such as the India Jewellery Park, the sector could further strengthen India's position as a global jewellery hub while creating significant employment and business opportunities.
Reliance Consumer Products Limited (RCPL), the FMCG arm of Reliance Industries Limited, has launched its beverage brand Campa in Australia, marking the brand’s entry into a new international market. New Sunrise has become the first petrol and convenience retail network in Australia to introduce Campa across its stores.
The launch brings the beverage brand, which has a legacy spanning nearly five decades, to Australian consumers through the New Sunrise national retail network. The move is part of RCPL’s broader international expansion strategy as it continues to strengthen its presence in global consumer goods markets.
Since acquiring Campa in 2022 and reintroducing the brand in India in 2023, RCPL has expanded the portfolio beyond carbonated soft drinks to include juices and packaged drinking water. The company has been growing Campa’s presence across multiple beverage categories within the Indian FMCG and beverage sectors. Australia becomes the latest market in RCPL’s international expansion journey, following the company’s growing footprint across GCC countries, Nepal and Sri Lanka.
The initial Campa product range is now available nationwide through approximately 1,200 New Sunrise petrol and convenience stores. The partnership provides the brand with immediate access to a large retail distribution network and strengthens its reach within Australia’s convenience retail and on-the-go beverage segments.
The company believes the Australian market presents opportunities for value-focused beverage brands as consumers increasingly seek affordability, convenience and product variety. Through its partnership with New Sunrise, Campa will be positioned within a retail channel that serves a significant share of impulse and convenience purchases.
The rollout also highlights the growing international ambitions of Indian FMCG companies and beverage brands seeking expansion opportunities beyond domestic markets. With Australia now added to its international portfolio, RCPL continues to build Campa’s presence across key global markets. The launch is expected to support wider brand visibility and distribution while strengthening RCPL’s position in the global non-alcoholic beverages industry.
Amazon India has announced a major expansion of its logistics and supply chain network ahead of the festive shopping season, with plans to add 20 fulfilment centres, six sort centres and 150 delivery stations across the country. The expansion is aimed at strengthening the company's e-commerce infrastructure and enhancing its ability to manage higher order volumes during one of the busiest shopping periods of the year. The additional facilities are expected to improve inventory storage, order processing, and last-mile delivery capabilities across multiple regions.
With the planned additions, Amazon is increasing capacity across key stages of its operations network. Fulfilment centres will support inventory storage for sellers, while sort centres will help streamline package movement between facilities. The new delivery stations are expected to strengthen last-mile logistics and improve delivery efficiency in both metropolitan and emerging markets.
The announcement comes as online retailers prepare for increased consumer spending during festive sales events. E-commerce platforms typically experience a sharp rise in demand across categories such as electronics, smartphones, fashion, beauty, home appliances and consumer goods during this period.
Amazon has continued to invest in its logistics network in India, including fulfilment infrastructure, delivery operations and quick commerce capabilities. The company recently expanded its operations network, created more than 160,000 seasonal work opportunities and increased investments in fulfilment and delivery infrastructure to support growing customer demand.
The expanded network is also expected to support Amazon's seller ecosystem by enabling faster order fulfilment and wider reach across serviceable pin codes. The company currently serves millions of customers and works with a large base of sellers across India through its fulfilment, sorting and delivery infrastructure.
As competition intensifies in India's e-commerce and quick commerce sectors, logistics capacity has become a key area of investment for online retailers. Amazon's latest expansion highlights the industry's focus on warehousing, supply chain optimisation and last-mile delivery ahead of the festive shopping season.
Adie Broswon Group has expanded its flavoured vodka portfolio by launching MOOOZ Cranberry Vodka in Uttar Pradesh. The introduction of the new variant strengthens the company’s presence in North India and adds to its growing range of vodka offerings in the Indian alcohol beverage market.
Uttar Pradesh continues to be a key market for alcohol beverage companies due to its scale, evolving retail ecosystem, and increasing demand for premium and flavoured spirits. The launch of MOOOZ Cranberry Vodka aligns with the company’s efforts to expand distribution and reach consumers seeking new flavour profiles within the vodka category.
MOOOZ is produced in Punjab using rice grains and undergoes a triple distillation process along with a multi-stage filtration system. The brand has already established a presence in markets including Delhi, Punjab and Chandigarh and has been expanding across North India through new product launches and market entries.
The launch comes at a time when flavoured vodka is gaining traction in India, particularly among younger adult consumers and cocktail-focused occasions. Industry trends indicate increasing demand for innovative spirit categories, with flavoured variants emerging as an important growth segment within the vodka market.
The addition of Cranberry Vodka further broadens the MOOOZ portfolio, which has recently seen the introduction of new flavour-led variants as the company continues to diversify its offerings in the Indian spirits industry. With the Uttar Pradesh launch, Adie Broswon continues to strengthen its footprint across key markets in North India, focusing on portfolio expansion and wider availability in the country's evolving alcobev sector.
Parag Milk Foods is expanding its nutrition portfolio beyond conventional protein products, entering the snacking segment with Avvatar Popped Protein Chips as consumers increasingly look for convenient ways to include protein in everyday eating.
The launch marks the latest move under the company’s New Age Business, extending Avvatar from its existing range of protein powders, ready-to-drink beverages and bars into a familiar snacking format.
Akshali Shah, Executive Director, Parag Milk Foods Ltd., said, “This launch marks an important step in Parag Milk Foods’ evolution from a dairy-led company to a broader nutrition-led food business.”
The company said the expansion is aimed at creating more consumption occasions for protein, including those beyond traditional sports and active nutrition.
Avvatar Popped Chips are available in Magic Masala and Pudina flavours. The non-fried chips provide 10 g of protein in a 30 g pack and are priced at INR 60.
The product contains no added sugar, palm oil, or preservatives, positioning it within the growing better-for-you snacking space while retaining the convenience of a packaged snack.
The chips are being distributed through Avvatar’s website, quick-commerce platforms, vending machines, general trade and modern trade outlets.
For Parag Milk Foods, the launch forms part of a broader effort to use its experience in dairy and protein to enter adjacent food categories. Avvatar is expected to play a role in this expansion as the company looks to build its presence across different nutrition formats and consumption occasions.
“We see a significant opportunity to take our expertise in dairy and protein and build it into categories that are increasingly relevant to the way consumers eat today,” Shah said.
She added, “With Avvatar, we are extending protein beyond traditional nutrition formats and into everyday consumption occasions, including snacking.”
The company’s approach reflects the wider shift in the packaged food market, where protein is increasingly being incorporated into convenient, ready-to-consume products rather than remaining limited to specialised nutrition products.
Established in 1992, Parag Milk Foods has built its business around dairy products and operates manufacturing facilities at Manchar and Thorandale in Maharashtra and Palamner in Andhra Pradesh.
Its portfolio includes milk, ghee, dahi and paneer under Gowardhan, while Go offers products such as cheese, UHT milk, buttermilk, lassi and flavoured milkshakes. The company also operates Pride of Cows, a premium farm-to-home dairy brand.
Avvatar represents its sports nutrition business and focuses on whey protein products. With the addition of popped chips, the company is now extending the brand into everyday snacking.
The move signals Parag Milk Foods’ attempt to build a broader nutrition portfolio where protein can be consumed across different parts of the day, from specialised sports nutrition to convenient snacks.
“Our ambition is to build a holistic protein ecosystem that brings together nutrition, convenience and accessibility across formats and lifestyles,” Shah said.
She added that entering snacking is “a strategic step towards creating a larger, more contemporary food and nutrition business with protein at its core.”
The House of Rare, the company behind fashion brands Rare Rabbit, Rareism, Rare’Z and Rare Ones, is ramping up its growth plans through an aggressive retail expansion strategy, new category launches and a stronger omnichannel presence across India.
The fashion retailer is aiming to achieve revenue of nearly Rs 1,600 crore in the current fiscal year, marking a significant increase from Rs 1,100 crore recorded in the previous year. The growth target comes as the company continues to expand its physical footprint and diversify its product portfolio across multiple fashion segments.
Launched over a decade ago with the introduction of Rare Rabbit, The House of Rare has evolved into a multi-brand fashion platform covering menswear, womenswear, kidswear and sneakers. The company currently operates 210 stores across its portfolio and plans to increase the count to at least 285 stores by the end of this fiscal year. An additional 50 outlets are expected to be added in the following year.
Rare Rabbit continues to be the company’s largest business segment, contributing around 70-72 percent of overall revenue. Womenswear brand Rareism accounts for nearly 20 percent, while Rare’Z and Rare Ones together contribute approximately 8-9 percent.
As part of its diversification efforts, The House of Rare is entering several new product categories, including fragrances, women’s handbags, open footwear, ballerinas, heels, belts and jewellery. The fragrance range is scheduled to launch next month. Meanwhile, its men’s innerwear label, Innerv, already contributes about 3 percent of Rare Rabbit’s menswear business and is being scaled further.
Currently, The House of Rare has a presence across more than 1,100 points of sale. Around 97 percent of its outlets are company-owned and company-operated. Its stores typically span between 1,100 and 1,200 square feet, with capital expenditure averaging Rs 3,400-3,500 per square foot. Metro cities and Tier I markets contribute roughly 60-65 percent of total revenue, though the company sees substantial growth opportunities emerging from Tier II and Tier III cities.
Offline channels remain the primary revenue source, accounting for around 60 percent of total sales, while online channels contribute the remaining 40 percent. The average selling price online ranges between Rs 1,600 and Rs 1,800, whereas the average order value in physical stores stands at approximately Rs 4,500-5,000.
The company has also reported strong customer growth, with its customer base expanding by nearly 50 percent this year. Repeat customers currently account for around 40 percent of total shoppers.
Allied Blenders and Distillers Ltd (ABDL) is planning to enter the single malt whisky segment with an investment of up to Rs 115 crore. The company’s Management Committee has approved the additional capital infusion into its subsidiary, Minakshi Agro Industries LLP (MAILLP).
The investment will be used to set up a malt distillery-cum-maturation warehouse in Aurangabad, Maharashtra. The proposed facility is expected to have an annual production capacity of around 3 million bulk litres and is targeted to be commissioned by the third quarter of FY28.
The proposed facility will support ABDL’s planned entry into the provenance-led single malt whisky category. The company said the investment forms part of its broader strategy to expand its presence in premium spirits.
“The proposed investment is aligned with the Company's long-term strategic vision of expanding and strengthening its premium spirits portfolio through entry into the provenance-led Single Malt Whisky segment,” the company said.
The move comes as Indian consumers have shown growing interest in premium and luxury spirits, with domestic single malt brands gaining greater visibility in recent years. ABDL currently has a portfolio spanning whisky and other spirits and is seeking to add a new category to its business.
Alongside the Rs 115 crore investment, the company has approved an additional capital contribution of up to Rs 10 crore for previously approved projects under MAILLP.
The additional funding will address cost overruns linked to a bottling unit and a distillery. According to the company, the increase in project costs is partly due to higher prices of key metals. A marginal expansion of the bottling hall and mezzanine area is also planned to accommodate longer automated bottling lines.
ABDL is the company behind brands including Officer’s Choice and has operations across the Indian spirits market. The company is also present in international markets and exports to 39 countries, according to the company filing.
The Aurangabad facility is expected to add manufacturing capacity for single malt whisky once commissioned. The investment will also mark ABDL’s entry into a segment that requires longer maturation periods and dedicated production infrastructure.
With the proposed investment and ongoing capacity projects, the company is expanding its manufacturing base while adding premium categories to its spirits portfolio.
Milky Mist Dairy Food Limited has commissioned a new Skyr and Greek Yogurt manufacturing facility at its integrated plant in Perundurai, Tamil Nadu, strengthening its presence in India's growing high-protein dairy and packaged food market. Built with an investment of approximately Rs 40 crore, the new facility uses Ultrafiltration Technology and has a processing capacity of up to 150 tonnes per day. The expansion is aimed at increasing production of high-protein dairy products and meeting rising consumer demand for protein-rich nutrition.
Milky Mist was among the first companies in India to introduce Ultrafiltration Technology for the production of Skyr and Greek Yogurt in 2022, targeting a category that has seen increasing consumer adoption over the last few years. The company's initial customised multi-product yogurt facility, established in 2022, had a production capacity of around 20 tonnes per day. Since then, annual demand for the category has grown by more than 50 percent, while demand for high-protein yogurts has more than doubled in recent months, according to the company.
The newly commissioned plant has been developed following an evaluation of international manufacturing technologies. Milky Mist said the facility will help improve production scale, maintain product consistency, and support the development of new high-protein dairy products for a broader consumer base. The project is part of the company's wider expansion and modernisation programme at its Perundurai facility and aligns with the objectives outlined during its initial public offering (IPO). The investment is expected to strengthen operational capacity in the value-added dairy segment, which continues to be one of the fastest-growing categories within India's food and beverage industry.
Dr. K Rathnam, Whole-time Director and Chief Executive Officer, Milky Mist Dairy Food Limited said, “High-protein nutrition is moving from a niche preference to an increasingly mainstream consumption trend. The strong growth in demand for Skyr and Greek Yogurt validates our early investment in this category and reinforces its long-term potential within India’s value-added FMCG market. The commissioning of our advanced manufacturing facility represents a strategic expansion of our technological capabilities. With processing capacity of up to 150 tonnes per day, it provides us with the scale to serve rising demand, accelerate innovation and expand the category. This investment strengthens Milky Mist’s position in the high-protein segment and creates a robust platform for sustained profitable growth.”
The expansion comes at a time when consumer interest in protein-rich foods, functional nutrition, and value-added dairy products is rising across urban and semi-urban markets. Industry demand for products such as Greek Yogurt, Skyr, high-protein snacks, and nutritional dairy products continues to grow as health-conscious consumption gains momentum.

a.title: Cyient DLM (NSE:CYIENTDLM): Why Did Its US Subsidiary Get a New Name?
a.content:
Cyient DLM Limited (NSE:CYIENTDLM) filed an intimation on 23 September 2026 under Regulation 30 of SEBI LODR, disclosing that its US-based step-down subsidiary has been renamed from "Altek Electronics, Inc." to "Cyient DLM Electronics Inc," effective from the same date.
Key Highlights
- The US step-down subsidiary formerly known as Altek Electronics, Inc. has been officially renamed Cyient DLM Electronics Inc, as disclosed on 23 September 2026.
- The name change is intended to align the US entity with the global Cyient DLM brand identity, according to the exchange filing.
- The company confirmed that ownership, business operations, assets, liabilities, contractual arrangements, and legal status of the entity remain entirely unchanged.
- The disclosure was made to both BSE and NSE pursuant to Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015.
About the Company
Cyient DLM Limited (NSE:CYIENTDLM) is an electronics manufacturing services company headquartered in Mysore, Karnataka, with a registered office in Hyderabad, Telangana. The company specialises in design-led manufacturing, offering printed circuit board assemblies, box-build products, and integrated solutions primarily for aerospace, defence, medical, and industrial sectors across domestic and international markets.
Announcement in Detail
In its Regulation 30 filing dated 23 September 2026, Cyient DLM Limited informed stock exchanges that the name of its step-down subsidiary incorporated in the United States has been changed from "Altek Electronics, Inc." to "Cyient DLM Electronics Inc." The company stated that this change is driven by the intent to bring the US entity in line with the broader Cyient DLM global brand, ensuring consistent brand representation across all international operations.
Critically, the filing confirmed that the renaming does not affect the subsidiary's ownership structure, day-to-day business operations, asset or liability positions, existing contractual arrangements, or legal standing under applicable US law. The step-down nature of the entity means it sits below a direct subsidiary in the corporate structure, and no shareholding change at any level has been disclosed in connection with this update.
Impact on Investors
Investors will note that the disclosed name change is administrative in nature. The filing explicitly states that there is no alteration to ownership, liabilities, or contractual terms, meaning that the financial exposure of Cyient DLM Limited to this subsidiary remains structurally unchanged. Shareholders will observe that no fresh equity issuance, dilution, or asset transfer has been associated with this action.
The filing shows that the company's US operations continue under the same legal entity, now carrying a name that reflects its parent brand. This reduces the risk of brand fragmentation across geographies, though the disclosed terms indicate no immediate financial impact to the consolidated entity arising from this change alone.
Sector / Market Context
India's electronics manufacturing services sector has seen expanding global footprints among domestic players, supported by the government's Production Linked Incentive scheme for electronics. Brand consolidation across international subsidiaries is a recognised practice among Indian manufacturers scaling operations in North America, as it supports uniform compliance, procurement, and client recognition across markets. Cyient DLM operates in the aerospace and defence electronics sub-segment, which has recorded increased order activity from both domestic and export customers in recent years according to industry body data.

a.title: Sun Pharma FY26 Results: Net profit up 5% YoY to ₹11,479 crore
a.content:
Sun Pharma FY26 Results: Net profit up 5% YoY to ₹11,479 crore
- Net profit for FY26 rose 5% YoY to ₹11,479 crore
- Gross sales grew 12% YoY to ₹58,220 crore
- EBITDA margin expanded to 30.3% from 29.0% in FY25
- India formulations contributed 33% to total revenue, while US formulations accounted for 29%
- Net cash position strengthened to ₹30,140 crore
*this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only.
Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited reported a net profit of ₹11,479 crore for FY26, marking a 5% increase year-on-year. The pharmaceutical major logged gross sales of ₹58,220 crore, reflecting a 12% growth compared to the previous fiscal year.
The company’s operational performance remained robust, with EBITDA rising 16% YoY to ₹17,731 crore. This expansion was supported by improved profitability metrics, as the EBITDA margin widened to 30.3% in FY26 from 29.0% in FY25. Gross margins also saw a steady upward trajectory, reaching 80.2% in FY26.
Segment-wise Revenue Performance
The revenue mix highlights the company's diversified global footprint, with international markets contributing significantly to the top line. India formulations remain the largest segment by contribution, followed closely by US formulations.
Emerging Markets demonstrated strong momentum with sales growing 19% YoY to ₹11,187 crore. The Rest of World segment also posted healthy growth, with revenues expanding 19% YoY to ₹8,568 crore. In contrast, US Formulations grew at a moderate pace of 3.6% YoY, reaching ₹16,824 crore.
What the Numbers Show
A divergence is visible between the robust double-digit revenue growth and the single-digit net profit expansion. While top-line figures expanded 12%, net profit grew only 5%. This gap is largely attributable to exceptional items disclosed in the financial notes. The adjusted net profit, which excludes these non-recurring provisions, stood at ₹12,402 crore, showing a more modest 3% increase. The reported profit includes adjustments for items such as GxMDL provisions and wage code impacts, which weighed on the bottom line despite strong operational cash flows.
Balance Sheet and Cash Flow Strength
Sun Pharma maintained a strong balance sheet position, characterized by significant cash reserves and low leverage. Net cash (excluding debt) increased to ₹30,140 crore in FY26 from ₹26,790 crore in FY25. The company’s cash and bank balances stood at ₹11,603 crore as of March 31, 2026.
Operating cash flow remained healthy, with net cash from operating activities at ₹12,420 crore for FY26. Free cash flow was recorded at ₹8,810 crore, indicating ample liquidity for future investments and shareholder returns.
R&D and Manufacturing Footprint
The company continues to prioritize innovation, with R&D spending accounting for 6.1% of sales in FY26. Cumulative R&D spend has reached approximately ₹34,500 crore to date. The innovative medicines portfolio now contributes 22% of total sales, up from 7.3% in FY18, signaling a strategic shift toward higher-value products.
Manufacturing capabilities span 40 facilities globally, supporting operations in over 100 countries. The company employs over 47,000 people worldwide and maintains a leadership position in the Indian pharmaceutical market with an 8.5% market share.

a.content:
Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited has released an investor presentation detailing its performance and strategic outlook. The document highlights substantial revenue growth, a dominant position in the Indian pharmaceutical market, and expanding global presence. Key focus areas include strengthening its innovative medicines portfolio, cost leadership, and sustainable long-term growth, underscoring a robust strategy for future profitability.
Sun Pharma Unveils Investor Presentation
Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited has shared its latest investor presentation, offering a comprehensive overview of its business operations, financial performance, and strategic initiatives. The presentation, dated September 22, 2026, outlines the company’s trajectory as a leading global specialty generic company and its commitment to creating lasting value.

a.title: Cyient (NSE:CYIENT): Why Did Independent Director Nitin Prasad Cease His Role?
a.content:
Cyient Limited (NSE:CYIENT) filed an intimation on 22 September 2026 under Regulation 30 of SEBI (LODR) Regulations 2015, disclosing that Mr. Nitin Prasad (DIN: 05261866) ceased to be a Non-Executive Independent Director upon completion of his three-year term on 21 September 2026.
Key Highlights
- Mr. Nitin Prasad (DIN: 05261866) ceased as Non-Executive Independent Director of Cyient Limited effective 21 September 2026 at midnight upon completion of his three-year tenure.
- Alongside his board role, Mr. Prasad also ceased to be a member of the Leadership, Nomination and Remuneration Committee of the company with immediate effect.
- The cessation is attributed solely to completion of tenure and is not a resignation; the filing confirms no other material reasons are involved.
- The disclosure was made in compliance with Regulation 30 read with Schedule III, Part A, Para A (7B) of SEBI Listing Regulations and the SEBI Circular dated 13 July 2023.
About the Company
Cyient Limited (NSE:CYIENT), headquartered at Madhapur, Hyderabad, is a global engineering and technology solutions company. It serves clients across aerospace, defence, utilities, medical technology, semiconductor, and communications sectors. The company delivers design, engineering, manufacturing, and digital transformation services from delivery centres across India, Europe, North America, and Asia-Pacific, with CIN L72200TG1991PLC013134.
Announcement in Detail
Pursuant to Regulation 30 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations 2015, Cyient Limited informed both BSE (Scrip Code: 532175) and NSE (Scrip Code: CYIENT) that Mr. Nitin Prasad completed his three-year term as an Independent Director on 21 September 2026 at 24:00 hours IST. The filing, signed by Deputy Company Secretary Ravi Kumar Nukala, confirms the cessation was due exclusively to the expiry of his prescribed tenure period.
Simultaneously, Mr. Prasad ceased his membership of the Leadership, Nomination and Remuneration Committee. The Annexure A attached to the filing explicitly states that the cessation is not attributable to any other reason beyond tenure completion, and the item relating to confirmation of no other material reasons is noted as not applicable to a resignation scenario, since this is a scheduled end of term.
Impact on Investors
Investors will note that the departure is a scheduled governance event rather than a mid-term exit, which the filing distinguishes clearly from a resignation. The disclosed terms indicate that no additional material reasons, disputes, or covenant-related concerns have been cited by Mr. Prasad, reducing uncertainty around the circumstances of the change.
Shareholders will observe that the company's board composition has changed with the exit of one independent director and the concurrent loss of that member from the Leadership, Nomination and Remuneration Committee. The filing does not disclose a replacement appointment, so investors may wish to monitor future exchange filings for a successor nomination to assess whether the board retains the required independent director quorum under SEBI norms.
Sector / Market Context
SEBI's LODR framework requires listed companies to maintain a minimum proportion of independent directors on their boards, with stricter norms for companies with a non-executive chairperson. The engineering and technology services sector in India, which includes players like Cyient, has seen increasing regulatory focus on board-level governance disclosures following SEBI's enhanced Regulation 30 circular of July 2023, which mandated more structured and timely disclosure of director-level changes across all listed entities.

a.title: First-Ever Standardized U.S. Treatment Recommendations Issued for Adults with Severe Alopecia Areata; Sun Pharma Welcomes Milestone
a.content:
New treatment recommendations provide clinicians and patients with consensus guidance to effective alopecia areata treatment
Recommendations establish oral JAK inhibitors as primary therapy, closing the gap between medical innovations and access to standardized patient care
 
PRINCETON, N.J., Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited (Reuters: SUN.BO, Bloomberg: SUNP IN, NSE: SUNPHARMA, BSE: 524715, together with its subsidiaries and/or affiliated companies, "Sun Pharma") today expressed its support for the first standardized United States treatment recommendations for adults with severe alopecia areata (AA). Developed through a rigorous, multi-round survey process, the consensus guidance issued independently by the National Alopecia Areata Foundation (NAAF) and the American Hair Research Society (AHRS) reflect the collective clinical expertise of 30 leading U.S. alopecia areata specialists. The treatment recommendations were published in Journal of the American Medical Association Dermatology (JAMA Dermatology).
AA is an autoimmune disease where the body's immune system mistakenly attacks hair follicles, leading to hair loss not only limited to the scalp, but can also affect other hair bearing body sites. Impacting an estimated 300,000 U.S. adults, severe AA causes more than hair loss; it also carries a significant physical and psychosocial burden for patients. The expert guidance adopts a standardized severity scale that goes beyond scalp hair loss percentage to include psychosocial impact, eyebrow and eyelash involvement, and prior treatment response, more accurately reflecting the challenges of living with severe AA.
"For patients with severe alopecia areata, the absence of standardized treatment recommendations has meant inconsistent and delayed access to effective therapy," said Arash Mostaghimi, MD, MPA, MPH, FAAD, Guidelines Lead and Vice Chair of Clinical Trials and Innovation and Associate Professor of Dermatology at Brigham and Women's Hospital/Harvard Medical School. "The expert panel determined oral JAK inhibitors as an appropriate first-line therapy in combination with supportive resources and adjunctive therapies, bringing consistency to how we treat this disease."
Key outcomes of the consensus process include:
- A standardized definition of severe AA using the Alopecia Areata Scale for Clinical Use, previously published in the Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology
- Oral JAK inhibitors (FDA-approved) established as the primary, long-term treatment of choice
- A framework for adjunctive therapies, like topicals and corticosteroids, tailored by site-specific indication (scalp, facial hair, eyebrows, eyelashes)
- Appropriate alternatives for patients with active atopy (a genetic predisposition to an exaggerated immune response) or history of atopic disease
- A longitudinal management model to guide ongoing patient care and treatment adjustments through trial duration period
- Mental health screening, patient advocacy organization referrals, and cranial prostheses formally integrated as pillars of holistic management
"Many individuals with alopecia areata struggle to find healthcare providers equipped to help them achieve their treatment goals. While the approval of JAK inhibitors was a major milestone in expanding access to effective care, significant gaps remain," said Laura Maciag, Chief Operating Officer and Interim Chief Executive Officer, National Alopecia Areata Foundation (NAAF). "These consensus recommendations aim to further democratize alopecia management by offering actionable guidance that any clinician can readily implement in practice."
Marking a meaningful step forward for patients, clinicians and the broader alopecia areata community, the published consensus recommendations are now available in JAMA Dermatology and can be accessed here. Additional resources are also available from NAAF at www.naaf.org/treatment-recs.
"These first-ever standardized U.S. treatment recommendations mark a defining moment for the alopecia areata community," said Ahmad Naim, MD, Senior Vice President, North America Chief Medical Officer, Sun Pharma. "As the maker of LEQSELVI® (deuruxolitinib), an FDA-approved oral JAK inhibitor for adults with severe alopecia areata, we see these consensus-based recommendations as an impactful advancement for healthcare providers toward further improving clinical decision making and care. We remain committed to providing access to effective and safe long-term treatment for every patient and clinician we serve."
About LEQSELVI®
LEQSELVI (deuruxolitinib) 8 mg tablets is an oral selective inhibitor of Janus kinases JAK1 and JAK2 FDA-approved for the treatment of adults with severe alopecia areata. Alopecia areata is an autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks hair follicles, resulting in partial or complete loss of hair on the scalp and body. Alopecia areata may affect up to 2.5% of the United States and global population during their lifetime. The scalp is the most commonly affected area, but any hair-bearing site can be affected alone or together with the scalp. Onset of the disease can occur throughout life and affects both women and men. Alopecia areata can be associated with serious psychological consequences, including anxiety and depression. There are currently limited approved treatment options available for alopecia areata.
Please click here for full Prescribing Information Including BOXED WARNING and Medication Guide.
LEQSELVI Important Safety Information & Use
What is LEQSELVI (deuruxolitinib)?
LEQSELVI is used to treat adults with severe hair loss (alopecia areata).
It is not known if LEQSELVI is safe and effective in children.
Who should not take LEQSELVI?
Do not take LEQSELVI if you are a poor metabolizer of CYP2C9 medicines or are taking moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitors. Before starting treatment, your healthcare provider should test you for CYP2C9 variants.  Tell your healthcare provider if you take moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitor medicines. Ask your healthcare provider or pharmacist if you are not sure.
What is the most important safety information I should know about LEQSELVI?
LEQSELVI is a medicine that affects your immune system and can lower the ability of your immune system to fight infections. Some people have had serious infections during treatment with LEQSELVI. Some people may die from these infections... Your healthcare provider should test you for TB before starting treatment with LEQSELVI and should watch you closely for signs and symptoms of TB during treatment. You should not start taking LEQSELVI if you have any kind of infection unless your healthcare provider tells you it is okay
There may be an increased risk of major cardiovascular events in people 50 years of age and older who have at least one heart disease risk factor and are taking a medicine in the class of medicines called JAK inhibitors, especially if they are a current or past smoker.
LEQSELVI may increase your risk of certain cancers by changing the way your immune system works.
Blood clots in the veins of your legs, lungs or brain (cerebral venous sinus thrombosis, CVT) can happen in some people during treatment with LEQSELVI. These may be life-threatening.
Some people taking LEQSELVI can get tears in their stomach or intestines.
If you have diabetes, your healthcare provider may instruct you to check your blook sugar levels more often during treatment with LEQSELVI. Call your healthcare provider if you have any problems with low blood sugar (hypoglycemia).
Before you start and taking LEQSELVI and during treatment, your healthcare provider should do blood tests to check for increased fat levels in your blood, Low white and/or red blood cell counts. You should not take LEQSELVI if your white blood cell or red blood cell counts are too low.
What should I tell my healthcare provider before starting LEQSELVI?
Tell your healthcare provider if you have an infection; are a current or past smoker; have had a heart attack, or other heart problems or stroke; have had blood clots in your legs, lungs or brain; have kidney problems; have liver problems; have any stomach area (abdominal) pain or been diagnosed with diverticulitis or ulcers in your stomach or intestine; have low red or white blood cell counts; or have recently received or are scheduled to receive a vaccine.
Females who are able to become pregnant should use effective birth control (contraception) during treatment with LEQSELVI. Talk to your healthcare provider if you are planning to become pregnant. You should not breastfeed during treatment with LEQSELVI and for one day after the last dose.
What else should I be aware of when taking LEQSELVI?
Your healthcare provider should do blood tests before you start taking LEQSELVI and during treatment to check for increased fat (lipid) levels in your blood (triglycerides and cholesterol), low red blood cell counts, or low white blood cells.
How should I take LEQSELVI?
Take LEQSELVI 2 times a day with or without food.
What are the possible side effects of LEQSELVI?

About the NAAF/AHRS DELPHI Consensus Treatment Recommendations
The treatment recommendations were developed using a validated Delphi consensus methodology, achieving ≥70% expert agreement across all core recommendations. A steering group of 30 AA specialists reviewed published data on 29 treatments, reaching consensus on a standardized definition of disease severity, treatment pathways for primary and adjunctive therapies, and a longitudinal management model. The treatment recommendations are designed as a living resource, with plans for ongoing updates as new clinical evidence emerges.

ADIA offloads 3.5 crore Lenskart shares for Rs 2,390.6 crore as the eyewear company's stock rallies 51.3 per cent year-to-date Lenskart, ADIA, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, Platinum Jasmine, block deal, Rs 2,390.6 crore, stake sale, eyewear, Q1 FY27, stock market, SoftBank, Temasek, Alpha Wave
Early investor Abu Dhabi Investment Authority has offloaded 3.5 crore shares of eyewear company Lenskart through its holding entity Platinum Jasmine A 2018 Trust, as per a media report.
The shares were sold at Rs 683.02 apiece, generating proceeds of Rs 2,390.6 crore through the bulk deal. The transaction came at a price slightly below Lenskart's closing price of Rs 683.85 on the NSE.
This marks the second instance of ADIA reducing its stake in Lenskart in recent months. In June, the investor sold 4 crore shares in a block deal worth Rs 1,960 crore.
The June transaction valued Lenskart shares at Rs 490 apiece, around 40 per cent below the latest closing price.
At the end of the June quarter, Platinum Jasmine A 2018 Trust held 16.98 crore Lenskart shares, representing a 9.77 per cent stake in the company. The latest sale accounts for slightly over 20 per cent of ADIA's holding and around 2 per cent of Lenskart's total equity.
Lenskart's shares have gained 51.3 per cent on a year-to-date basis, providing an opportunity for several early investors to monetise their holdings. SoftBank, Temasek and Alpha Wave have also sold shares in the company in recent months.
In September, BNP Paribas, Societe Generale and US-based hedge fund Millennium Management sold Lenskart shares worth Rs 2,670.2 crore through multiple bulk deals.
Lenskart touched an all-time high of Rs 725 on 18 September. The company made its stock market debut at Rs 390 per share on the BSE in November 2025.
The stock's recent rally followed positive brokerage commentary after Lenskart reported strong Q1 FY27 results. Jefferies raised its target price to Rs 680 from Rs 600, while Macquarie increased its target to Rs 675 from Rs 625.
Lenskart's consolidated net profit jumped 273 per cent year-on-year to Rs 228.4 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 61.2 crore a year earlier. Operating revenue rose 43 per cent year-on-year and 8 per cent quarter-on-quarter to Rs 2,714.2 crore.
However, Lenskart shares closed 3.3 per cent lower at Rs 683.85 on the NSE.

a.title: THIS MORNING: Masdar exits hydrogen project with OMV + Adia offloads more of Lenskart
a.content:
Good morning, everyone. We begin with some sad news: Dubai begins 10 days of mourning for Sheikh Ahmed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, brother of Dubai Ruler Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid and deputy chairman of Dubai Police, group chairman of ARM Holding, and president of Al Wasl Sports Club.
In business news, the wartime financial cushion for UAE banks is likely to start coming off as the AED 13.5 bn in loan deferrals the Central Bank of the UAE (CBUAE) granted at the start of the regional conflict starts coming due this month, presenting the first real test of UAE bank asset quality without regulatory support.
Meanwhile, UAE developers continue to look abroad, with Eagle Hills signing on for a USD 12 bn mixed-use waterfront project in the Maldives in what would be one of the largest single foreign investment commitments the country has landed, as well as the latest stop in Mohamed Alabbar’s quickly expanding overseas pipeline.
Elsewhere, Masdar walked away from its planned 49% stake in OMV’s 140 MW electrolysis project in Austria, with the two firms saying they’ll keep exploring other ways to collaborate, and Adia has once again trimmed its stake in Indian eyewear retailer Lenskart.
With the EnterpriseAM Egypt Forum two weeks away, here's what's shaping up on the agenda:
- Where does AI fit on the list of topics keeping CEOs awake at night as they plan their strategies for 2027 and beyond?
- Is there really an AI opportunity for Egypt?
- An industry insider warns that your company is about to get attacked.
- What does AI mean for your company, your team, and your job?
- What does AI mean for your family — from what your kids should be studying to how to protect aging parents from scams and disinformation
Join us on 5 October in Cairo. Attendance is by invitation only, and seats are filling up quickly.
Request your invitation here.
BlueFive has more in the pipeline
BlueFive’s USD 3 bn defense fund, first flagged back in April, is now “ready to launch,” founder Hazem Ben-Gacem told Semafor. He also confirmed a Jakarta office is coming, aimed at chasing shariah-compliant demand across Southeast Asia off the back of last year’s Sidra Capital buy. In addition, he said he’s eyeing an agreement with one of the region’s stock exchanges to convert it into a venue for digital assets.
Why it matters: BlueFive has been one of the region’s most active dealmakers this year, war notwithstanding — its USD 3 bn Onyx tech fund closed just before the war started, on top of a 30% stake in Bugatti and backing for an Islamic digital bank. At USD 15 bn AUM and counting royal families across the Gulf (bar Qatar) as founding LPs, this is a firm that moves fast once it starts talking.
Adia offloads from Lenskart again
Adia offloads more of Lenskart: Abu Dhabi Investment Authority’s (Adia) investment vehicle Platinum Jasmine A 2018 Trust may have offloaded a 1.7% stake in India’s Lenskart Solutions through a block transaction worth INR 20.4 bn (USD 213.8 mn), CNBC-TV18 reports, citing people it says are in the know.
IN CONTEXT- As of 30 June, the trust held a 9.77% stake in the Indian eyewear retailer, according to NDTVProfit. The transaction follows another block transaction in June this year, when Platinum Jasmine sold 2.3% of Lenskart, or 40 mn shares, at INR 490 apiece for around INR 19.6 bn (USD 205 mn).
Lenskart’s latest results give the sell-down some context. Net income jumped 270% y-o-y to INR 2.2 bn (USD 22.9 mn) in 1Q FY 2027, while revenue climbed 43% to INR 27.1 bn (USD 282.6 mn). The stock is up 64.5% YTD. That means the Gulf sovereign allocator is likely banking gains on an early tech-retail bet while keeping the bulk of its stake intact.
BACKGROUND- Adia first built its position back in March 2023, when Platinum Jasmine put in USD 500 mn for a 10% stake — one of its earliest bets on India’s consumer-tech boom, as we noted when Lenskart went public last November.
IHC clarifies who sits at the top
International Holding Company (IHC) confirmed Fount Trust as its ultimate parent following a restructuring above Royal Group, according to an ADX disclosure (pdf). The trust is intended to preserve ownership continuity across generations, without changing who ultimately controls the Abu Dhabi investment group or affecting its operations and strategy.
The ownership chain explained: Pal Group remains IHC’s majority shareholder, Royal Group controls Pal Group, and Fount Trust sits at the top. Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed, IHC’s chairman, is the trust’s ultimate beneficial owner, The National reports. IHC’s existing governance and ADX disclosure obligations remain unchanged.
Not an entirely new arrangement: Fount Trust became IHC’s parent in 2025 and has already appeared as the ultimate parent in financial statements from other group companies, including 2PointZero Group, Palms Sports, and Emirates Stallions Group, according to The National.
Air returns to markets — this time for debt
Dubai shisha maker Air is heading back to capital markets just four months after its Nasdaq debut, this time with a planned USD 400 mn debt offering, Zawya reports. Air has launched a USD-denominated Regulation S offering of senior unsecured notes backed by Nasdaq-listed parent Air Global. Proceeds will repay outstanding term loans and revolving credit facilities, including related costs, with any remainder going toward general corporate purposes. Moody’s assigned the proposed notes a Ba3 rating.
From equity to debt: Air Global, the parent of shisha brand Al Fakher, began trading under ticker AIIR in May following a SPAC merger. We reported in April that the transaction targeted a USD 1.75 bn valuation despite regional volatility and higher logistics costs from Hormuz disruptions.
The post-listing buildout continues: Air is also planning a Romanian manufacturing facility for 1Q 2027, with annual capacity exceeding 4k tons of flavored shisha molasses.
Masdar walks away from Austrian hydrogen wager
Masdar pulled out of a planned EUR 600 mn green hydrogen project in Austria, reversing an agreement that would have given it a 49% stake alongside Austrian energy group OMV, Reuters reports, citing Austrian newspaper Salzburger Nachrichten. Masdar had been expected to invest several hundred mn EUR in the venture, which was announced last November. OMV attributed the withdrawal to “strategic changes in Abu Dhabi” without elaborating.
The plant is going ahead without Masdar: OMV says the departure will not affect the 140 MW project, which is expected to produce up to 23k tons of green hydrogen annually starting end-2027. The European Investment Bank has committed a EUR 450 mn loan, while Austria has indicated it will provide public funding, leaving the project largely financed.
The bigger picture: The Austrian exit follows other pullbacks from green hydrogen for Masdar. We reported last month that the company scrapped a planned 100 MW hydrogen plant for Emsteel, after previously pushing its 1 mn-ton annual hydrogen target beyond 2030 amid cost and demand headwinds. Masdar has also redirected solar capacity once earmarked for green ammonia toward AI data centers.
A settlement of Paramount importance
Paramount has settled the US antitrust lawsuit threatening its USD 110 bn Warner Bros. Discovery takeover, clearing the way for the Gulf-backed merger, Bloomberg reports. The media giant agreed to commit to an annual 30-film requirement, spend an extra USD 1.5 bn on US production over the next five years, and enter distribution agreements for its cable arms. These are among several terms agreed upon with the California-led group of US states.
L’imad clinches US media foothold: The merger is backed by nearly USD 24 bn in commitments from Abu Dhabi’s L’imad, Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, and the Qatar Investment Authority. The Gulf funds are set to hold minority, non-voting stakes in the combined company.
PSA
Abu Dhabi is putting the verification rules behind its carbon reporting program into place, with the Environment Agency - Abu Dhabi (EAD) issuing a resolution setting out how companies must have their greenhouse gas emissions independently checked, according to an Abu Dhabi Media Office statement. Facilities in targeted sectors that meet specified emissions thresholds must submit reports for review by EAD-accredited verifiers.
What changes for businesses? EAD will register and accredit independent verifiers, paving the way for environmental consultancies and carbon-accounting specialists to participate. The agency will also establish a digital database to collect, verify, and store emissions reports, helping inform future emissions policies.
BACKGROUND- Abu Dhabi announced its carbon reporting program in December 2024, requiring major industrial and energy emitters to begin submitting independently verified data in 2026 ahead of a planned domestic carbon pricing mechanism. That followed an earlier decree requiring EAD-licensed businesses to report energy use, water consumption, and emissions annually.
WEATHER- Temperatures will be hitting highs of 39°C today in Dubai and 40°C in Abu Dhabi, with lows of 30°C in both emirates, according to our favorite weather app.
The big story abroad
In the absence of a single story dominating the international press, several developments have taken the spotlight. Here are the most pressing updates making the rounds this morning.
JP Morgan Asset Management has signed an agreement with the Qatar Investment Authority (QIA) to establish a USD 20 bn multi-asset strategic partnership, which will span public and private equities and credit. The effort includes a USD 15 bn long-term public equities mandate for QIA and a USD 5 bn private markets initiative targeting established US middle-market companies.
US bases on Greenland? The Trump administration is reportedly looking to open two military bases in Greenland as per a trilateral agreement expected to be signed with Denmark and the Greenlandic government today. The locations include a former Cold War-era base in southern Greenland and a facility on the east coast.
AI will reshape credit ratings + ins., S&P says: Variations in how quickly financial institutions adopt AI, manage governance, and prepare operationally mean the technology will play a growing role in either bolstering or eroding their credit standing in the coming years, S&P Ratings said in a report. Ins. players are also expected to be swept up in the new AI-powered status quo, with many of the largest multiline insurers and reinsurers already transitioning to formal AI integration.

a.title: ADIA sells 2.01% stake in Lenskart Solutions for ₹2,390 crore
a.content:
Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA) pared its holding in eyewear company Lenskart Solutions on Monday, selling shares worth Rs 2,390 crore in an open market transaction.
ADIA, through its affiliate Platinum Jasmine A 2018 Trust, sold 3.5 crore shares, representing a 2.01 per cent stake in Gurugram-based Lenskart Solutions, according to the bulk deal data on the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
The shares were offloaded at an average price of Rs 683.02 apiece, taking the aggregate value to Rs 2,390.57 crore.
The transaction brought ADIA's holding down to 7.76 per cent from 9.77 per cent. After the stake sale, ADIA will remain the second largest public shareholder in Lenskart after SoftBank.
The buyers of the shares could not be identified from the exchange data.
Lenskart's shares on Monday fell 3.10 per cent to close at Rs 685.30 apiece on the NSE.
The stake sale comes after a series of transactions by existing investors in the eyewear retailer.
In June this year, technology investor SoftBank Group divested a 3.25 per cent stake in Lenskart Solutions for Rs 2,873 crore.
In May, Lenskart reported a 7.5 per cent year-on-year decline in consolidated profit after tax (PAT) to Rs 203.6 crore in the March quarter due to a rise in expenses on components and inventories.  The company had posted a PAT of Rs 220.1 crore in the same period a year ago, according to a regulatory filing.  Its revenue from operations grew 45.62 per cent to around Rs 2,516 crore in the March quarter from Rs 1,728 crore in the year-ago period.
Published on September 21, 2026

a.title: Lenskart (NSE: LENSKART) Block Deal: Early Investor Trims Stake Worth Over Rs 2,000 Crore
a.content:
Highlights
- An early institutional investor in Lenskart sold a stake worth over Rs 2,000 crore through a block deal.
- The transaction is part of a broader pattern of post-listing exits by early backers.
- Several domestic and global institutional investors have participated as buyers in recent deals.
- Lenskart's post-IPO lock-in periods have progressively opened up larger blocks of shares.
- Early investor stake sales do not necessarily reflect a company's operating performance.
A Large Block Deal in Focus
Shares of Lenskart Solutions (NSE: LENSKART) were in the spotlight after a block deal involving a sizeable stake, valued at over Rs 2,000 crore, changed hands on the stock exchanges. The transaction added to a series of large secondary sales by early institutional backers of the eyewear retailer that have taken place since the company's stock market listing.
Who Are the Sellers in Such Deals
Early investors in newly listed companies typically include private equity funds, sovereign wealth vehicles and venture capital firms that backed the business well before its public listing. In Lenskart's case, reported sellers in various block deals over recent months have included large global investment entities that held stakes acquired during the company's earlier funding rounds.
Why Early Backers Sell After Listing
A large shareholder reducing its holding does not necessarily signal a negative view of the company's prospects. Private equity and venture capital investors commonly monetise part of their investment once a company lists and stock market liquidity improves, allowing them to return capital to their own investors while often retaining a residual stake in the business.
The Mechanics of a Block Deal
A block deal refers to a large transaction in listed shares of Lenskart (NSE: LENSKART) that is executed through a special trading window on the stock exchange, typically outside the regular continuous trading session. Such deals allow large blocks of shares to change hands at a negotiated price without causing excessive short-term volatility in the open market, and the details are subsequently disclosed to the exchanges.
Who Typically Buys in These Transactions
Block deals of this nature often attract a mix of domestic mutual funds, insurance companies, pension funds and foreign institutional investors as buyers, reflecting continued institutional interest in the underlying business even as early investors reduce their positions. Participation from a broad base of buyers is often seen as a sign of sustained demand for the stock.
Regulatory Disclosure Requirements
Under securities regulations, any transaction of this size in a listed company is subject to disclosure norms, with details of the buyer and seller typically made available through exchange filings within a defined reporting window. This transparency allows market participants to track shifts in ownership patterns over time and assess how a company's shareholder base is evolving following its public listing.
What This Means for the Stock's Free Float
Each successive block deal involving early investors gradually increases the proportion of Lenskart's (NSE: LENSKART) shares that are held by a wider, more diversified set of institutional and public shareholders, commonly referred to as the free float. A rising free float can, over time, contribute to better liquidity in the stock for all categories of investors.
Key Insights
The latest block deal involving a stake worth over Rs 2,000 crore in Lenskart (NSE: LENSKART) reflects the continuation of a broader trend of early investors gradually monetising their holdings following the company's stock market listing. While such transactions can draw attention to short-term price movements, they are a routine part of how early-stage investors realise returns on long-held positions, and their occurrence does not by itself indicate a change in the underlying business. This is not investment advice; readers considering any transaction in listed securities should assess their own financial circumstances and consult a qualified advisor.
FAQs
Q: What is a block deal?
A: A block deal is a large transaction in listed shares executed through a special exchange window, typically at a negotiated price outside regular trading.
Q: Does an early investor selling shares mean the company is doing poorly?
A: Not necessarily. Early investors often sell part of their holding after listing simply to realise returns, regardless of the company's performance.
Q: Who usually buys shares in a block deal?
A: Buyers often include domestic mutual funds, insurance companies and foreign institutional investors.
Q: What happens to a company's free float after such deals?
A: The free float, or shares held by the wider public and institutions, typically increases as early investors sell down their stakes.
Q: Are block deal sales reported to stock exchanges?
A: Yes, block deal transactions are disclosed to the stock exchanges as part of standard market reporting requirements.

a.title: Lenskart Solutions (NSE:LENSKART) Sees Major Block Deal as Shareholding Changes Draw Attention
a.content:
Highlights
- Lenskart Solutions witnessed a sizeable block transaction involving a meaningful portion of its outstanding equity.
- The transaction appears to involve an existing institutional shareholder reducing part of its holding.
- The company’s underlying eyewear operations are not directly altered by the secondary-market transaction.
- Large block deals can temporarily influence market activity because substantial quantities of shares change hands at once.
- Investors may focus on subsequent shareholding disclosures for confirmation of ownership changes.
Lenskart Solutions Limited (NSE:LENSKART) came into focus after a large block transaction involving around 3.53 crore shares, representing approximately 2% of the company’s equity, was reported in the market. The transaction appears to involve a partial exit by an existing institutional shareholder, although the final identities of all buyers and sellers would need to be established through relevant disclosures. The development primarily represents a change in ownership between shareholders rather than a change in Lenskart’s day-to-day business operations.
Block Deal Brings Ownership Structure Into Focus
A block deal is a large transaction in which a substantial number of shares change hands between market participants through a dedicated trading mechanism. Such transactions are generally used by institutional or large shareholders because executing the same quantity through ordinary market trades could create greater disruption.
In Lenskart’s case, approximately 3.53 crore shares were reported to have changed hands through the transaction. Reports ahead of the deal had indicated that an existing institutional shareholder could sell up to around 3 crore shares, equivalent to approximately 1.7% of Lenskart’s equity.
The company’s earlier ownership disclosures show that the shareholder associated with the proposed transaction was among Lenskart’s larger non-promoter investors. The latest transaction could therefore reduce that investor’s ownership while introducing or increasing the holdings of other investors.
However, a secondary share sale does not provide new capital to the company. The shares simply move from one investor to another, meaning the transaction should be distinguished from a fresh issue of shares in which the company itself raises funds.
Why Large Block Transactions Attract Attention
Large shareholder transactions often attract market attention because they can alter the ownership structure of a recently listed company. When a substantial investor reduces its stake, market participants may assess whether the transaction reflects portfolio rebalancing, partial monetisation or another shareholder-specific decision.
It is important, however, not to automatically interpret such a transaction as a judgment on the underlying business. Institutional investors may sell shares for several reasons unrelated to a company’s operating performance, including fund maturity, liquidity requirements, asset allocation or portfolio concentration.
A block transaction can also temporarily increase the supply of shares available in the market. Because a large quantity is being placed at one time, transaction pricing may differ from prevailing market levels to facilitate execution.
Once the transaction is completed, attention generally shifts toward the identity of the buyers and the revised ownership structure. Future shareholding disclosures can provide more clarity on how the company’s investor base has changed.
Core Eyewear Business Remains Separate From the Deal
The block transaction does not directly change Lenskart’s operating business. The company continues to operate in the eyewear market through its integrated retail, digital and supply-chain model.
For readers assessing the development, separating ownership changes from business fundamentals is useful. The sale of shares by an existing investor does not change customer demand, store operations, manufacturing capabilities or the company’s ability to execute its commercial strategy.
Lenskart has also continued to make corporate and strategic disclosures during 2026, including activity related to acquisitions and business restructuring. Its investor-relations records show ongoing corporate developments beyond the shareholding transaction, indicating that the company continues to pursue its wider operating strategy.
The significance of the block deal therefore lies mainly in shareholder composition and market liquidity rather than in any immediate operational change.
What Could Change After the Transaction
The most visible impact of a large secondary transaction is likely to be reflected in future ownership disclosures. If the reported seller reduced its stake materially, its percentage holding would decline while buyers participating in the transaction may emerge as larger shareholders.
A broader institutional investor base can also change the distribution of ownership in a listed company. Depending on who acquired the shares, the transaction could increase holdings among domestic or international institutions, funds or other eligible investors.
Official disclosures following settlement will provide the clearest confirmation of these changes. Until then, reported seller identities should be treated as provisional where they have not been formally confirmed.
For Lenskart, the transaction comes after its transition into a publicly listed company, making changes in institutional ownership a more visible part of its market profile.
Key Insights
Lenskart Solutions’ large block deal represents a meaningful secondary-market ownership transaction rather than a change in the company’s operating business. Approximately 3.53 crore shares were reported to have changed hands, while an existing institutional shareholder had earlier been expected to reduce part of its holding. The main issues to monitor are confirmation of the final buyers and sellers and the resulting shareholding pattern. The company’s underlying retail operations, customer strategy and business execution remain separate from the ownership transfer.
FAQs
Q: What happened in the Lenskart block deal?
A: A large quantity of Lenskart Solutions shares changed hands through a block transaction involving approximately 3.53 crore shares.
Q: What is a block deal?
A: A block deal is a large share transaction executed through a dedicated trading mechanism, generally involving institutional or large investors.
Q: Does the transaction provide funds to Lenskart?
A: No. It is a secondary-market transaction between shareholders rather than a fresh issue of shares by the company.
Q: Does the deal change Lenskart’s business operations?
A: No. The transaction primarily changes share ownership and does not directly alter the company’s eyewear operations.
Q: What should be monitored next?
A: Subsequent ownership disclosures may provide confirmation of the buyers, sellers and the revised shareholding structure.
