a.title: Lenskart Vs Eternal: Which High-PE New-Age Stock Has The Stronger Investment Case?
a.content:
Fast-growing consumer companies often trade at expensive valuations when investors expect them to become much bigger over time. Lenskart and Eternal are both in that category, but their businesses are very different. Lenskart is expanding its eyewear business in India and overseas, while Eternal already has a profitable food-delivery business and is now betting heavily on Blinkit for its next phase of growth.
But there is one thing both stocks have in common: they are extremely expensive. Lenskart currently trades at a PE ratio of around 181 times, while Eternal trades at nearly 737 times earnings. At valuations like these, investors are not paying for what the companies earn today.
They are paying for what they could earn several years from now. That makes the real question simple: which company has the stronger business to support such a high valuation?
Two Premium Valuations With Different Growth Engines
Lenskart’s growth story is relatively easy to understand. It sells eyewear, adds stores, gets more people tested, sells more pairs and gradually moves customers towards higher-value products. In Q1FY27, revenue grew 33.6 percent year-on-year, pre-Ind AS EBITDA grew 95 percent and PAT rose 2.8 times to Rs. 228 crore. Volumes grew 25.7 percent, while India same-store sales growth remained strong at 18.3 percent.
That growth is also broad-based. India revenue grew 30.7 percent to Rs. 1,531 crore, while international revenue grew 38 percent to Rs. 1,203 crore. Lenskart added 132 net stores during the quarter, taking the network to 3,459 stores. More importantly, consolidated product margin crossed 70 percent for the first time.
Eternal is growing faster, largely because Blinkit is scaling at a much quicker pace. In Q1FY27, Blinkit’s NOV jumped 86 percent YoY to Rs. 17,132 crore, helped by more stores, a wider product range and customers ordering more frequently in existing markets. Food delivery also grew more than 20 percent, while District grew 60 percent. This pushed Eternal’s overall B2C NOV up 54 percent.
However, Eternal’s headline adjusted revenue growth of 173 percent needs some context. Blinkit has shifted towards owning inventory, which means Eternal now records the full value of goods sold as revenue. On a like-for-like basis, adjusted revenue still grew a strong 66 percent.
Lenskart Is Turning Growth Into Better Economics
The biggest point in Lenskart’s favour is that the operating model is already showing leverage. Its gross margin moved from 69.2 percent in Q2FY26 to 68.9 percent in Q3, 69.6 percent in Q4 and 70.3 percent in Q1FY27. At the same time, EBITDA margin moved from around 19.9 percent in Q2FY26 to 21.7 percent in Q1FY27.
This is happening even while the rupee has weakened against the RMB (Chinese Yuan), which matters because frames and components have China linked costs. Management’s answer has been to manufacture more in-house, increase backward integration and use scale to negotiate better costs.
The Hyderabad facility, which is being built for around 50 million pairs annually, is an important part of this strategy. Management had already highlighted in Q3FY26 that higher in-house manufacturing could allow future margin gains that were then being absorbed by rupee-RMB depreciation.
There is also growth at both ends of the customer base. Lenskart says its Rs. 500 offering can now be sold sustainably, while premiumisation is moving faster than expected. Owndays premium lenses are generating more than Rs. 1,500 crore of annual prescription eyewear sales, while Rodenstock and Tokai together contribute around Rs. 250 crore.
Most importantly, accounting profit is turning into cash. Q1FY27 operating cash flow was Rs. 297 crore against roughly Rs. 207 crore of store and plant capex. ROCE improved to 23.2 percent from 14.6 percent in FY26. That gives Lenskart room to keep opening stores and investing in manufacturing without the growth story depending entirely on fresh capital.
Eternal Is Increasingly A Blinkit Story
Eternal’s food-delivery business is now the stabilising engine. Zomato’s food-delivery NOV grew more than 20 percent in Q1FY27 to Rs. 10,769 crore, while adjusted EBITDA margin reached 5.6 percent of NOV. That produced Rs. 606 crore of adjusted EBITDA, up 34 percent year-on-year.
The bigger excitement, however, is Blinkit. Its NOV grew 86 percent to Rs. 17,132 crore, 200 net stores were added and the network reached 2,443 stores. Blinkit also moved from an adjusted EBITDA loss of Rs. 162 crore in Q1FY26 to a profit of Rs. 102 crore in Q1FY27.
The journey across the last year matters. In Q2FY26, management was still saying that overall Blinkit profitability was a moving average between mature profitable markets and the cost of new stores, cities and customers. It was willing to keep spending while customer acquisition costs and lifetime value remained healthy. By Q3FY26, the business had reached adjusted EBITDA break-even, although management continued to caution that competitive intensity could make the margin journey uneven.
By Q1FY27, management had enough visibility to point towards the upper end of its long-term 5-6 percent adjusted EBITDA margin range. Older Blinkit customers are also spending around three times more than they did three years ago. Management says this is mainly because they are ordering more often, not because each order has become much bigger. Growth continues to come mainly from existing cities.
The Capital Intensity Gap Matters
This is where the two investment cases separate sharply. Blinkit is not an asset-light marketplace anymore. Eternal says quick commerce operates around 19 million square feet of store and warehousing space across more than 300 cities and has absorbed around Rs. 3,000 crore of capex over the past four years. Inventory ownership also pushed net working capital to Rs. 2,545 crore at the end of Q1FY27.
In Q1FY27 alone, Blinkit capex reached roughly Rs. 711 crore, materially above previous quarters, largely because of warehousing capacity additions. Quick-commerce free cash burn was around Rs. 778 crore. Eternal can afford the investment, with its quarter-end cash balance at Rs. 18,288 crore, but investors still need that capital to eventually generate attractive returns.
Lenskart’s capital intensity is different, but it is not disappearing. The company is making a large manufacturing bet through its Hyderabad facility, which is being built for around 50 million pairs annually. That means capex will remain important as Lenskart tries to bring more production in-house.
There is also a currency angle. Lenskart still has exposure to the rupee-RMB movement, particularly in frame manufacturing, and management has said some of the margin benefit from greater in-house production was being absorbed by currency depreciation. The Hyderabad investment could therefore do two things over time: support capacity growth and reduce some of that dependence on imported inputs.
That makes the comparison more balanced. Lenskart is already generating cash from its existing business, but it is still committing capital today to manufacturing expansion and lowering currency dependence. Blinkit is committing even larger amounts to stores, warehouses and inventory as it builds scale. In both cases, the investment case depends on whether today’s spending leads to stronger margins and returns later.
Valuation Leaves Very Little Room For Execution Mistakes
Both stocks are expensive, so the key question is whether earnings can grow fast enough to bring those valuations down. For Lenskart, Motilal Oswal estimates adjusted PAT rising from around Rs. 534 crore in FY26 to Rs. 899 crore in FY27 and Rs. 1,283 crore in FY28. That implies profit growth of around 69 percent in FY27 and another 43 percent in FY28. As earnings grow, its PE falls from 181 times currently to 113.1 times in FY27 and 79.3 times in FY28.
Eternal has a much sharper expected earnings jump. Motilal Oswal estimates adjusted PAT rising from around Rs. 366 crore in FY26 to Rs. 2,072 crore in FY27 and Rs. 4,143 crore in FY28. That means profit is expected to grow more than five times in FY27 and then roughly double again in FY28. As earnings scale, its PE is expected to fall sharply from 737 times currently to 125.2 times in FY27 and 62.6 times in FY28.
That creates a clearer trade-off. Eternal has the faster expected earnings growth and therefore sees its valuation multiple fall much faster. But achieving that depends heavily on Blinkit continuing to scale, margins improving and the large amount of capital being invested earning good returns. Lenskart’s earnings growth is slower, but its current profit is already more established.
The risk profiles are also different. Eternal still has to manage competition, dark-store economics, warehouse capex, working capital and continued spending on newer businesses. Lenskart faces execution risks around new stores, the Hyderabad manufacturing expansion, international growth and currency exposure, especially to the rupee-RMB movement.
The Choice Is Between Visibility And Optionality
So which has the stronger investment case? Based on the numbers today, Lenskart looks easier to understand. Revenue is growing above 30 percent, margins are improving, cash flow is supporting its expansion, and both India and international businesses are getting stronger. The valuation is still expensive, but the earnings growth needed to justify it is already starting to show.
Eternal offers more upside if Blinkit delivers. Food delivery is profitable, Blinkit is growing much faster, District is expanding and the company is building more businesses around the same customer base. If Blinkit keeps growing quickly and margins improve, Eternal’s profits could rise very fast.
That does not make Lenskart cheap or Eternal unattractive. Both stocks are priced for strong growth, but the path to justify those valuations is different. Lenskart needs to keep growing while steadily improving margins and returns. Eternal needs Blinkit’s massive scale to eventually turn into equally massive profits. At these valuations, the winner may not be the company that grows the fastest, but the one that delivers closest to what investors are already paying for.

a.title: Anushka Sen enters her beauty chapter as face of Nykaa K-Beauty
a.content:
Nykaa has consistently built its beauty universe around some of the most recognisable names in Indian entertainment from Deepika Padukone as its brand ambassador to Sharvari as a face of Nykaa and Rasha Thadani as the face of Nykaa Cosmetics. Now, adding a new dimension to that celebrity-led beauty narrative is Anushka Sen, who represents Nykaa’s K-Beauty category.
Anushka’s connection with Korea goes beyond beauty. The actor is set to make her Korean cinema debut with Jeju Olle, marking a significant new chapter in her international career. Having long been drawn to Korean culture and entertainment, her move into Korean cinema makes her association with K-Beauty feel especially organic.
For Nykaa, Anushka represents a generation that has grown up with Korean culture as part of its everyday world from K-dramas and music to skincare and beauty rituals. Her strong digital presence and Gen Z appeal further position her as a relevant voice for a category that has moved well beyond being a passing trend.
K-Beauty’s appeal today lies in its skin-first approach, emphasis on thoughtful routines and the idea that beauty is as much about care as it is about makeup. Through Nykaa, these philosophies have become increasingly accessible to Indian beauty consumers, with Korean beauty brands and innovations becoming a significant part of the platform’s offering.
Anushka’s association with Nykaa K-Beauty therefore comes at the intersection of beauty, pop culture and a growing India-Korea connection. As she prepares to enter Korean cinema, she is also becoming a face for the beauty culture that has influenced audiences worldwide.
For Nykaa, Anushka brings something distinctive to the K-Beauty conversation a young Indian star whose own journey is increasingly connected to Korea.

a.title: Lenskart shares fall 2% after Rs 2,468-crore block deal; 2.07% equity stake sold
a.content:
Shares of Lenskart Solutions fell more than 2 percent in early trade on September 21 after a large block deal worth Rs 2,468 crore took place in the eyewear retailer, marking another sizeable secondary-market transaction in the stock in recent weeks. Around 3.6 crore Lenskart shares, equivalent to 2.07 percent of the company's equity, changed hands through block deals at Rs 688 apiece.
Lenskart shares were trading at Rs 692 in early trade, down 2.2 percent for the day. Despite Monday's decline, the stock has gained 57.5 percent so far in 2026, compared with a 10.7 percent decline in the Nifty 50. The company's market capitalisation stood at around Rs 1.2 lakh crore.
The transaction came after reports that Platinum Jasmine A 2018 Trust was looking to sell shares in Lenskart. The proposed transaction had initially been pegged at around Rs 2,047.4 crore, representing about 1.7 percent of the company's equity, at a floor price of Rs 682.45 per share.
The floor price represented a 3.5 percent discount to Lenskart's previous closing price. The actual block trades on Monday were larger than the size indicated earlier, with 3.6 crore shares changing hands for Rs 2,468 crore at Rs 688 apiece. According to the earlier deal terms, shares sold through the transaction would be subject to a 90-day lock-up on any further sale of shares.
Monday's transaction follows two other large block deals in Lenskart shares in August. In late August, Alpha Wave Ventures sold 2.95 crore shares, or 1.7 percent equity, for Rs 1,857 crore at an average price of Rs 630 per share. National Pension System bought 78.57 lakh shares, or 0.45 percent equity, for Rs 495 crore in that transaction, while ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund purchased 60.3 lakh shares, equivalent to 0.35 percent equity, for Rs 380 crore. WhiteOak Capital Mutual Fund acquired another 15.87 lakh shares, or 0.1 percent equity, for Rs 100 crore.
Earlier in August, SVF II Lightbulb sold 4.5 crore Lenskart shares worth Rs 2,887.9 crore on the BSE. Societe Generale ODI bought 1.07 crore shares worth Rs 688.92 crore in the transaction, which was executed at an average price of Rs 641.75 per share.
The latest block deal also comes after Lenskart reported a sharp improvement in its first-quarter earnings. Net profit rose to Rs 222 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 60 crore a year earlier, while revenue increased 43.3 percent year-on-year to Rs 2,714.2 crore. EBITDA climbed 75.1 percent to Rs 588.5 crore, with the EBITDA margin expanding to 21.7 percent from 17.7 percent a year earlier. The company's PAT margin rose 443 basis points to 8.4 percent, while consolidated product margin crossed 70 percent for the first time, reaching 70.3 percent during the quarter.

a.title: Ronnie Screwvala’s $15 billion Lenskart call is almost there. Why brokers still see upside
a.content:
The Lenskart share price has had a dream run since its listing last November. The shares have surged over 70% since debut. With the market cap now well above $14 billion, one cannot but remember Ronnie Screwvala defending its valuation during the IPO. While the street was apprehensive about Lenskart’s IPO pricing , Screwvala famously said he will “eat his hat out” if valuations didn’t surge to “$15 billion in the next 12 months or less.”
Ronnie Screwvala before Lenskart listing
Lenskart’s valuation had raised a storm before its listing. While many market experts had called the valuations expensive, Screwvala, an entrepreneur and one of the early investors in the eye wear brand, had stated that “Peyush Bansal priced the IPO at roughly 20% below the company’s actual intrinsic value.” Elaborating on his argument, he had mentioned that “Lenskart is a very unique company. Its real strength will unfold in the months ahead. Its listing price is at $8 billion, if it does not touch $15 billion in the next 12 months or less, I’ll eat my hat.”
Lenskart: What’s driving the bullish momentum now
Interestingly, 10 months on, there are more backers to the Lenskart story. Not only has the valuation jumped from the $8 billion at listing to close to $15 billion, but the strong earnings performance is also being seen as a key game changer.
Brokerage houses have come up with reports that indicate close to 40% upside from current levels. Analysts are now seeing it as “one to keep for generations” or the “next Rayban.”
They believe that while Lenskart started its operations in 2010, the growth journey has just started and has the potential and visibility to open 10,000 stores over the next 10-15 years. According to most industry observers, “the focus on demand creation, rather than share shift from other players,” makes the stock a strong contender for exponential growth going forward.
Jefferies on Lenskart: ‘Ray-Ban of future’
International brokerage house Jefferies is betting on the strong growth & sharp margin expansion through Q1FY27. It believes that Lenskart’s premium sunglass vertical, “Meller, could be the Ray-Ban of future.”
Given that “market creation remains a top priority, with supply, rather than demand, being a key constraint in India, evidenced by 70,000 daily eye tests. The company now plays at the bottom end with a fully loaded Rs 500 product, while a clear premiumisation trend is visible,” Jefferies added.
According to them, “margin improvement in international should put a key investor concern to rest.” They have revised the price target higher to Rs 680 a share with a ‘Buy’ recommendation. This implies approximately 15% upside from current levels.
They pointed out that Lenskart is India’s largest tech-driven eyewear retailer with just 5% market share and “offers strong growth potential. Its vertically integrated omni-channel model ensures cost efficiency, rapid delivery, and superior customer experience.”
Lenskart is addressing both ends of the price spectrum, and this, they believe, gives it “strong headroom” for growth. On the one hand, the Rs 500 proposition “managed to crack the code on costing. Rs 30,000 progressive lenses,” on the other hand, “generated Rs 2.5 billion annual sales,” on the premium end of the market.
They pointed out that “superior unit economics and a faster payback period of its stores” would help higher EBITDA growth between now and FY29.
Nomura on Lenskart: ‘Keep for generations’
Nomura calls Lenskart “the one to keep for generations.”
Eyewear is a growing category in the Indian context. Nomura estimates that nearly “two-thirds of those needing correction still go without, and 60 optical stores/millon people (vs 400 for footwear) show how thinly the market is covered.”
What makes the Lenskart story striking in this context is that the company “spent a decade building what the fragmented trade could not – centralised manufacturing, remote optometry, and an asset-light store that opens almost anywhere.”
They have initiated coverage with a ‘Buy’ rating and a price target of Rs 888, implying a whopping 40% upside potential from current levels. According to them, the “proven track record looks ahead at the credible path of mapped 10,000+ stores across 6,400 pincodes, of which only 5% is walked.”
“The road further extends to international geographies (scale up in existing and entering new ones), keeping it on track to become a global leader. Above this lies the untapped pool of margin improvement through scale and better mix (progressive lenses),” the Japanese brokerage house added.
As per their estimates, Lenskart has the potential to deliver EPS growth of 49% annually on a compounded basis between FY26-FY29. The stock currently trades at 34x FY28 estimated EV/EBITDA. They believe that Lenskart is likely to maintain a long-term EBITDA margin of 25% Vs 11% in FY26.
Motilal Oswal on Lenskart: Strong moats in a difficult-to-scale category
The domestic brokerage house, Motilal Oswal believes that Lenskart “has built strong moats in a difficult-to-scale category.” They have reiterated the ‘Buy’ rating and revised the target price higher to Rs 800 a share. This implies close to 16% upside from the current market price.
They believe some of the factors that have contributed to the optimism surrounding the stock price include –
-A centralised, highly automated manufacturing facility
– Strong backward integration
– Large omnichannel presence
– Leveraging technology to ease constraints in scaling up and
-House-of-brands architecture spanning mass to premium eyewear.
According to the analysis by the brokerage house, “the stock price decomposition suggests that earnings surprises, leading to consensus estimate upgrades, along with roll-forward, have been the key drivers of stock outperformance, rather than multiple re-rating.”
Motilal Oswal analysts pointed out that “Lenskart has among the best-in-class store economics among listed retailers (10 months store payback across India and international operations).”
Moreover, they believe “the store economics has room for further improvement as newer stores hit maturity and benefits of backward integration are reflected in higher product margins (currently impeded by rupee depreciation).”
Despite operating one of the largest retail networks in India, comprising 2,725 stores, in the eyewear retail category, Motilal Oswal is betting on the company’s “large runway for store expansion.” This is primarily on the back of underpenetration and limited organised competition in the category.
Motilal Oswal anticipates that Lenskart can potentially add “over 10,000 stores over the medium term through densification in its existing footprint (1.8k+ pincodes), entry into unserved pincodes within existing cities (2.7k), and foray into new economically viable towns (3.5k+ pincodes).”
The company has been able to generate free cash flow in FY26 as well as Q1 FY27 despite the upfront capex expenses. Over FY26-FY29, Motilal Oswal expects Lenskart’s free cash flow generation to be “significant.” They estimate about “Rs 32 billion cumulative, which the company could use to fund growth through accelerated store additions and expand into new markets internationally.”
Lenskart set to move higher?
The Lenskart share valuation is inching towards the $15 billion that Screwvala had referred to while listing. The management is betting on demand, and with international profitability established and the focus is now shifting toward store additions and healthy same-store sales. While the future earnings would hold the key to long-term potential, the room for growth for the next 12 months appears to be a forgone conclusion.

a.title: Lenskart Shares Fall 2% After ₹2,468 Crore Block Deal
a.content:
Shares of eyewear retailer Lenskart Solutions slipped more than 2% in early trading on Monday after a significant block deal worth Rs 2,468 crore was executed in the company’s stock.
Around 3.6 crore shares, representing 2.07% of Lenskart’s total equity, were exchanged at Rs 688 per share.
According to a report by Moneycontrol, Lenskart shares have delivered strong returns in 2026, rising 57.5% compared with a 10.7% fall in the Nifty 50 index, despite the Monday's decline. The company’s market capitalisation stood at nearly Rs 1.2 lakh crore.
Large block deals drive investor attention
The latest transaction followed reports that Platinum Jasmine A 2018 Trust was planning to sell its stake in Lenskart. The deal was earlier estimated at Rs 2,047.4 crore, involving about 1.7% of the company’s equity at a floor price of Rs 682.45 per share.
The actual transaction exceeded the earlier estimate, with shares changing hands at Rs 688 apiece. The floor price was around 3.5% lower than Lenskart’s previous closing price. Shares sold under the arrangement were reportedly subject to a 90-day lock-in period.
The deal follows multiple large-scale share transactions in August. Alpha Wave Ventures sold 2.95 crore shares worth Rs 1,857 crore, while SVF II Lightbulb sold 4.5 crore shares valued at Rs 2,887.9 crore earlier in the month.
Strong quarterly performance supports stock
The block deal comes after Lenskart reported significant improvement in its financial performance for the first quarter of FY27. The company’s net profit increased to Rs 222 crore from Rs 60 crore in the same period last year.
Revenue grew 43.3% year-on-year to Rs 2,714.2 crore, while EBITDA rose 75.1% to Rs 588.5 crore. The EBITDA margin expanded to 21.7% from 17.7% a year earlier.
The company also reported an increase in profitability metrics, with PAT margin improving to 8.4%. Its consolidated product margin crossed the 70% mark for the first time, reaching 70.3% during the quarter.

Lenskart reported its first quarter earnings last month. Its net profit surged to ₹222 crore from ₹60 crore last year, while its revenue increased 43.3% to ₹2,714.2 crore from ₹1,894.5 crore.

a.title: Sun Pharma Launches Fashion-Inspired Alopecia Areata Awareness Campaign Featuring Designer Christian Siriano
a.content:
Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited has unveiled a new educational campaign called Regrowth Restyled, aimed at supporting adults living with severe alopecia areata.
The campaign launched during Alopecia Areata Awareness Month and takes an unconventional fashion-led approach to raising awareness of the autoimmune condition.
Sun Pharma partnered with renowned fashion designer Christian Siriano to create a one-of-a-kind wearable garment inspired by the hair regrowth journey experienced by patients.
The collaboration brought together Siriano and patient advocates to explore themes of confidence, identity, and self-expression through clothing and personal style.
People living with alopecia areata often say the condition affects far more than their physical appearance, touching deeply on their sense of self and emotional wellbeing.
A panel featuring Siriano and three members of the patient community formed a central part of the campaign’s public-facing activities and outreach efforts.
Sun Pharma’s head of marketing, Stephanie Loiseau, discussed the strategy behind the Siriano partnership and explained why pharma brands should look beyond the usual roster of celebrity spokespeople.
John Bujnoski, Vice President, Head of Dermatology and Immunology, U.S. Innovative Medicines at Sun Pharma, said: “Through this campaign, we hope to inspire confidence, celebrate self-expression, and encourage patients to speak with their dermatologist about treatment options, including LEQSELVI, that may help them achieve their hair regrowth goals.”
LEQSELVI, known generically as deuruxolitinib, is an FDA-approved medicine for adults with severe alopecia areata that works by blocking certain signals thought to play a role in hair loss.
Clinical trial data showed that around 3% of patients were able to regain almost all their hair in as little as eight weeks after beginning treatment with LEQSELVI.
By the 24-week mark in clinical trials, approximately one-third of patients had regained almost all of their hair, demonstrating the treatment’s potential for significant regrowth outcomes.
The Regrowth Restyled campaign reflects a broader shift in pharmaceutical marketing toward more human-centred storytelling that connects treatment to lived patient experience.

a.title: Lenskart Shares Slip 3% After ₹2,468 Cr Block Deal
a.content:
Lenskart Solutions fell sharply on Monday after a large block deal worth ₹2,468 crore hit the counter, dragging the stock to its day’s low.
A chunk of Lenskart’s equity changed hands through block deals on the exchange.
As many as 3.6 crore shares, or 2.07% of the company’s total equity, were traded for a combined value of ₹2,468 crore, at an average price of ₹688 per share.
The identity of the buyers and sellers has not been officially confirmed yet. However, market sources suggest the seller was Platinum Jasmine A 2018 Trust, an investment vehicle linked to the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority.
As per standard block deal norms, the seller will not be able to sell any further shares in the company for the next 90 days.
This is not an isolated event. It is actually the third such block deal in Lenskart over the past month.
On August 24, SoftBank’s Vision Fund sold close to 4.5 crore shares worth nearly ₹2,888 crore.
Then on August 28, Alpha Wave Ventures sold around 2.9 crore shares valued at roughly ₹1,857 crore, with buyers such as the National Pension System, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund and WhiteOak Capital Mutual Fund picking up stakes in that deal.
Despite the string of block deals, Lenskart’s stock has held up reasonably well over a longer stretch.
As of 10:00, the stock is trading at ₹691.25 well above its IPO issue price of ₹402 and is up close to 57% since the start of the year.
It also remains sharply higher than its listing price of ₹395 from November last year, even after today’s fall.

a.content:
Lenskart Solutions Share Price Target at Rs 850: ICICI Securities
ICICI Securities has initiated coverage on Lenskart Solutions with a BUY rating and a 12-month target of Rs 850, implying about 23 percent upside from the current price of Rs 693. Tagging it a Conviction Pick, the brokerage argues that India's largest direct-to-consumer eyewear player is riding a rare mix of a fast-widening market and a deep, self-built moat — vertical manufacturing that undercuts rivals, an AI-led omnichannel network of nearly 3,500 stores, and a house of brands. It expects consolidated revenue, operating profit and net profit to compound at 27, 37 and 59 percent a year through FY29, valuing the stock at 43 times FY28E operating profit.
Lenskart: a clear vision of growth, with the moat already in place
Vertical manufacturing that makes eyewear for a fraction of the industry's cost, a technology-led store network spanning India and Asia, and a market still barely a third penetrated — ICICI Securities begins coverage with conviction.
35-40%
Lower input costs vs the industry
50-70%
Cheaper retail vs local opticians
69%
Gross margin, FY26
1.6 crore
Annual transacting customers, FY26
A market only a third penetrated
The opportunity begins with how few Indians who need glasses actually own a proper pair. Eyeglass penetration sits at just 35 percent, against 69 percent in Japan and 88 percent in the United States — each square below is one percentage point of the Indian population.
India — 35% eyeglass penetration
The tailwinds are structural. Refractive errors are set to afflict 62 percent of Indians by FY30 — as high as 75 percent among teenagers and children — from 43 percent in FY20. As awareness rises and buyers shift to organised brands, whose share is seen climbing to 31 percent by FY30 from 22 percent in FY20, the domestic eyewear market is projected to grow at a 13 percent compound rate — roughly three times the pace of the global industry — from Rs 78,800 crore in FY25 to about Rs 1,48,300 crore by FY30. Lenskart holds only about 5 percent of it today.
The moat: making eyewear for less
Lenskart's edge is that it owns the entire chain. Its Bhiwadi facility — running at 75 percent automation — integrates procurement, lens coating, edging, cutting, polishing, assembly and dispatch, while AI-led design, remote eye-testing and an omnichannel platform speed innovation and cut cost. The result is a structural price advantage: frame and lens costs run 35 to 40 percent below the Indian industry average, letting Lenskart sell 50 to 70 percent cheaper than local opticians.
That integration is deepening. Prescription eyeglasses made at its centralised plants rose to 1.75 crore units in FY26 from 1.01 crore in FY24; in-house frames climbed to 78 lakh from 53 lakh and lenses to 56 lakh from 25 lakh. A new Hyderabad facility will add roughly 5 crore units of capacity on top of the current 2.5 crore, extending the cost advantage as volumes scale. Cheap, reliable supply has helped annual transacting customers roughly double to 1.6 crore in FY26 from 77 lakh in FY23.
A house of brands on an omnichannel net
Above the supply chain sits a multi-brand storefront, each label aimed at a different customer and occasion but sharing Lenskart's technology, sourcing and distribution.
John Jacobs
Owndays
Meller
Hooper
Vincent Chase
Le Petit Lunetier
India, about 60 percent of revenue, remains the core, with international markets — led by Japan and Southeast Asia — the other 40 percent. Ambition is scaling in step: management aims to run 10 crore eye tests a year, up from roughly 2 crore today.
From losses to compounding profit
The financial arc is the clincher. Revenue has compounded at 33 percent to Rs 8,814 crore over FY23-26, but the sharper move is in profitability: EBITDA margins have widened from 7 percent in FY23 to 19.9 percent in FY26, dragging the business from a small loss to real earnings.
Looking ahead, ICICI expects revenue, EBITDA and net profit to compound at 27, 37 and 59 percent respectively over FY26-29E, with margins reaching 25 percent and return on capital employed climbing to 28 percent. Net profit swings from a marginal loss in FY24 to about Rs 2,058 crore by FY29E, and the company is expected to throw off cumulative free cash flow of roughly Rs 5,300 crore across the period.
The target for investors
ICICI Securities initiates with a BUY and a target of Rs 850, an upside of roughly 23 percent, valuing Lenskart at 43 times FY28E operating profit. This is unambiguously a premium-multiple growth stock — it trades at around 234 times FY26 earnings, easing to about 58 times on FY29E estimates as profits compound — so the case rests on execution rather than cheapness. With the stock near its 52-week high of Rs 698 after a powerful run off the Rs 356 low, the measured approach is to accumulate on market-linked dips and hold for the multi-year penetration and margin story, rather than chase the price.
Key risks
What ICICI Securities flags
Medical advances denting demand. Improvements in medical infrastructure and vision-correction technology could, over time, reduce demand for corrective eyewear.
Innovation slowdown. Lenskart's growth leans on rapid product launches; a slower cadence of innovation or fewer launches could blunt the momentum.
Valuation sensitivity. At a rich multiple on early-stage profits, the shares leave little room for disappointment — any execution stumble or demand wobble would be felt sharply in the price. (Flagged by TopNews, given the valuation.)

Research analysts: Kaustubh Pawaskar, Abhishek Shankar and Sonal Rajpal. The Rs 850 target values the company at 43 times FY28E EV/EBITDA.

Japan-based SoftBank Group, through its affiliate SVF II Lightbulb (Cayman) Ltd, has further pared its stake in Lenskart, selling 4.5 crore equity shares across 22 tranches for a total consideration of ₹2,887.87 crore in August. a.title: Sun Pharma to Zydus: Healthcare stocks outperform broader market despite price pressure; can they sustain growth?
a.content:
Market News
6 min read | Updated on September 18, 2026, 15:57 IST
SUMMARY
Healthcare stocks have consistently outperformed the broader markets over the past months as investors focus on sectors with visible earnings potential ahead amid the geopolitical crisis.
Nifty Healthcare outperformed NIFTY50 index delivering close to 15% returns to investors in the last 6 months. | Image: Shutterstock
Indian healthcare sector stocks have significantly outperformed the broader market indices over the past few months, as investors focus on the potential for further growth despite the elevated price pressure and geopolitical supply headwinds in the market.
Companies like Sun Pharmaceuticals, Zydus Lifesciences, Laurus Labs, Aurobindo Pharma, among several other defensive healthcare stocks, have added to the gains, while the broader markets suffer from the impact of the geopolitical crisis in West Asia.
Experts predict that earnings visibility, pricing power, regulatory developments, product pipelines and valuations, among other factors, should remain in focus of investors in the healthcare sector.
While the US business remains important for pharma companies, hospitals and diagnostics firms should be analysed based on their occupancy, realisations, margins and capacity addition factor.
“We believe the market is pricing in domestic market growth and price headwinds in vanilla generics in US market, but not the rainmakers and Emerging Markets growth,” said analysts from Bernstein Research.
Saikat Kumar, Board Member of Red Lions Capital, ADGM MD & CEO, DIP Market, said that with the stock market facing macro and geopolitical volatility, investors are gravitating towards sectors with relatively visible earnings like healthcare.
“Healthcare’s relative outperformance reflects a combination of defensive characteristics, resilient earnings and improving fundamentals across hospitals, diagnostics and select pharma segments,” said Saikat Kumar.
However, Kumar also highlighted that the impact of the same is increasingly becoming differentiated across companies depending on their product mix, complex generics, speciality portfolio and new launches.
NSE data showed that the sectoral benchmark Nifty Healthcare has outperformed the benchmark NIFTY50 index, delivering close to 15% returns to investors in the last six months, while the broader index lost nearly 2% of its value in the same period.
The chart attached below further showed that on a one-year basis, Nifty Healthcare has gained almost 12% while the benchmark NIFTY50 index has lost around 8%, according to the exchange data.
Market experts predict that regulatory concerns, along with pricing pressure from the US generics market, are expected to remain key challenges for Indian healthcare companies in the upcoming period.
Despite the price pressure, the US generics import market remains a key source of revenue for Indian healthcare companies, with domestic companies exporting a major chunk of general prescription drugs and healthcare equipment to America.
“Headwinds include elevated valuations in some pockets, regulatory intervention, pricing pressure in generics and higher input or compliance costs,” said Saikat Kumar.
Investors should also know that factors like increasing patient volumes, along with the premiumisation of healthcare services, capacity expansion, and rising healthcare penetration will act as key tailwinds alongside the ability to adapt with AI and automation.
On the AI use case front, analysts from Japanese investment firm Nomura said that Lupin undertaking artificial intelligence (AI) and automation in multiple use cases and across functions is expected to drive efficiency gains and cost savings that have not been quantified at this stage.
Bernstein analysts expect AI leveraging, a lifestyle shift towards image consciousness, along with a rise in disposable income, will create around $400 billion in opportunities for the sector in the next few years.
US-based investment firm Bernstein analysts said India’s Healthcare sector has a constructive outlook for the coming years, with key focus on increasing penetration of health infrastructure in emerging economies.
Six areas including – 505(B)(2) NDAs; Orphan indications; Drug-device combinations; Drug repurposing in niche therapies, metabolic peptides, and RNA; and cellular therapies like CAR-T, will produce rainmakers for Indian biopharma.
Rainmakers are emerging catalyst sectors or business streams which have the potential to bring in higher revenues, in this case, high-growth ventures in the healthcare industry.
“We expect over the next decade these rainmakers to add $70-75 billion to Industry size and total Industry to grow by 4 times to $195 billion,” said Bernstein analysts.
Companies like Zydus, Lupin, and Sun Pharma, among others are key companies which operate in the sector.
As per the latest advisory from the Union Health Ministry, the States and Union Territories’ have been directed to oversee and ensure strict compliance on government and private clinics which are involved in stem cell research, treatment, promotion or administration.
The directive also said that the authorities will ensure strict compliance with the applicable framework governing stem cell research and therapy.
This advisory was released on September 17 in response to a Supreme Court ruling in a case which highlighted facilities which failed to comply with the standards now facing consequences, including professional misconduct.
While this move serves as a caution for unproven and experimental stem cell treatments, it also provides a push towards heavily regulated and proven therapies which are offered by several companies that have succeeded in clinical trials.
Capital markets experts predict that the longer-term outlook for the Indian healthcare sector will be supported by several factors like rising demand, increased affordability, innovation opportunities in niche therapies and complex specialities, among other things.
“The long-term case remains supported by structural under-penetration of healthcare, rising affordability, formalisation and increasing demand for quality care,” said Saikat Kumar.
The analyst said that although the sector may have support from the structural tailwinds, outperformance in the stock market will ultimately depend on company-specific earnings growth relative to valuations.
In line with expectations, Bernstein analysts also said that they have a positive sector view on the Indian healthcare sector, with a key focus on niche therapies and complex specialities, which is expected to drive Indian Biopharma’s revenue acceleration and sustainable scale-up in earnings.

a.title: Lenskart Solutions zooms 98% from November low; stock hits new high
a.content:
Lenskart Solutions zooms 98% from November low; stock hits new high
Lenskart's share price hit a new high of ₹703.85 on the BSE in Friday's trade. The stock now trades at a 75 per cent premium to its issue price of ₹402 per share.
Listen to This Article
Lenskart Solutions share price movement
Lenskart Solutions (Lenskart) share price hit a new high of ₹703.85, gaining nearly 4 per cent on the BSE in Friday’s intra-day deals in an otherwise range-bound market. The stock price of one of the leading direct-to-consumer (D2C) eyewear players in India, with presence across select international markets, surpassed its previous high of ₹703.75 touched on September 10, 2025. In comparison, the BSE Sensex was up 0.15 per cent at 74,428 at 11:40 AM.
 
In the past month, Lenskart outperformed the market by surging 12 per cent, against a 3.6 per cent decline in the BSE Sensex. The stock has nearly doubled or zoomed 98 per cent from its listing day low of ₹355.70 on the BSE. The company made its stock market debut on November 10, 2025. Currently, Lenskart quotes 75 per cent higher against its issue price of ₹402 per share.
 
Brokerages remain bullish on Lenskart
Rising prevalence of refractive errors in India, growing awareness of eyecare, and a shift to organised players will help India’s eyewear market grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 13 per cent to ₹1.48 trillion over FY25-30, expanding by 3x of the global eyewear industry. Refractive errors amongst India’s population are expected to go up to 62 per cent by FY30 (highest amongst teenagers & children at 75 per cent) from 43 per cent in FY20, according to analysts at ICICI Securities. 
Penetration level for eyeglasses in India is low at 35 per cent compared to the US and Japan at 88 per cent and 69 per cent respectively. Strong business models are aiding organised D2C players in gaining high demand through affordability, omni-channel presence and better services. Organised brand’s share is expected to move to 31 per cent by FY30 from 22 per cent in FY20. 
Also Read
Lenskart, with a strong business model, domestic manufacturing capacity of 25 million units (another 50 million unit facility will commence in Hyderabad), and an extended store network of 2,725 stores in India (as of Q1FY27), is well capitalised to grab a large share in the Indian eyewear market with a focus on growing the market share from the current 5 per cent in the coming years, the brokerage firm said.
With store additions across India/international markets expected to grow at 13 per cent CAGR, a better product mix through innovation and transacting customers growing at 22 per cent CAGR over FY26-29E, analysts at ICICI Securities expect consolidated revenue/ earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA)/profit after tax (PAT) to grow at 27 per cent/37 per cent/59 per cent CAGR over FY26-29E.
 
With strong cash generation, analysts expect Lenskart to cumulatively generate free cash flow (FCF) of ₹5,300 crore over FY26-29E. The brokerage firm initiated its coverage on Lenskart with a Buy rating and target price of ₹850 (valuing at 43x FY28E EV/EBIDTA).
Meanwhile, India’s optical retail infrastructure remains significantly underpenetrated, with management noting the country has materially fewer opticians relative to other consumer retail categories. This underpins confidence in opening thousands of additional stores over time. 
 
Lenskart’s portfolio spans products from $5 to $500, enabling broad market coverage across price points. Separately, emerging insurance-led eye-care programmes could become an incremental demand driver over time, improving affordability and increasing adoption rates, analysts at Jefferies said.
 
Further, Lenskart has built strong moats in a difficult-to-scale category through: i) a centralized, highly automated manufacturing facility; ii) strong backward integration; iii) large omnichannel presence; iv) leveraging technology to ease constraints in scaling up; and v) house-of-brands architecture spanning mass to premium eyewear, analysts at Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL) said.
The brokerage firm raised its FY27-28E consolidated pre-IND AS EBITDA by 4 per cent/8 per cent, driven by higher store additions in India and operating leverage across India and International.
 
Analysts at MOFSL model 27 per cent/46 per cent/59 per cent CAGR in revenue/pre-Ind-AS EBITDA/adjusted PAT over FY26-29E, driven by 29 per cent/25 per cent revenue CAGR in India/International. The brokerage firm expects pre-IND AS EBITDA margin to expand to 19.4 per cent/13.5 per cent in India/International by FY29. Cyient Schedules Analyst and Investor Meeting for September 22
Cyient is scheduled to engage with analysts and institutional investors on September 22, 2026, to discuss business strategies and performance. In its latest Q1 FY27 results, the company displayed strong margin resilience, with its core DET normalized EBIT margin expanding to 13.2% (up 114 basis points YoY), despite a minor revenue degrowth of 0.9% YoY in constant currency. These upcoming meetings provide a key platform for management to discuss growth scaling in its semiconductor segment and updates on capital allocation strategies.
Market snapshot: Cyient Limited has announced its participation in analyst and investor meetings scheduled for September 22, 2026. The engagement will allow the company's senior leadership, including Executive Vice Chairman Krishna Bodanapu and Chief Financial Officer Shrinivas Kulkarni, to interact with institutional investors. These interactions come on the heels of Cyient's resilient Q1 FY27 profitability performance, which was marked by notable margin expansion in its core Digital Engineering and Technology (DET) business despite soft top-line growth.
Data Snapshot
- The Digital, Engineering, and Technology (DET) segment recorded an operating revenue of ₹1,540 crore in the first quarter of the fiscal year 2027, growing 10.6% year-on-year.
- The core DET segment's normalized EBIT margin expanded to 13.2% in Q1 FY27, representing a year-on-year expansion of 114 basis points.
- The company successfully completed a fundraise for Cyient Semiconductors Private Limited with EAAA India Alternatives Limited, valuing the subsidiary at a post-money valuation of $500 million.
- The group's design-led manufacturing subsidiary, Cyient DLM, recorded its highest-ever order book of ₹2,598.9 crore in Q1 FY27.
What's Changed
- The core Digital Engineering & Technology (DET) segment's normalized EBIT margin expanded by 114 basis points year-on-year to 13.2% from 12.1% in Q1 FY26, driven by optimized cost discipline.
- Cyient DLM's order backlog reached a historic high of ₹2,598.9 crore, up sequentially from ₹2,416.6 crore in Q4 FY26, highlighting strong mid-term visibility.
- Cyient Semiconductors completed a strategic fundraise with EAAA India Alternatives, which set a post-money valuation of $500 million for the subsidiary, facilitating capital injection to scale its operations.
Key Takeaways
- Cyient's senior management will interact directly with analysts and institutional investors on September 22, 2026, offering clarity on mid-term strategies and performance.
- The company's core DET business continues to face short-term revenue growth headwinds, with constant currency revenue contracting slightly by 0.9% year-on-year.
- Operating margins have proved highly resilient, with sequential improvements of 79 basis points and year-on-year growth of 114 basis points to hit 13.2% in Q1 FY27.
- The semiconductor business and the DLM manufacturing subsidiary (order book of ₹2,598.9 crore) represent key growth engines that are expanding faster than the traditional engineering segments.
SAHI Perspective
The upcoming analyst meeting on September 22, 2026, provides Cyient's management with a critical opportunity to rebuild investor trust regarding its top-line recovery timeline. While the core DET business has shown admirable cost control and margin expansion to 13.2%, the persistent softness in traditional engineering verticals remains a concern for valuation multiples. Investors should look for updates on the integration of Kinetic Technologies and whether the deferred EBIT margin target of 15% remains on track for H1 FY28. Direct discussions on capital allocation, particularly regarding the execution of its share buyback, will also be pivotal.
Market Implications
The direct engagement with long-term institutional investors is expected to reinforce structural support for the stock, particularly as the IT-services index faces volatile global demand. While the market has responded cautiously to Cyient's deferred profitability targets, clarity on semiconductor scaling and the utilization of the $500 million valuation milestone could catalyze positive sentiment. Over the medium term, execution of the record ₹2,598.9 crore order book at Cyient DLM and stabilization of the core DET revenue growth will be the primary drivers of stock rerating.

Cyient's scheduled meetings at the JP Morgan Investor Meetings on September 22 and Anand Rathi G-200 Summit on September 21-22 will provide platforms to highlight its Q1 FY27 normalized EBIT margin expansion to 13.2% (up 114 bps YoY), despite a flat constant currency revenue decline of 0.9% YoY in the core DET segment.

- Management commentary on the timeline for achieving the 15% EBIT margin target (currently deferred to H1 FY28).
- Growth progress in the newly acquired Kinetic Technologies and the Cyient Semiconductors segment (valued post-money at $500 million).
- Consolidated revenue recovery across key segments like energy and aerospace.
Time Horizon: Near-term (0-3 months)
Industry Context
The engineering research and development (ER&D) sector is undergoing a transition, where traditional connectivity and industrial projects are seeing localized delays due to global macroeconomic uncertainties. In this environment, Indian service providers are shifting focus toward high-margin niches. Cyient's strategic focus on semiconductors, lifecycle engineering, and artificial intelligence mirrors this industry-wide pivot. The successful fundraising at a post-money valuation of $500 million for its semiconductor arm reflects the strong appetite among institutional investors for specialized chip design and fabrication-linked services.
Key Risks to Watch
- Decision-making and project execution delays in traditional segments like energy and connectivity, which could drag down core DET revenue growth.
- Operational integration risks associated with the recent acquisition of Kinetic Technologies and the execution ramp-up of the semiconductor business.
- Execution timelines of Cyient DLM's large order book (₹2,598.9 crore) amid global supply chain and inventory bottlenecks.
Recent Developments
On September 17, 2026, Cyient confirmed its scheduled participation in the JP Morgan Investor Meetings on September 22, 2026, in Mumbai, with Executive Vice Chairman Krishna Bodanapu and CFO Shrinivas Kulkarni representing the firm. Additionally, on September 16, 2026, the company disclosed that Chief Financial Officer Shrinivas Kulkarni will attend the Anand Rathi G-200 Summit on September 21-22, 2026, in Mumbai. Cyient also hosted its Investor Day 2026 on August 25, 2026, showcasing detailed capital allocation strategies and deep-dives into its three core growth engines.
Closing Insight
While Cyient continues to optimize its cost efficiency to produce resilient operating margins, reviving top-line growth in its core digital engineering business remains the key puzzle. The upcoming institutional interactions offer a platform to articulate how its high-value semiconductor and manufacturing divisions will act as compounding value engines over the coming fiscal years.

a.title: FTSE September rebalance takes effect tomorrow: Meesho and Lenskart lead inflows, Biocon and Wipro see outflows
a.content:
FTSE Russell's September semi-annual rebalance of its global equity indices takes effect this week, and it forces the funds that track those indices to reshuffle their holdings in lockstep. The passive trades cluster around Friday's close, with the changes effective from the following Monday's open. Brokerage Nuvama has put out stock-wise estimates of how much money is likely to flow into and out of Indian names, and the list has a clear character.
The inflows are dominated by the new-age listings of the past year. On Nuvama's estimates, Meesho leads with an expected inflow of around $81 million as its index weight rises, followed by Lenskart at about $76 million and Groww's parent Billionbrains Garage Ventures at roughly $59 million. Among the large-caps getting a weight increase, Infosys is set for about $60 million and Bharti Airtel around $58 million. The bigger cluster of activity, though, is in fresh additions to the index, led by Cupid at about $52 million, with Urban Company near $38 million, Pine Labs around $34 million, Anthem Biosciences about $32 million and ACME Solar near $28 million also joining. For scale, the top inflow of roughly $81 million is in the region of ₹775 crore of passive buying concentrated into one name.
On the other side, the heaviest estimated outflows fall on Biocon, facing about $18 million of selling as its weight drops, and Wipro at around $13 million. Aadhar Housing Finance, Star Health, Metro Brands and TVS Holdings are also among the weight reductions. The outright deletions carry a recognisable theme, with a set of consumer and footwear names leaving. Whirlpool of India, Bata India and Relaxo Footwears are dropping out at the All-World level, while Route Mobile, Rajesh Exports and Orient Cement exit at the All-Cap level.
The number a casual reader tends to fixate on is the dollar flow, and that is the wrong one to lead with. What actually determines how much a stock moves is the size of the flow relative to how much the stock normally trades. Nuvama captures this with an impact measure showing how many days of average volume each flow represents, and on that lens the standout is SKF India, where an inflow of around $23 million works out to roughly 14 days of average trading volume. That is a mid-sized dollar figure with an outsized footprint, the kind of setup where a passive buy can move the price far more than the headline number suggests. The same effect, to a lesser degree, shows up in names like Emcure Pharmaceuticals, Anthem Biosciences and Central Bank of India on the buy side, and Star Health, Metro Brands and TVS Holdings on the sell side, all of which carry flows worth several days of normal volume. By contrast, the large flows into Infosys and Bharti Airtel amount to less than half a day of their trading, so despite the big dollar tags they are absorbed with barely a ripple.
A few caveats are worth keeping in mind. These are estimates, and the actual money that moves depends on how much passive capital tracks each FTSE index and on the final constituent list. Prices also tend to adjust before the event itself, as active traders position ahead of the known passive buying and selling, so some of the impact may already be in the price by the time Friday's close arrives. The cleaner takeaway is directional: the new-age listings are graduating into global index portfolios, an older set of consumer names is on the way out, and the sharpest single-stock moves are most likely where the flow is large against thin liquidity rather than where the dollar number is biggest.

a.title: Sun Pharma and Christian Siriano Launch "Regrowth Restyled" to Inspire Adults Living with Severe Alopecia Areata
a.content:
New awareness campaign celebrates confidence and self-expression through fashion while encouraging adults with severe alopecia areata to learn more about treatment options such as LEQSELVI® (deuruxolitinib)
PRINCETON, N.J., Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited (Reuters: SUN.BO, Bloomberg: SUNP IN, NSE: SUNPHARMA, BSE: 524715, "Sun Pharma" and includes its subsidiaries and/or associate companies) announced the launch of Regrowth Restyled, an educational campaign that celebrates how beauty, confidence, and self-expression continue throughout the hair regrowth journey for adults living with severe alopecia areata.
Kicking off in Alopecia Areata Awareness Month, this fashion-inspired campaign spotlights the experience of severe alopecia areata patients. As part of this collaboration, Sun Pharma has partnered with renowned fashion designer Christian Siriano to create a one-of-a-kind wearable garment inspired by the journey of hair regrowth. The piece will debut following New York Fashion Week on September 17, 2026.
"As a designer, I've always believed style is a form of self-expression – and for adults living with severe alopecia areata, hair loss can complicate that expression in ways that go far beyond appearance," said Siriano. "I'm excited to participate in this campaign because it creates a platform to broaden the conversation around alopecia areata and reminds anyone navigating this condition that self-expression is uniquely theirs and does not have to wait."
Alopecia areata is an autoimmune disease where the body's immune system mistakenly attacks hair follicles, causing hair loss. Hair may fall out in small, round patches, or in some cases, patients can lose all of their hair on their scalp and/or body. Impacting an estimated 300,000 U.S. adults, severe alopecia areata causes more than hair loss; it also carries a significant physical and psychosocial burden for patients. Alopecia areata can negatively change how patients feel about themselves, potentially leading to increased anxiety, depression, feelings of isolation, and reduced self-esteem.
"When people think about alopecia areata, they often focus on hair loss itself," said dermatologist Dr. Meena Singh, Board Certified Dermatologist and Dermatologic Surgeon, Skin and Hair Center in Overland Park, KS. "But as dermatologists, we consider the full spectrum of each patient's journey from initial hair loss to the psychological impacts alopecia areata can bring leading to a decision to explore treatment to address rapid hair regrowth."
Treating severe alopecia areata can look different for everyone. For people interested in regrowing their hair, fast results matter. Seeing bald patches shrink or new hair growth appear may help patients feel more comfortable in their journey and inspire them to take steps toward reclaiming their identity.
"Regrowth Restyled reflects our commitment to supporting people living with severe alopecia areata at every stage of their journey," said John Bujnoski, Vice President, Head of Dermatology & Immunology, U.S. Innovative Medicines, Sun Pharma. "Through this campaign, we hope to inspire confidence, celebrate self-expression, and encourage patients to speak with their dermatologist about treatment options, including LEQSELVI, that may help them achieve their hair regrowth goals."
LEQSELVI® (deuruxolitinib) is an FDA-approved medicine for adults with severe alopecia areata. It works by blocking certain signals in the body that are thought to play a role in hair loss. In clinical trials, LEQSELVI demonstrated rapid results. Some patients (3%) were able to get almost all their hair back as fast as 8 weeks. By 24 weeks, about one-third of patients regained almost all their hair. Even if some patients didn't regrow most of their hair, many still experienced visible regrowth.
LEQSELVI may cause serious side effects including infections, cancer, immune system problems, blood clots, and stomach tears. Do not take LEQSELVI if you are a poor metabolizer of CYP2C9 medicines or if you take moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitor medicines. The most common adverse events were headache, acne, nasopharyngitis, blood creatine phosphokinase increased, and hyperlipidemia. Please full Prescribing Information, including Boxed Warning and Medication Guide, and see below for Important Safety Information.
Visit RegrowthRestyled.com to learn more about the campaign and LEQSELVI as a treatment option.
About LEQSELVI®
LEQSELVI (deuruxolitinib) 8 mg tablets is an oral selective inhibitor of Janus kinases JAK1 and JAK2 FDA-approved for the treatment of adults with severe alopecia areata. Alopecia areata is an autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks hair follicles, resulting in partial or complete loss of hair on the scalp and body. Alopecia areata may affect up to 2.5% of the United States and global population during their lifetime. The scalp is the most commonly affected area, but any hair-bearing site can be affected alone or together with the scalp. Onset of the disease can occur throughout life and affects both women and men. Alopecia areata can be associated with serious psychological consequences, including anxiety and depression. There are currently limited approved treatment options available for severe alopecia areata.
Please click here for full Prescribing Information Including BOXED WARNING and Medication Guide.
LEQSELVI Important Safety Information & Use
What is LEQSELVI (deuruxolitinib)?
LEQSELVI is used to treat adults with severe hair loss (alopecia areata).
It is not known if LEQSELVI is safe and effective in children.
Who should not take LEQSELVI?
Do not take LEQSELVI if you are a poor metabolizer of CYP2C9 medicines or are taking moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitors. Before starting treatment, your healthcare provider should test you for CYP2C9 variants.  Tell your healthcare provider if you take moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitor medicines. Ask your healthcare provider or pharmacist if you are not sure. 
What is the most important safety information I should know about LEQSELVI?
LEQSELVI is a medicine that affects your immune system and can lower the ability of your immune system to fight infections. Some people have had serious infections during treatment with LEQSELVI. Some people may die from these infections... Your healthcare provider should test you for TB before starting treatment with LEQSELVI and should watch you closely for signs and symptoms of TB during treatment. You should not start taking LEQSELVI if you have any kind of infection unless your healthcare provider tells you it is okay
There may be an increased risk of major cardiovascular events in people 50 years of age and older who have at least one heart disease risk factor and are taking a medicine in the class of medicines called JAK inhibitors, especially if they are a current or past smoker.
LEQSELVI may increase your risk of certain cancers by changing the way your immune system works.
Blood clots in the veins of your legs, lungs or brain (cerebral venous sinus thrombosis, CVT) can happen in some people during treatment with LEQSELVI. These may be life-threatening.
Some people taking LEQSELVI can get tears in their stomach or intestines.
If you have diabetes, your healthcare provider may instruct you to check your blook sugar levels more often during treatment with LEQSELVI. Call your healthcare provider if you have any problems with low blood sugar (hypoglycemia).
Before you start and taking LEQSELVI and during treatment, your healthcare provider should do blood tests to check for increased fat levels in your blood, Low white and/or red blood cell counts. You should not take LEQSELVI if your white blood cell or red blood cell counts are too low.
What should I tell my healthcare provider before starting LEQSELVI?
Tell your healthcare provider if you have an infection; are a current or past smoker; have had a heart attack, or other heart problems or stroke; have had blood clots in your legs, lungs or brain; have kidney problems; have liver problems; have any stomach area (abdominal) pain or been diagnosed with diverticulitis or ulcers in your stomach or intestine; have low red or white blood cell counts; or have recently received or are scheduled to receive a vaccine. 
Females who are able to become pregnant should use effective birth control (contraception) during treatment with LEQSELVI. Talk to your healthcare provider if you are planning to become pregnant. You should not breastfeed during treatment with LEQSELVI and for one day after the last dose.
What else should I be aware of when taking LEQSELVI?
Your healthcare provider should do blood tests before you start taking LEQSELVI and during treatment to check for increased fat (lipid) levels in your blood (triglycerides and cholesterol), low red blood cell counts, or low white blood cells.
How should I take LEQSELVI?
Take LEQSELVI 2 times a day with or without food.

a.title: Lenskart: Jefferies hosts Peyush Bansal, who says eyewear penetration leaves a long runway
a.content:
Jefferies has published notes from a fireside chat with Lenskart founder Peyush Bansal, in which he framed the company's opportunity around how few Indians currently buy corrective eyewear.
- Brokerage: Jefferies
- Format: Fireside chat, no target price stated
- Last close: Rs 680 (September 16)
The core framing
Bansal described the company's vision as simple: solve vision correction at scale. With eyewear penetration still low, he sees a long runway ahead.
That is the whole growth argument in one line. In a category where most of the addressable population has never bought the product, growth comes from converting non-consumers rather than from taking share — a materially easier position than competing for an existing market.
The moats
Bansal rested them on three things: customer obsession, technology, and full-stack control.
The third is the one specific to this business. Lenskart manufactures, distributes and retails its own product, which means margin that would otherwise be shared across a supply chain stays inside the company — and pricing can be set without a wholesaler's markup in between.
International and margins
The international business is described as net additive, with cross-learnings flowing between markets. Focus remains on rapid expansion, with margins expected to follow scale.
That last phrase is the one to hold onto. It places margin improvement after growth rather than alongside it, which is a choice about sequencing that investors will be asked to fund in the meantime.

- Operational efficiencies are set to improve with a dedicated field force and innovative distribution models targeting over 150,000 healthcare professionals across India.
Novartis India Limited (NSE: NOVARTIND) is laying out a comprehensive strategy aimed at revitalizing its presence in the pharmaceutical market. Recently shared during an investor presentation, the company's leadership discussed avenues for growth amidst a competitive landscape and evolving market demands.
Company and Market Overview
With a legacy spanning over 79 years, Novartis India has become an established name in the pharmaceutical industry, having been publicly listed for 27 years. The company has strategically positioned itself within the Indian pharmaceutical market, leveraging a deep-rooted brand portfolio that includes six flagship products generating revenues exceeding ₹30 crore. Amidst these dynamics, Novartis India reports a revenue decline of 2% for FY23, with a projected compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of -2% through FY26.
Business Strategy Focus
The company outlined a clear strategic playbook focused on compounding equity and expansion across key therapeutic areas, including cardiology and neurology. This includes an enhanced specialist engagement approach, where Novartis plans to deploy over 900 field representatives to interact with around 150,000 healthcare professionals nationwide. The intent is to capture greater market share and improve brand recall among prescribers, a segment significantly affected by historical outsourcing and marketing strategies.
Recent M&A Developments
Novartis India's acquisition of the rights to the 'Minipress' brand represents a pivotal move aimed at augmenting its portfolio in the cardiac treatment domain. This deal, valued at ₹1,250 crore, is anticipated to impact the company's growth trajectory positively as Minipress has historically been a market leader, showcasing a consistent revenue growth rate. Such investments are a part of Novartis' strategy to fill in gaps and expand presence in high-value therapeutic segments.
Flagship Brands and Market Leadership
Novartis India boasts an impressive roster of top-selling products, including Voveran® and Calcium-Sandoz®, contributing significantly to an RPM exceeding ₹2,010 crore. Notably, products like Methergin® and Myfortic® continue to lead their categories, reflecting the company's enduring prescriber loyalty and brand equity. However, the lack of an in-house sales force has been identified as a challenge, with plans to rectify this by re-establishing direct field promotion to revitalize brand engagement.
Strong Governance and Future Outlook
With an experienced board and a governance framework emphasizing compliance and strategic oversight, Novartis India aims to navigate regulatory demands effectively. The company remains focused on disciplined capital allocation, ensuring investments are targeted towards high-return growth opportunities. As operational efficiencies improve through an asset-light model and robust supply chain management, Novartis India is well-poised to capitalize on emerging market opportunities.
Conclusion on Future Growth
Overall, Novartis India presented a multidimensional approach to future growth, with strategies rooted in strong product positioning and enhanced market engagement. While facing financial headwinds illustrated by past revenue declines, the commitment to revamp its operating strategies and expand through M&A indicates a positive outlook for stakeholders and investors alike.

A: Novartis India recently acquired the rights to the 'Minipress' brand for ₹1,250 crore, a strategic move to bolster its offerings in the cardiac medication market and achieve an enhanced market share.

A: To counter past revenue declines, Novartis India is implementing a direct sales force model, transitioning from outsourced partnerships to in-house promotions aimed at reactivating brand loyalty and expanding market coverage.

a.title: Novartis India targets revenue doubling in four years after key acquisitions
a.content:
Novartis India targets revenue doubling in four years after key acquisitions
- Novartis India aims to double its ₹650 crore annualized run rate within four to five years
- Acquired Minipress XL trademark from Pfizer for ₹1,250 crore; brand holds >50% market share
- In-licensed ophthalmology portfolio (Pagenax, Accentrix) worth >₹100 crore for ₹10 crore upfront fee
- Quarterly costs to rise to ₹40-50 crore from legacy ₹10-15 crore due to commercial reset
- ChrysCapital holds 70.68% stake; new management focuses on six anchor therapy areas
*this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only.
Novartis India outlined a strategy to double its annualized run rate of ₹650 crore within four to five years, driven by recent acquisitions and a commercial reset. The company acquired the Minipress XL trademark from Pfizer and in-licensed ophthalmology brands to expand its portfolio.
Strategic Shift and Acquisitions
Management announced a shift from a flat revenue trajectory to a growth-focused model centered on six anchor therapy areas: cardiology, pain management, women's health, CNS, transplant, and ophthalmology. To support this, the company is building a direct sales force covering approximately 150,000 healthcare practitioners and expanding its distribution network from four cash-and-carry forwarders (C&Fs) to nearly 25.
The most significant recent move was the acquisition of the Minipress XL trademark from Pfizer Inc. Minipress XL holds over 50% market share in the alpha-blocker segment, with reported MAT July '26 revenue of ₹228 crore. The brand has grown at a CAGR of 6.5%, lagging the broader market growth of 9-10%. Management expects an initial EBITDA of roughly ₹90 crore from this asset against an investment of ₹1,250 crore, targeting a payback period of eight to nine years post-synergies.
Additionally, the company in-licensed the ophthalmology portfolio comprising Pagenax and Accentrix from NHPL for an upfront fee of ₹10 crore. This portfolio contributes over ₹100 crore in revenue, providing a platform for further expansion in eye care.
Financial Outlook and Costs
The transition involves significant near-term costs. Quarterly operating expenses are expected to rise from a legacy run rate of ₹10-15 crore to ₹40-50 crore as the company builds its team and marketing infrastructure. Management anticipates these costs will be fully reflected from Q4 onwards, with the sales engine operational by December. Consequently, short-term profitability may dip before recovering, with margins expected to return to above 20% within two to three years.
What the Numbers Show
The acquisition of Minipress XL highlights a strategic focus on high-return, established assets rather than greenfield development. With an implied entry multiple of roughly 14x EBITDA (₹1,250 crore investment vs ₹90 crore EBITDA), the return profile relies heavily on execution-driven margin expansion and volume growth exceeding the current 6.5% CAGR to meet the targeted eight-to-nine-year payback period.
Governance and Ownership
ChrysCapital holds a 70.68% stake in the company following an open offer priced at ₹860.64 per share. The new board includes independent directors with extensive industry experience, such as Ramesh (ex-MD 3M India), Suchita Sharma, and Shashank Sinha (ex-MD Strides Pharma). Management confirmed that trademarks for core brands like Voveran and Methergin have been assigned to the company, while Sandoz brands remain under long-term licensing agreements without future royalties.
