a.title: Alpha Wave offers $137 mn Lenskart stake as investor exits gather pace
a.content:
Lenskart Solutions Ltd’s secondary share sales show no signs of slowing, with Alpha Wave Global becoming the latest investor to offer to sell shares worth up to ₹1,313 crore ($137 million) on Friday, 28 August, according to a term sheet seen by Mint.
The New York-based asset manager is offering up to 20.8 million shares, or 1.2% of Lenskart’s outstanding equity, through Alpha Wave Ventures II LP. The floor price is ₹630 per share, a 1.7% discount to Lenskart’s closing price of ₹640.60 on the National Stock Exchange on Thursday. The sale is subject to a 45-day lock-in period for the seller.
Spark Institutional Equities Pvt. Ltd, a subsidiary of Mizuho-backed Avendus Capital Pvt, and Kotak Securities Ltd are the joint bookrunners and brokers.
Alpha Wave Ventures II LP, a private growth and venture fund launched in September 2021, is selling its entire stake in Lenskart through the deal. Alpha Wave, which focuses on growth-stage companies, will continue to hold a 3.4% stake through another fund, Alpha Wave Ventures LP. Both funds are listed as public shareholders of the company.
Alpha Wave (formerly Falcon Edge Capital) invested in Peyush Bansal's eyewear retailer with Temasek in July 2021, leading a $220 million funding round that valued the firm at $2.5 billion.
More investors cash out
The proposed sale is the latest in a series of secondary transactions by existing Lenskart investors. On 25 August, Masayoshi Son’s SoftBank sold shares worth ₹2,888 crore, two months after offloading ₹2,873 crore worth of shares in the firm. In July, Singapore sovereign wealth fund Temasek sold a 2% stake worth an estimated ₹1,940 crore, following a ₹1,944-crore secondary sale by Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth fund.
Earlier, multiple block deals on 8 May saw investors, including TR Capital, KKR-backed Birdseye View Holdings, Alpha Wave Ventures and ABG Capital, divest a combined 6.46% stake for ₹5,314 crore at ₹473.4 per share.
The May transactions followed the expiry of the six-month shareholder lock-in after Lenskart’s public listing. According to Nuvama Alternative & Quantitative Research, the expiry made nearly 1.05 billion shares eligible for trading, equivalent to around 60% of Lenskart’s outstanding equity and valued at about ₹51,573 crore based on the 7 May closing price.
The share sale also comes at a time when Lenskart's stock is trading at record highs.
The company reported a 273% year-on-year jump in net profit to ₹228 crore for the quarter ended June. Revenue from operations rose 43.3% to ₹2,714.18 crore, while international revenue increased 38% to ₹1,203 crore.
Lenskart has also announced the incorporation of a new step-down subsidiary in China to focus on the eyewear and allied optical products business.

a.title: Internet stocks look expensive, but Nykaa and Lenskart remain long-term bets: Mayuresh Joshi
a.content:
India’s new-age internet stocks may no longer qualify as bargain buys, but the sector’s long-term growth case remains firmly intact, according to Mayuresh Joshi, Head of Equity Research at William O’Neil India. Even as valuations across the space turn expensive after a sharp rally, Joshi believes select names such as Fsn E-Commerce Ventures Ltd (Nykaa) and Lenskart Solutions Ltd still merit a place in portfolios because of their earnings profile, scale potential and expanding digital footprint.
Rich valuations, but a structural story
Joshi struck a note of caution on near-term pricing, saying the broader internet pack is “richly valued as we speak.” That assessment comes amid strong moves in counters such as Paytm, Lenskart, Nykaa and PB Fintech, reflecting renewed investor appetite for platform-led consumer businesses.
Yet his broader message was not bearish. Instead, he argued that the sector is likely to command a “lion’s share over the next decade,” with a handful of companies becoming significantly larger as consumption patterns evolve and India’s demographic shifts deepen the market for digital-first brands.
Why Nykaa and Lenskart stand out
Within that universe, Joshi identified Nykaa and Lenskart as continuing portfolio holdings. “Lenskart and Nykaa is something that we continue holding in our portfolio,” he said, while clarifying that these positions were accumulated “at way lower levels.”
The rationale, he suggested, lies in the quality of recent numbers and the scale of the opportunity ahead. He pointed to the “kind of numbers that they have posted,” alongside the “addressable market size, the TAM as we call it,” as key reasons these businesses remain compelling despite elevated valuations.
Digital footprint drives earnings leverage
A central part of the investment case is operating leverage. Joshi argued that as these companies deepen their digital footprint, operating costs remain relatively contained, allowing earnings growth to accelerate faster than revenue over time.
That is a crucial distinction in a market that has become more selective on profitability after years of rewarding growth at any cost. For investors, the takeaway is that scale alone is no longer enough; the market is increasingly backing internet businesses that can convert reach into margins.
Targets signal selective optimism
Joshi’s stance captures the balancing act now defining the internet theme: expensive on conventional valuation metrics, but still attractive for investors willing to back category leaders with long runways. His stated targets stand at 710 for Lenskart and around 350 for Nykaa.
The broader backdrop also supports that selective approach. In a market where Joshi has repeatedly emphasised earnings over market-cap labels, internet names that combine growth, profitability potential and large total addressable markets appear to be earning a premium — and, in some cases, justifying it.

a.title: Nykaa expands luxury retail footprint with new Luxe outlet in New Delhi
a.content:
Nykaa has opened a 5,500 sq. ft. Nykaa Luxe store at Ambience Mall, Vasant Kunj, New Delhi, expanding its luxury beauty retail footprint in India. The outlet brings together premium and prestige beauty brands across makeup, skincare, haircare, fragrance and wellness, alongside experiential services including makeovers, consultations, gifting and fragrance discovery.
The new store features more than 10 dedicated shop-in-shop formats from brands including Chanel, Yves Saint Laurent, Charlotte Tilbury, M.A.C, Estée Lauder, Lancôme and Kiehl’s. The launch follows Nykaa’s recent opening of Charlotte Tilbury’s flagship Beauty Wonderland at Nexus Select Citywalk and a second Charlotte Tilbury boutique in Noida, reflecting the company’s continued focus on premium beauty retail as India’s beauty and personal care market expands.
The store further brings Nykaa’s beauty expertise to the physical retail experience through a suite of experiential touchpoints. The Beauty Studio offers makeovers and skin consultations led by expert beauty advisors, while Consultation Hubs enable guided product discovery and hands-on experimentation. Personalised services including gifting and engraving add another layer to the experience, while a dedicated Fragrance Finder helps consumers navigate the fragrance category and discover scents suited to their preferences.
The assortment spans multiple dimensions of premium beauty, reflecting the increasingly diverse ways in which consumers discover and engage with the category. The makeup edit features sought-after brands including Rare Beauty, Huda Beauty, Kylie Cosmetics, Benefit Cosmetics, Anastasia Beverly Hills, e.l.f. Cosmetics, NARS, Urban Decay, Milk Makeup, NYX Professional Makeup, Bobbi Brown and Too Faced.
The store also brings together an expansive Korean and Japanese beauty edit featuring Laneige, SK-II, Sulwhasoo, Anua, Celimax, Numbuzin, Tonymoly, Beauty of Joseon, The Face Shop, Biodance and Innisfree. The derma-focused assortment includes La Roche-Posay, CeraVe, Eucerin, ISDIN and Aestura, alongside global skincare names such as Dermalogica, Murad, Pixi, The Ordinary, Clarins, Shiseido and Kama Ayurveda. The hair and styling edit features Kérastase, Redken, L’Oréal Professionnel, Olaplex, Dyson, Good Hair Day, indē wild, OUAI and Aveda, while the fragrance offering includes Tom Ford, Jo Malone London, Carolina Herrera, Paco Rabanne, Bvlgari, Prada, Versace, Armani, Jean Paul Gaultier, Maison Margiela and Sol de Janeiro.
The new Nykaa Luxe store opening builds on a broader expansion of Nykaa’s luxury retail footprint in India. Earlier this year, the company opened Charlotte Tilbury’s first flagship Beauty Wonderland in India at Nexus Select Citywalk, followed by a second Charlotte Tilbury boutique at Mall of India, Noida.
Both stores were built and operated end-to-end by Nykaa, spanning retail operations, staffing, merchandising, supply chain and brand management. Together with the new Nykaa Luxe destination, these investments demonstrate Nykaa’s continued focus on creating differentiated luxury beauty experiences while strengthening its presence in one of India’s key premium consumption markets.
Anchit Nayar, Executive Director and CEO, Nykaa Beauty, said: “The opportunity in premium beauty is not simply about offering more products; it is about creating a more sophisticated beauty ecosystem around the consumer. As discovery becomes increasingly digital, physical retail has an opportunity to become more experiential, more expert-led and more personal. Our role is to make premium beauty not just more accessible, but also more discoverable and easier to navigate for the Indian consumer.
“Delhi has been an important market in this evolution, which is why we have continued to invest in differentiated luxury formats here. With our newNykaa Luxe store at Ambience Mall, Vasant Kunj, we are bringing together the breadth of our assortment, our partnerships with leading global brands and the expertise of our teams to create a destination that reflects where beauty in India is headed. We are grateful to our brand partners and the Ambience Group for partnering with us in bringing this vision to life,” Nayar added.

a.title: Nykaa Now puts beauty emergencies in the fast lane with Sharvari-led campaign

a.title: SoftBank Sells 2.59% Stake in Lenskart for ₹2,888 Crore via Block Deal
a.content:
It is a technology driven eyewear company in the design, manufacturing, branding and retail of eyewear products, with operations in India, Japan, Southeast Asia and the Middle East.
The shares of Lenskart Solutions are currently trading at a market price of Rs. 656 up by 1.31%. The market capitalization of the company in the stock market is Rs.1,13,829 crore. The company's stock's 52 week high is Rs. 673.90 and its 52 week low is Rs. 356.10. The P/E Ratio is 168.45 times.
What's The News
The shares were sold by SVF II Lightbulb (Cayman) Limited, an investment affiliate of Japan's SoftBank Group and one of Lenskart's earliest institutional backers. Unlike a promoter transaction, the disclosure filing itself confirms that SVF II Lightbulb does not belong to Lenskart's promoter or promoter group it is a public/institutional shareholder that retained a large stake following the company's IPO.
The company sold off 4.5 crore equity shares of Lenskart Solutions Limited, representing about a 2.59% stake. Following the sale, its stake has declined from 9.86% to 7.27%. Market reports put the average sale price at around Rs. 641.75 per share, a discount to the previous close, bringing the overall deal size to Rs. 2,888 crore. The shares were taken by a wide base of domestic and global institutional buyers, reportedly including Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, Vanguard and Societe Generale, among others.
Stake Sale Details
Before the sale, SVF II Lightbulb (Cayman) Limited held 17,14,11,974 shares, which was 9.86% stake in Lenskart's total voting capital. With the sale of 4.5 crore shares, its holding has been reduced to 12,64,11,974 shares, that is 7.27% of the total. The mode of sale was disclosed as "open market," and Lenskart's total equity/voting share capital remained unchanged at 1,73,93,06,168 shares, both before and after the transaction confirming this was a secondary sale of existing shares rather than a fresh issuance by the company.
Impact On SoftBank's Holding
This is not SoftBank's first trim of its Lenskart position this year. In June 2026, SVF II Lightbulb had already sold a 3.25% stake for around Rs. 2,873 crore, cutting its holding from about 13.13% to roughly 9.86–9.88%. Taken together, the two sales have reduced SoftBank's stake in Lenskart by close to 5.85 percentage points since June 2026.
Despite the reduction, SoftBank remains one of Lenskart's largest shareholders, alongside Platinum Jasmine A 2018 Trust, an Abu Dhabi Investment Authority vehicle, which separately holds a 9.77% stake. Because SVF II Lightbulb sits outside the promoter group, this sale has no bearing on promoter shareholding, which stood at 17.5 to 18% as of the June 2026 quarter.
Financial Performance
Looking at the quarterly results of Lenskart Solutions Limited, the company's consolidated revenue from operations increased by 43% YoY, from Rs. 1,894.46 crore in Q1 FY26 to Rs. 2,714.18 crore in Q1 FY27, for the quarter ended June 30, 2026.
Consolidated net profit for the quarter came in at around Rs. 228 crore, up roughly 270% YoY from about Rs. 60–61 crore in Q1 FY26 on a reported basis. The company separately cites a smaller, "pro-forma" prior-year base, adjusted for recent acquisitions, under which the increase works out closer to 182%. Consolidated EBITDA rose 61.3% YoY to Rs. 589 crore, with the EBITDA margin expanding to 21.7% from 17.7% a year earlier.
The basic earnings per share (EPS) increased by 255.56% YoY to Rs. 1.28 in Q1 FY27, compared with Rs. 0.36 recorded in the same quarter of the previous financial year, FY2026.
India operations contributed Rs. 1,530.82 crore of revenue during the quarter, while international operations, spanning Japan, Southeast Asia and the Middle East, contributed Rs. 1,203.29 crore, up 38% YoY. The company added 132 new stores during the quarter, taking its total active store count to 3,459.
What Does This Mean For Investors
For investors, the main takeaway is that SoftBank has reduced its stake in Lenskart from 9.86% to 7.27%, continuing its gradual exit from the company since its listing. The filing does not explain why the shares were sold or what SoftBank plans to do with the proceeds. With a sizable stake still remaining, investors will likely keep an eye on whether SoftBank makes any further sales after the reported 45-day lock-in period ends.

a.title: Lenskart Gold Membership as a Customer Retention Innovation
a.content:
Lenskart Gold Membership as a Customer Retention Innovation
Industry & Competitive Context
India's eyewear industry was valued at approximately USD 9.2 billion in FY25, according to a RedSeer-authored market study cited in Lenskart's DRHP, and is projected to grow at a compound annual rate of roughly 13%, reaching about USD 17.2 billion (₹1,483 billion) by FY30. Within this market, prescription eyeglasses account for roughly 73% of value, with sunglasses and contact lenses making up smaller shares. Organised retail chains and branded omnichannel players as opposed to independent local opticians held only about 19–24% of the market as of FY24/FY25 on RedSeer's estimates, with the balance held by unorganised, single-outlet opticians and street vendors. This structural fact is central to the industry's competitive logic: the largest addressable growth pool is not share taken from branded rivals but conversion of unorganised, one-time, discretionary purchasers into a repeat-purchase, branded relationship.
Lenskart's own market-sizing has been publicly contested by its principal listed competitor. Titan Eye+ has stated the Indian organised eyewear opportunity is closer to USD 3.4 billion, against Lenskart's disclosed USD 9.2 billion estimate a dispute that surfaced in financial media coverage around Lenskart's IPO in late 2025, with Titan arguing that Lenskart's larger figure incorporates unorganised-sector and latent-demand estimates rather than organised retail sales alone. Beyond Titan Eye+, named competitors identified in Lenskart's own disclosures and in financial press coverage include Specsmakers, Vision Express, Warby Parker, and the Italian conglomerate EssilorLuxottica.
Lenskart, founded in 2010, is documented in its DRHP as India's largest seller of prescription eyeglasses by volume in FY25, operating an integrated omnichannel model online, mobile app, and physical retail with manufacturing centralised in Bhiwadi and Gurugram (India) and supported by facilities in Singapore and the UAE. As of March 31, 2025, the company operated 2,723 stores globally (2,067 in India, 656 overseas); by June 30, 2025 this had risen to 2,806 stores (2,137 in India), and the company subsequently announced plans to add roughly 450 stores in FY26, taking its global footprint past 3,150 outlets across 14 countries. In FY25, Lenskart reported revenue from operations of ₹6,652.5 crore, up 22.5% year-on-year from ₹5,427.7 crore in FY24, alongside its first full-year net profit of ₹297.34 crore (versus a net loss of ₹10.15 crore in FY24). The company listed on the NSE and BSE in November 2025 following an IPO that was subscribed 28.26 times.
Brand Situation Prior to the Membership Program
Lenskart Gold was launched in 2018, at a stage when Lenskart was primarily known as a high-growth online-first eyewear retailer expanding into physical retail. The company's own press communication at launch, issued via its founder and CEO Peyush Bansal, framed the program as a mechanism to reward customers who purchase eyewear repeatedly, drawing an analogy to how consumers already own multiple wardrobe items for different occasions and could similarly own multiple pairs of eyewear. At launch, the membership was priced at ₹500 per year and offered a "Buy One, Get One" benefit across the company's John Jacobs and Vincent Chase private-label brands, redeemable from the customer's very first purchase and shareable with family members through a single registered mobile number.
Strategic Objective
Lenskart's own IPO disclosures frame Gold as one of several instruments alongside store network expansion, remote eye-testing infrastructure, and app-led engagement intended to convert episodic eyewear purchasers into a recurring, higher-frequency customer base. This is consistent with the category's underlying economics described above: with prescription eyeglasses typically replaced infrequently and much of the market unorganised and price-driven, a paid annual membership tied to a "second pair free" mechanic gives the company a structural reason for customers to make more than one purchase per membership cycle, and to consolidate multiple purchases (spectacles, sunglasses, contact lenses) within a single brand relationship rather than splitting them across the unorganised or organised competitive set.
The program's subsequent evolution Lenskart Gold Max launched in FY2024 and Lenskart Gold Max Pro launched in FY2025, according to Lenskart's official IPO investor-education note prepared by Axis Capital indicates a stated intent to tier the offer, extracting more value from higher-intent members through an escalating benefits ladder rather than a single flat membership.
Program Architecture & Execution
Lenskart operates its "Gold" membership in India and select international markets, distinct from a separate points-based loyalty scheme run through its Japanese/Southeast Asian subsidiary Owndays, which allows customers to earn redeemable points for purchases rather than a flat pre-purchased discount. According to the Axis Capital IPO note (drawing on the DRHP), Lenskart had 0.71 crore (7.1 million) Gold members in India as of June 30, 2025. A separate DRHP-based analysis published by financial-data platform Entrackr put India membership at 68 lakh (6.8 million) as of March 31, 2025 a figure broadly consistent with the Axis Capital number three months later. A further analytical write-up by Datum Intelligence, also drawing on DRHP disclosures, reported a considerably larger figure of 13.4 million members by H1 FY26, up from 3.4 million in FY23 a near four-fold increase over three years. Because these three sources do not specify identical geographic scope (India-only versus a possible broader/global count), this case reports all three as documented, rather than reconciling them into a single number; no single authoritative, unambiguous global membership figure is available from Lenskart's own primary filings as reviewed for this case.
On subscription revenue specifically, the Datum Intelligence analysis reports that Gold-related subscription income rose from ₹65.6 crore in FY23 to ₹108 crore in FY25, and reached ₹63.2 crore in the first half of FY26 alone already about 60% of the full FY25 total, which the source frames as a signal of renewal momentum. Separately, Entrackr's DRHP-based reporting shows a broader "services" revenue line which bundles membership income with home eye-checkup and training revenue growing 27% year-on-year to ₹133 crore in FY25, expressly attributed in the DRHP to the expansion of the Gold program. These are two different, only partially overlapping revenue lines (membership subscription alone versus a wider services bucket that includes membership), and both are reported here exactly as disclosed rather than merged.
On program mechanics, Lenskart's own loyalty page states that the Buy-One-Get-One benefit is valid on the company's Vincent Chase, Lenskart Air, John Jacobs, Hooper, and New Balance-branded eyewear (across eyeglasses and sunglasses combinations), is usable up to twice a month, is honoured across the app, website, 1,200-plus stores, and the company's home try-on service, and can be shared with family and friends by using the registered mobile number as the membership identifier. Consumer-facing deal-aggregator reporting (which carries lower editorial authority than a press release or the DRHP, and is flagged as such here) additionally describes a tiered structure in which the base Gold membership is priced around ₹500 per year, while Gold Max, priced higher, adds a 5% cashback on orders, free eye tests, and a 10% discount on Aqualens-branded contact lenses. These tier-specific prices are not confirmed in the DRHP excerpts reviewed for this case and should be treated as secondary-source reporting rather than official company disclosure.
On distribution, publicly available consumer-deal reporting describes Lenskart bundling free or discounted Gold/Gold Max memberships through partnerships with digital-payments and super-app platforms, including PhonePe, Google Pay, Times Prime, CRED, Swiggy One, and Zomato.
Positioning & Consumer Insight
The consumer insight articulated publicly by Lenskart at the program's 2018 launch via its CEO's own words in company press material was that eyewear was shifting from a single-purpose medical necessity to a category in which consumers might reasonably want multiple pairs for different occasions, in the way they already own multiple pairs of shoes or outfits. The Buy-One-Get-One structure operationalises that insight directly: rather than discounting a single pair, it monetises the second purchase decision, nudging a customer who came in for a functional prescription pair toward also acquiring a sunglasses pair or a second style, within the same brand.
The program's family-sharing mechanic allowing the same phone-number-linked membership to be used across a household extends the insight from an individual to a household unit, which is strategically significant in a market where eyewear purchases are often clustered by family occasion (school-age children, ageing parents needing corrective lenses, etc.). This mechanic is documented directly on Lenskart's own website and is not a third-party inference.
The tiering into Gold, Gold Max, and Gold Max Pro (FY2024 and FY2025 respectively, per the Axis Capital IPO note) suggests a positioning shift from a single flat-rate loyalty instrument toward a value-laddered subscription business, in which higher-paying members receive incremental benefits (cashback, additional category discounts). No verified public information is available on the relative mix of members across these three tiers, nor on differential purchase behaviour by tier.
Media & Channel Strategy
What is documented is
(a) the program's channel presence across Lenskart's own app, website, and 1,200-plus physical stores, as stated on the company's official loyalty page, and
(b) its bundling into third-party platform ecosystems (PhonePe, Google Pay, Times Prime, CRED, Swiggy One, Zomato) as reported in consumer deal-aggregator coverage, which functions as a distribution and acquisition channel rather than a media campaign in the traditional sense.
At the company level (not specific to Gold), Lenskart disclosed total marketing costs of ₹448 crore in FY25, up 27% year-on-year, according to DRHP-based reporting by Entrackr but this figure covers the company's overall marketing spend across brand and performance channels, and cannot be attributed specifically to the Gold membership program. No breakdown isolating loyalty-program marketing spend from the ₹448 crore total is available in public sources reviewed.
Business & Brand Outcomes
The following outcomes are documented in the sources cited and are reported here without extrapolation:
Membership scale reached 0.71 crore (7.1 million) in India as of June 30, 2025, per the Axis Capital IPO note; a separate DRHP-based estimate put it at 68 lakh (6.8 million) as of March 31, 2025 (Entrackr); and a third analytical source (Datum Intelligence) reported a figure of 13.4 million by H1 FY26 against 3.4 million in FY23, describing this as a near four-fold increase over three years. As noted above, these figures are not necessarily measuring an identical scope and are presented as separately sourced, rather than reconciled.
Subscription-linked revenue rose from ₹65.6 crore (FY23) to ₹108 crore (FY25) to ₹63.2 crore in H1 FY26 alone, per the Datum Intelligence DRHP-based analysis. The broader "services" revenue line that includes membership income, alongside home eye-checkup and training revenue, grew 27% to ₹133 crore in FY25, per Entrackr's DRHP-based reporting, which explicitly attributes this growth to Gold program expansion.
Lenskart's overall annual transacting customer base rose 23% to 99 lakh (9.9 million) in FY25, and unit eyewear sales rose 30% to 2 crore (20 million) pairs, per Entrackr's DRHP-based reporting company-wide figures that provide relevant context for the scale of the customer base into which the Gold program is embedded, though they are not membership-specific metrics.
Lenskart was named "India's Most Trusted Eyewear Brand of 2025" by TRA Research, according to the company's own IPO investor-education note a brand-level, third-party-adjudicated recognition disclosed by the company, though not directly attributable to the Gold program in the source material.
The company's IPO in which loyalty-driven recurring revenue was cited by DRHP-based commentary as a contributing narrative to its "sticky ecosystem" positioning was subscribed 28.26 times overall (40.35x in the Qualified Institutional Buyer category) when it closed on November 4, 2025, at a price band of ₹382–402 per share, according to Business Standard's reporting of exchange data. This is a company-level capital-markets outcome, not a Gold-specific outcome, and should be read as market validation of Lenskart's overall business model rather than direct evidence of the membership program's individual contribution.
Strategic Implications
Three implications follow directly from the documented facts above, without extending into unverified inference about mechanisms Lenskart has not disclosed.
First, Lenskart's membership architecture illustrates a route to building recurring revenue inside a category prescription eyewear that is structurally low-frequency at the level of a single product but can be made higher-frequency at the level of a household relationship, through mechanics (BOGO, family sharing, multi-tier upgrades) that are documented as central to Gold's design. The near four-fold membership growth reported by Datum Intelligence over three years, alongside the DRHP's own attribution of services-revenue growth to Gold's expansion, indicates the program has scaled meaningfully as the company approached its public listing, even though the precise financial contribution and profitability of the program are not independently disclosed.
Second, the tiering strategy Gold, then Gold Max (FY2024), then Gold Max Pro (FY2025) reflects a standard subscription-business pattern of introducing higher-value tiers once a base membership has proven adoption, a sequencing that is documented in the company's own IPO note rather than inferred. This suggests Lenskart's leadership treats the membership program as an evolving product line in its own right, not a static promotional device.
Third, the public dispute over market sizing between Lenskart and Titan Eye+ with the two companies citing materially different addressable-market figures ($9.2 billion versus $3.4 billion) is now a matter of public record following Lenskart's listing, and it illustrates a broader implication for any retailer that leans on unorganised-market conversion (rather than organised-competitor share capture) as its primary growth narrative to public-market investors: the credibility of that narrative, and by extension of loyalty-led conversion mechanisms like Gold, is now subject to ongoing public and analyst scrutiny in a way it was not while Lenskart was a private company.
Discussion Questions
- Lenskart discloses at least three different membership-count figures (7.1 million India-only as of June 2025; 6.8 million India-only as of March 2025; 13.4 million globally as of H1 FY26) drawn from different secondary interpretations of the same DRHP. As an analyst evaluating this business ahead of investment, how would you reconcile or interrogate these figures, and what does the discrepancy itself suggest about the reliability of loyalty-program metrics in IPO disclosures generally?
- Gold's core mechanic Buy One, Get One effectively monetises a second purchase decision rather than discounting the first. What are the margin and inventory implications of this design choice compared with a simple percentage-discount loyalty program, and under what category conditions (purchase frequency, unit economics, private-label mix) does a BOGO membership make more sense than a points-based scheme like Owndays'?
- Lenskart operates two structurally different loyalty models in parallel a flat-fee BOGO membership (Gold, in India and select markets) and a points-accrual scheme (Owndays, in Japan/Southeast Asia). What might explain this divergence by geography, and what should a multinational retailer consider before deciding whether to standardise a single loyalty architecture globally versus letting acquired subsidiaries retain their own models?
- The DRHP attributes 27% growth in "services revenue" (which bundles membership, eye-checkups, and training) to Gold's expansion, but does not disclose the standalone profitability of the membership program. Why might a company choose to disclose top-line growth attribution for a program while withholding its unit economics, and what should this signal to a public-market investor evaluating the durability of that growth?
- Titan Eye+ and Lenskart publicly disagree on the size of the addressable Indian eyewear market by a factor of nearly three. If Lenskart's loyalty-led strategy depends on converting unorganised-market, first-time buyers (as opposed to taking organised-market share from Titan), how should an investor's confidence in Gold's long-term contribution to revenue be affected by which of the two market-sizing narratives proves closer to reality?

SVF II Lightbulb disposes 4.5 crore Lenskart shares in open market
- SVF II Lightbulb sold 4.5 crore Lenskart Solutions Ltd shares on August 24, 2026
- The open market transaction reduced the seller's stake from 9.86% to 7.27%
- The disposal breached the 2% threshold under SEBI Takeover Regulations
- Total equity share capital remained unchanged at 17.39 crore shares
*this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only.
Lenskart Solutions disclosed a significant reduction in its shareholding by SVF II Lightbulb (Cayman) Limited, which sold 4.5 crore equity shares on August 24, 2026. The open market transaction triggered a mandatory filing under Regulation 29(2) of the SEBI Takeover Regulations due to the breach of the 2% threshold.
The disposal reduced SVF II Lightbulb’s total holding from 1.71 crore shares to 1.26 crore shares. Consequently, its stake in the eyewear retailer fell from 9.86% to 7.27% of the total voting capital. The seller confirmed that no warrants, convertible securities, or other instruments entitling them to voting rights were involved in the transaction.
Transaction Details
The sale was executed entirely through the open market mechanism. There were no encumbrances, pledges, or liens associated with the shares held by the seller before or after the disposal. The company’s total equity share capital remained unchanged at 17.39 crore shares, with a face value of ₹2 per equity share.
What the Numbers Show
The disposal represents a substantial exit of 2.59% of the company’s total voting capital in a single day. With the stake dropping below the 10% mark to 7.27%, SVF II Lightbulb remains a significant institutional holder but has materially reduced its exposure compared to its previous near-10% position. The absence of any remaining encumbrances suggests the shares were freely tradable prior to the sale.

Market News
7 min read | Updated on August 26, 2026, 13:16 IST
SUMMARY
SEPC stock rallied as much as 8.5% to hit an intraday high of ₹6.26 per unit on the NSE, as its board approved a restructuring of the equity and capitalisation reserves of its wholly owned UAE subsidiary, SEPC FZE, Sharjah, enabling the acquisition of a UAE petroleum trading business entirely through non-cash consideration.
While the markets opened in the green, they pared their early gains during the noon session on August 26.
The Indian benchmark indices, SENSEX and NIFTY50, were in negative territory during the afternoon session on Wednesday, August 26, with the SENSEX trading flat amid a sell-off in information technology (IT) and infrastructure stocks. While the markets opened in the green, they pared their early gains.
At 1:02 PM, the S&P BSE SENSEX was trading flat at 77,625.83, down by 30.27 points, or 0.04%,, while NSE’s NIFTY50 stood at 24,271.15, marking a 63.40-point, or 0.26% decline.
Shares of oil-linked stocks and oil marketing companies (OMCs) were trading higher during the morning market hours on Wednesday, August 26, as investors focused on the third consecutive day of declining crude oil prices in the global market amid mixed cues from the West Asia conflict.
NSE data showed that the sectoral benchmark index, Nifty Oil & Gas, recorded key support from downstream oil-linked stocks, gaining 0.3% to touch an early market high of 11,248.40 points on Wednesday, compared to 11,214.90 points at the previous equity market close.
While oil downstream companies, aviation stocks, and paint stocks were gaining momentum, on the other hand, oil upstream companies like ONGC and Oil India were among the losers during the trading session on August 26.
The stocks of maritime companies (shipping and shipbuilding theme) such as Shipping Corporation of India (SCI), The Great Eastern Shipping Company (GE Shipping), Cochin Shipyard, Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders, and Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers Ltd (GRSE) were trading in the green zone on Wednesday, August 26.
The shares came under buying interest as the government plans to add 100 more new vessels to its merchant fleet over the next five years to cut $75 billion in freight bills, Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal said on Tuesday.
The plan, discussed at the National Shipping Board’s (NSB) first ‘Sagar Samvad’ event on Tuesday, is part of a broader five-pillar roadmap aimed at making Indian-flagged shipping more competitive and helping the country emerge as one of the world’s top five ship-owning nations by 2047.
Shares of Cyient soared as much as 7.7% to hit an intraday high of ₹1,054.85 apiece on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) on Wednesday, August 26, as the Competition Commission of India (CCI) on Tuesday gave approval to the global engineering services provider for its proposed acquisition of TAO Digital Solutions Inc.
The approval came after Hyderabad-based Cyient Ltd, in May this year, announced that it had entered into a definitive agreement to acquire TAO Digital Solutions Inc, an AI-native data and product engineering solutions firm headquartered in Santa Clara, California.
"The proposed combination envisages the acquisition of 100% of the share capital from the existing shareholders of TAO Digital Solutions Inc (target), by Cyient Ltd (acquirer)," the regulator said in a release.
"CCI approves the acquisition of 100% of the share capital of Tao Digital Solutions Inc by Cyient Limited," the regulator said in a post on the microblogging platform X (formerly Twitter).
The stock of Hindustan Copper gained as much as 3.59% to hit a high of ₹551.80 apiece on Wednesday, August 26, a day after the stock witnessed a sharp slide following the launch of the government’s offer for sale (OFS).
Institutional investors on Tuesday oversubscribed Hindustan Copper share sale by putting in bids worth over ₹4,600 crore.
As against the 2.61 crore shares reserved for them, institutional investors put in bids for over 8.91 crore shares, oversubscribing the issue 3.41 times. At an indicative price of ₹520.35 per share, the bids are valued at over ₹4,600 crore.
The government is selling over 5.80 crore shares, or up to a 6% (including 3% green shoe option) stake in Hindustan Copper through a two-day Offer-for-Sale (OFS) at a floor price of ₹514 apiece.
Adani Energy Solutions shares gained as much as 3% to touch an intraday high of ₹1,637 apiece on Wednesday, August 26, after the company bagged a transmission project in Maharashtra.
The Adani Group firm, in a regulatory filing, said it has secured a project that involves key transmission work for evacuation of renewable energy generated in Karnataka to major load centres in Maharashtra. Worth approximately ₹4,700 crore, the project will also support the growing pumped storage ecosystem in the Satara, Pune and Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR).
Adani Energy said that the project, called “Network Expansion Scheme in Western Region to Cater to Pumped Storage Potential near Satara (up to 4500 MW) - Part A”, was won through the Tariff Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB) process, where AESL emerged as the lowest bidder.
KPI Green Energy stock advanced as much as 1.4% to hit the session’s peak of ₹323.65 per equity share on the NSE, as the company achieved its highest-ever capacity energization of more than 630MW DC across IPP and EPC/CPP businesses in the June-August quarter.
“It marks yet another step forward in the Company’s journey toward its stated ambition of scaling capacity in line with KP Group’s broader target of over 10 GW of renewable capacity by 2030 and reinforces its position as one of India’s fastest-growing renewable energy platforms,” the company said in a regulatory filing.
The existing share capital of SEPC FZE, comprising one share of AED 150,000, will be subdivided into 1,500 shares of AED 100 each. A further 38,500 shares of AED 100 each will be issued out of capitalisation of reserves, creating a total equity pool of 40,000 shares, according to a regulatory filing. Of this enlarged pool, only 1,700 shares (4.25%) have been earmarked as non-cash consideration for the share swap. The balance 38,300 shares will be issued to SEPC Limited as fully paid-up shares by capitalisation of reserves, leaving the parent with a post-issue holding of 95.75% in SEPC FZE, Sharjah.
Shares of Welspun Corp declined after, according to news reports, the company's promoter group, Welspun Investments and Commercials, and MD & CEO Vipul Mathur have proposed to sell up to 6.3 million shares, or around 2.4% of the company’s equity, through a block deal.
The offer price has been set at ₹2,250 per share, implying a discount of up to 4.1% to the prevailing market price, with the transaction valued at around ₹1,418 crore ($149 million).
Shares of Gaja Alternative Asset Management Ltd listed at ₹185 per unit on the NSE. This reflects a premium of 15.63% over the IPO issue price of ₹160 per share. On the BSE, the stock started trading at ₹185.20 per equity share, up 15.75% from the issue price.

a.title: From Nykaa to Traker: Pradeep Khandekar's Tech-Led Vision Drives Traker Past 1 Lakh+ App Downloads in India
a.content:
From Nykaa to Traker: Pradeep Khandekar's Tech-Led Vision Drives Traker Past 1 Lakh+ App Downloads in India
.
	Mumbai, India: From leading engineering at Nykaa to building a homegrown mobility and logistics platform, Pradeep Khandekar’s journey from Nykaa to Traker has reached another significant milestone. The application has crossed 1 lakh+ app downloads, strengthening its growing presence in India’s technology-driven transportation ecosystem.
	For users searching for a reliable cab service in Mumbai, cabs in Mumbai, bike taxi in Mumbai, auto rides or local transportation, the brand is building a multi-service experience designed to bring everyday transport options together. At the same time, its Boss Partner solution connects bike, auto, cab and mini truck partners with technology-enabled earning choices. It is now available in Mumbai, Pune, Indore and Hyderabad.
	The milestone therefore represents growth on both sides of the ecosystem—customers looking for convenient transportation and drivers looking for flexible work.
From Nykaa to Building a Mobility Business
	Before founding the venture, Pradeep Khandekar developed extensive experience in engineering and digital product development.
	He served as VP Engineering at Nykaa, working with engineering teams across mobile applications, product strategy and planning. He later served as CTO at RupeeBoss, leading technology across mobile, desktop, Android and iOS environments.
	Today, Khandekar is applying that technology-first experience to the venture, developing a digital service built around the everyday transportation needs of Indian customers and transport partners.
Making Everyday Travel Simpler for Users
	The business is positioning itself as more than a traditional cab booking app.
	Through one interface, users can access:
- Bike rides
- Auto rides
- Car rides
- Mini truck services
	For someone searching for online cab booking in Mumbai, a quick bike taxi, or an online solution for everyday local travel, the service aims to simplify the process by providing multiple vehicle categories within one ecosystem.
	Features such as digital booking, partner and vehicle information, live trip visibility and digital payment options are designed to give customers greater convenience throughout their journey.
	By combining passenger rides with goods transportation, the service can also support people whose needs extend beyond daily commuting—from booking a car to arranging a mini truck for local goods movement.
Building Opportunities for Driver Partners
	The other half of the brand’s growth story is its expanding partner community.
	The Traker Boss Driver Partner App supports two-wheeler riders, auto operators, cab drivers, mini truck operators and independent vehicle owners.
	For people searching for a bike driver app, cab driver app India, auto partner solution or driver partner service, the technology is designed to simplify ride management while offering flexible earning options.
	Partner-focused features include digital onboarding, real-time trip information, earnings visibility, weekly payouts and support.
	The brand has also introduced its Driver Loyalty Rewards Program, under which eligible partners who meet the required daily activity and trip criteria while maintaining zero cancellations can receive an additional ₹100 in their wallet.
	The initiative recognises transport partners who consistently contribute to a reliable customer experience.
One Technology Ecosystem for Customers and Drivers
	What differentiates the venture’s journey is the connection between both sides of urban transport.
	Customers need convenient and dependable rides. Drivers need access to trip opportunities and technology that helps them work efficiently. The service is being developed around both requirements rather than treating them separately.
	Two-wheelers. Auto. Cars. Mini Truck.
	By bringing these categories together, the venture is building a broader transport and logistics ecosystem for urban India.
	For Khandekar, the transition from Nykaa to this new venture represents the application of years of engineering and product experience to a new challenge: using technology to improve how people and goods move through Indian cities.
1 Lakh+ Downloads and the Journey Ahead
	Crossing 1 lakh+ app downloads is an important marker in the brand’s growth, but the team sees it as part of a larger journey.
	As the business strengthens its presence and expands its network, the focus remains on attracting more customers, creating earning options for driver partners and using technology to make local transportation easier to access.
	From a customer searching for cabs in Mumbai to a transport partner looking for flexible earning choices, the service is working to bring both sides of the ecosystem onto one connected network.
	The 1 lakh+ milestone signals growing momentum for that vision and a new chapter in Pradeep Khandekar’s journey from building technology at Nykaa to developing Traker for India’s evolving mobility market.
About Traker
	Traker Networks Private Limited is a technology-driven mobility and logistics business offering two-wheeler, auto, cab and mini truck services through its digital ecosystem. The brand connects customers seeking convenient transportation with partners looking for flexible earning options.

a.title: Cyient (NSE:CYIENT): Did CCI Clear Its Acquisition of Tao Digital Solutions Inc?
a.content:
Cyient Limited (NSE:CYIENT), in an exchange filing dated 26 August 2026, disclosed that the Competition Commission of India approved its proposed acquisition of 100% stake in Tao Digital Solutions Inc., a US-incorporated company, under Section 31(1) of the Competition Act, 2002.
Key Highlights
- The CCI communicated its approval via a letter dated 25 August 2026, referencing combination registration number C-2026/06/1433 filed by Cyient on 15 June 2026.
- Cyient had originally disclosed a definitive agreement to acquire 100% stake in Tao Digital Solutions Inc. through an exchange filing on 30 May 2026.
- The CCI approved the combination under Section 31(1) of the Competition Act, 2002, following its meeting held on 25 August 2026.
- The transaction remains subject to customary closing conditions; the CCI order confirming the approval is expected to follow the letter of communication.
About the Company
Cyient Limited (NSE:CYIENT), headquartered at Madhapur, Hyderabad, is a global engineering and technology solutions provider. The company delivers design, manufacturing, and digital technology services across aerospace, defence, medical devices, semiconductor, and rail industries, serving clients across North America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific. It is listed on BSE (scrip code 532175) and NSE.
Announcement in Detail
In its filing under Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, Cyient confirmed receipt of the CCI's approval letter dated 25 August 2026. The commission considered the proposed combination in its meeting on the same date and cleared it under Section 31(1) of the Competition Act, 2002. The CCI's formal order is stated to follow the communication.
The combination notice bearing registration number C-2026/06/1433 was originally filed by Cyient with the CCI on 15 June 2026, under sub-section (2) of Section 6 of the Competition Act, 2002. The underlying definitive agreement to acquire the entire 100% stake in Tao Digital Solutions Inc., a company incorporated in the United States, was entered into by Cyient and disclosed to exchanges on 30 May 2026.
Impact on Investors
Investors will note that the CCI approval represents a material regulatory milestone in the acquisition process. The filing indicates the transaction has cleared a mandatory competition-law review. However, the disclosure specifies that customary closing conditions must still be satisfied before the deal concludes, meaning the acquisition is not yet complete at the time of this filing.
Shareholders will observe that the consideration structure and financial terms of the acquisition were not re-stated in this specific filing; those details, as disclosed on 30 May 2026, remain the applicable reference. The disclosed terms indicate any final impact on Cyient's consolidated financials will depend on the completion of remaining closing formalities.
Sector / Market Context
India's engineering research and development services sector has seen sustained cross-border acquisition activity as domestic players seek to expand digital and software-embedded engineering capabilities in North American markets. According to NASSCOM data, India's technology and engineering services exports have grown consistently, with engineering R&D services forming an expanding share of total IT-sector revenue, making inorganic international expansion a widely adopted strategic approach among listed Indian engineering services companies.

a.title: Hold Cyient; target of Rs 1040: Prabhudas Lilladher
a.content:
Prabhudas Lilladher's research report on Cyient
We attended CYIENT’s Investor Day, where management outlined its strategy to pivot from project-led ER&D toward lifecycle engineering and annuity-based models, with the objective of improving predictable and quality revenues. The strategic pivot expands Cyient’s addressable opportunity beyond the ~USD 100bn traditional ER&D outsourcing market to ~USD 2.4–3.2tn of outsourced spend across the broader asset lifecycle. Cyient has already established a foothold in the after-sales opportunity, with access to 58% of its Top 200 accounts in after-sales services and aims to increase the contribution of after-sales/lifecycle services to 25% of revenue and recurring revenue to 50%. Additionally, the improving NN order intake (+64% YoY in FY26) within its selective buckets (Transportation, Wireless Connectivity and Energy) drives better revenue visibility in the medium-term. However, project-based work still contributes significantly at ~25–30% of revenue, while ~55–60% of contracts get renewed quarterly, resulting in growth volatility. Cyient aspires to drive more annuity-based arrangements by (1) offering a breadth of service portfolio, (2) having established senior leaders to dedicated BUs and (3) fixing internal constraints to drive better execution. With this, Cyient aspires to deliver revenue CAGR above industry peers with 15%+ EBIT margin in FY28-29, followed by industry-leading growth and 16%+ EBIT margin by FY31. We believe that the pivot towards managing lifecycle engineering can structurally improve the quality of Cyient’s revenue; however, the key monitorable remain the success rate and execution within its marquee accounts. We have not integrated Tao Digital’s financials, as the acquisition is yet to be completed and have largely maintained our FY27E and FY28E DET USD revenue growth estimates, while marginally increasing our EBIT margin estimates to 13.5% and 14.0% (13.2% and 13.7% earlier), respectively.
Outlook
We maintain our HOLD rating with a TP of INR 1,040, based on the SOTP methodology.

a.title: Cyient shares rocket 8% after investor day, but brokerages see up to 24% downside. Here’s why
a.content:
Listen to this article in summarized format
Cyient said its immediate focus is to reignite growth, targeting double-digit year-on-year revenue growth and steady quarter-on-quarter growth through FY28-29. In the near term, the company is targeting EBIT margins of more than 15%, while its medium- to long-term goal is to deliver industry-leading growth with EBIT margins above 16%.
The company said its go-to-market (GTM) team is now fully in place to pursue larger deals and gradually move the business from project-based work towards annuity-based contracts, which provide greater revenue predictability. Project-based work currently makes up around 40% of the business.
Management said Cyient's large-deal pipeline has reached a record high, with nine qualified deals carrying a combined total contract value of around $300 million.
Cyient described FY26 as a year of stabilisation after several strategic interventions. It expects FY27 and FY28 to mark the start of a recovery driven by its revamped strategy.
The company has also made progress on margins, with EBIT margin rising to 13.2% in Q1 FY27 from around 12.2%. Management aims to reach the 15% medium-term target through AI-led revenue leverage and operating cost efficiencies.
Motilal Oswal on Cyient
Motilal Oswal reiterated its Sell rating on Cyient with a target price of Rs 740, 24% downside, saying the recovery remains back-ended and that FY27 organic growth is expected to remain broadly flat. The brokerage said it is encouraged by the semiconductor opportunity but would wait for proof of concept before assigning considerable valuation to the business.
The domestic brokerage continues to value the Digital, Engineering and Technology (DET) business at 9x FY28E EPS. This reflects gradual margin improvement, a muted organic growth outlook and continued execution risk. The brokerage also continues to apply a holding company discount to the value of the DLM stake.
Nuvama on Cyient
Nuvama retained its Hold rating on Cyient while raising its target price to Rs 1,050 (7.5% upside) from Rs 900. The brokerage said the company's total addressable market (TAM) has expanded significantly, from around $100 billion to $2.4-3.2 trillion, creating a larger long-term growth opportunity.
Nuvama highlighted Cyient's three-year roadmap, which envisages stabilisation in FY26, transformation in FY27 and scaling in FY28. The company has set an FY31 objective of achieving industry-leading growth alongside a 16% EBIT margin. Cyient Semiconductors, meanwhile, is targeting nearly 4X revenue growth, a gross margin of more than 40% and an EBIT margin above 20% by FY31.
The company has also introduced CYINGINE, a platform designed to help clients scale AI adoption and deliver measurable engineering outcomes.
PL Capital on Cyient
PL Capital said the key monitorables remain the success rate and execution within Cyient's marquee accounts. The brokerage has not incorporated Tao Digital's financials as the acquisition is yet to be completed.
It has largely retained its FY27E and FY28E DET USD revenue growth estimates while marginally raising its EBIT margin estimates to 13.5% and 14.0%, respectively, from 13.2% and 13.7% earlier. PL Capital maintained its Hold rating with a target price of Rs 1,040, an upside of 6.5% from the last closing price.

a.title: Cyient shares surge 8%: Targets by MOFSL, Antique, Choice, Nuvama post Investor Day
a.content:
Cyient Ltd shares rallied 8 per cent in Wednesday’s trade after a couple of brokerages raised their target prices on the stock following the midcap IT firm’s Investor Day. At the event, the management indicated a significant expansion in Cyient’s addressable market, from $100 billion in traditional ER&D outsourcing to $2.4-3.2 trillion by covering the full engineering lifecycle across nine value-chain stages.
This provided a much larger runway for future growth, Nuvama Institutional Equities said as it upped its target on the stock to Rs 1,050 from Rs 900.  On Wednesday, Cyient share price jumped 7.66 per cent to hit a high of Rs 1,054.60.
Cyient's DET (Digital, Engineering, and Technology) EBIT margin target is set at 15 per cent by FY28 against at 13.2 per cent in Q1. Cyient Semiconductors targets 4 times revenue growth by FY31 with 40 per cent gross margin and 20 per cent-plus EBIT, supported by Kinetic Technologies and increasing traction in its ASSP and ASIC businesses.
"We continue to value the stock using SotP methodology —DET business at 11 times FY28E PE and DLM at current market cap (post 20 per cent holdco discount). We now include semicon business (1x FY28E EV/sales) in our valuation," Nuvama said.
Inexpensive valuations limit downside potential, it said.
Choice Institutional, which attended Cyient's Investor Day, said the Investor Day takeaways strengthened the medium-term growth and earnings-quality thesis, although large-deal conversion and the pace of growth recovery remain key execution watchpoints. It maintained ‘Buy’ rating on Cyient and raise its target to Rs 1,200.
Antique Stock Broking said while the FY27-31 roadmap remained clear, execution is the key monitorable as the company navigates capitalising on the service-oriented stages of the industry lifecycle.
"We continue to maintain our BUY rating with an SOTP-based target of Rs 1,125, reflecting our 11 times 1HFY29E EPS target multiple for Cyient’s DET business," it said.
MOFSL, meanwhile, retained its 'Sell' rating on Cyient as the recovery continued to remain back-ended and expectation for FY27 is a flat organic growth.
"While we are excited about the semiconductor opportunity, we will wait to see some proof of concept before giving a considerable valuation to the business," MOFSL said.
"Based on our SoTP valuation, we continue to value the DET business at 9x FY28E EPS, reflecting gradual margin improvement, a muted organic growth outlook, and continued execution risk," it said while suggesting a target of Rs 740.

a.content:
Delhi High Court Temporarily Restrains Sale Of Counterfeits With Sun Pharma's 'Photostable,' 'Bello' Marks
Riya Rathore
25 Aug 2026 4:53 PM IST
The Delhi High Court on 10 August granted an ad-interim injunction restraining several entities from selling counterfeit dermatological and skincare products bearing Sun Pharma Laboratories Ltd's registered trademarks 'PHOTOSTABLE' and 'BELLO'.
Justice A. J. Bhambhani passed the order in a commercial suit filed by Sun Pharma Laboratories Ltd against Wear and Glow and other defendants, alleging trademark infringement. The Bench observed:
“the plaintiffs have succeeded in making-out a prima-facie case in its favour” and held that “the balance of convenience also lies in favour of the plaintiffs and against the defendants.”
Sun Pharma submitted that it was the registered proprietor of the trademarks 'BELLO' and 'PHOTOSTABLE'. It submitted that 'PHOTOSTABLE' covers two distinct product sub-ranges, 'BELLO PHOTOSTABLE' and 'PHOTOSTABLE GOLD', both marketed in India in relation to dermatological and skincare products.
The company alleged that Defendants No. 1 to 13 were selling identical counterfeit products bearing these trademarks. It sought an ad-interim injunction restraining the defendants from using 'PHOTOSTABLE', 'BELLO', or any mark deceptively similar to these marks or to its house mark 'SUN'. It also sought restraint against reproduction of its original artistic works, trade dress, packaging and labels.
The Court held that “irreparable loss and injury would be caused to the plaintiffs if the interim injunction as prayed-for is not granted” and restrained the defendants from using the marks 'PHOTOSTABLE', 'BELLO' and the plaintiffs' house marks 'SUN'/'SUN PHARMA', and from reproducing the plaintiffs' original artistic works, trade dress or packaging, until the next date of hearing.
The matter is listed before the Joint Registrar on 17 November 2026 for completion of pleadings.

a.title: SoftBank cuts Lenskart stakes for second time, sells  ₹2,888 cr worth shares to Goldman Sachs, Societe Generale, others
a.content:
SoftBank continues to offload its holding in Lenskart, selling shares worth ₹2,888 crore just two months after selling ₹2,873 crore worth of its stake in the eyewear retailer.
In the latest transaction, Japan-based SoftBank Group, through its affiliate SVF II Lightbulb (Cayman) Ltd, offloaded a total of 4.5 crore equity shares in 22 tranches, amounting to a 2.58 per cent stake in Gurugram-based Lenskart, said the block deal data on the BSE.
In June, SoftBank sold a 3.25 per cent stake in Lenskart for ₹2,873 crore. Following the sale, shares of Lenskart Solutions fell 0.28 per cent to close at ₹659.70 apiece on the BSE on Monday.
The block deal saw participation from a wide range of institutional investors.
Domestic buyers included National Pension System Trust and mutual funds managed by SBI, Edelweiss, Nippon India, Franklin Templeton, HDFC, HSBC, ICICI Prudential, Motilal Oswal and Sundaram.
ICICI Prudential Life Insurance was also among the buyers.
Among foreign investors, financial services company Societe Generale picked up the largest number of shares, acquiring 1,07,35,000 shares, representing a 0.62 per cent stake.
This was followed by Goldman Sachs, which bought 84.31 lakh equity shares in Lenskart for ₹541.06 crore. Motilal Oswal Mutual Fund acquired 47.71 lakh shares for ₹306.17 crore, while Pennsylvania-based Vanguard Group Inc. picked up 37.28 lakh shares for ₹239.2 crore.
Other foreign investors that lapped up Lenskart shares included Ghisallo Capital Management, Morgan Stanley, BNP Paribas Financial Markets, Wasatch Global Investors, and Integrated Core Strategies Asia.
Other buyers included Frankfurt-based Universal Investment, Teachers' Retirement System of the State of Illinois, Pennsylvania Public School Employees' Retirement System and Kuwait Investment Authority.
The shares were sold at an average price of ₹641.75 apiece, taking the combined deal size to ₹2,887.87 crore, the block deal data showed
As per the shareholding pattern for June 2026, SoftBank held a 9.86% stake in Lenskart, which appears to have reduced to 7.28% following the above-mentioned block deals. Meanwhile, HSBC MF held a 1.15% stake, while SBI Mutual Fund held a 2.44% stake in the company.
The latest transaction brought SoftBank's holding in Lenskart down to 7.28% from 9.86%, although it remains the second-largest public shareholder in the eyewear firm.
Platinum Jasmine A 2018 Trust, an arm of Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, continues to be the largest public shareholder of Lenskart with a 9.77 per cent stake.

a.title: SoftBank Offloads 4.50 Cr Lenskart Shares For Rs 2,887.9 Cr In Second Block Deal
a.content:
SoftBank sells 4.50 crore Lenskart shares for Rs 2,887.9 crore in latest block deal, marking its second major partial exit after the eyewear retailer’s listing.
SoftBank Vision Fund II Lightbulb Ltd sold the shares at an average price of Rs 641.75 each, a 3 per cent discount to the previous close, according to BSE data. Societe Generale was the largest buyer with 1.1 crore shares, while Goldman Sachs, Motilal Oswal Mutual Fund, HSBC Mutual Fund, Vanguard-linked investors, HDFC Mutual Fund, Ghisallo Capital, BNP Paribas, Morgan Stanley and Kuwait Investment Authority were among other buyers.
The transaction follows a June block deal in which SoftBank sold 5.65 crore shares for Rs 2,873.3 crore. Despite that sale, SoftBank held a 9.79 per cent stake, or 17.14 crore shares, as of 30 June 2026.
Lenskart’s stock has risen about 69 per cent from its listing price of Rs 390 and is up roughly 50 per cent year-to-date, even as it closed 0.67 per cent lower at Rs 656.95 on the day of the deal. The rally has enabled other institutional investors, including KKR, ABG Capital, Alpha Wave, TR Capital and ADIA, to reduce stakes after the lock-in period ended on 8 May.
The eyewear retailer reported its first full-year profit in FY25, with net profit more than doubling to Rs 530 crore in FY26 on 32.3 per cent revenue growth to Rs 9,002.3 crore. In Q1 FY27, profit more than tripled year-on-year to Rs 228.4 crore, while operating revenue rose 43 per cent year-on-year and 8 per cent quarter-on-quarter to Rs 2,714.2 crore.
Lenskart also disclosed overseas investments, including Rs 10.6 crore in Singapore-based Baofeng Framekart Technology Ltd, a joint venture with Geng Yongchao, and Rs 20 crore to expand OWNDAYS into South Korea and set up a new subsidiary in China. Separately, the company reported a cyber incident affecting a sub-vendor of its Singapore-based group company last week.

a.title: Softbank Sells Another 2.6% Stake In Lenskart For Rs 2,888 Cr
a.content:
SoftBank Group has further reduced its stake in eyewear retailer Lenskart Solutions, selling shares worth Rs 2,888 crore in an open-market transaction on Monday, according to BSE block deal data.
SoftBank, through its affiliate SVF II Lightbulb (Cayman) Ltd, sold 4.5 crore shares, representing a 2.58 per cent stake in Lenskart, in 22 tranches at an average price of Rs 641.75 per share.
The latest sale comes two months after SoftBank offloaded a 3.25 per cent stake in Lenskart for Rs 2,873 crore in June, signalling a continued reduction in its exposure to the Gurugram-based company.
Following Monday's transaction, SoftBank's holding in Lenskart fell to 7.28 per cent from 9.86 per cent, although it remained the second-largest public shareholder in the company.
Platinum Jasmine A 2018 Trust, an investment vehicle linked to Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, remained Lenskart's largest public shareholder with a 9.77 per cent stake.
The shares sold by SoftBank were absorbed by a broad group of domestic and international institutional investors, highlighting continued investor interest in the eyewear retailer despite the large block transaction.
Among foreign investors, Societe Generale was the largest buyer, acquiring 1.07 crore shares, equivalent to a 0.62 per cent stake, for about Rs 688.91 crore at the same price of Rs 641.75 per share.
Other overseas buyers included Ghisallo Capital Management, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, BNP Paribas Financial Markets, Vanguard, Wasatch Global Investors and Integrated Core Strategies Asia.
Domestic institutional investors participating in the transaction included the National Pension System Trust and mutual funds managed by SBI, Edelweiss, Nippon India, Franklin Templeton, HDFC, HSBC, ICICI Prudential, Motilal Oswal and Sundaram. ICICI Prudential Life Insurance was also among the buyers.
Other investors that acquired shares included Frankfurt-based Universal Investment, Teachers' Retirement System of the State of Illinois, Pennsylvania Public School Employees' Retirement System and Kuwait Investment Authority.

a.title: Nykaa’s Premiumisation Strategy Faces Quick-Commerce Test
a.content:
Nykaa is expected to benefit from rising premium smartphone ownership and increasing spending on premium beauty and personal care products, with its beauty and personal care gross merchandise value estimated to grow at a compound annual growth rate of about 25 per cent between FY26 and FY30. The company’s active user base in the segment is expected to expand as its penetration among women using premium smartphones rises from about 50 per cent in FY26 to nearly 60 per cent by FY30.
Premium smartphone ownership, defined as devices priced above Rs 30,000, is being used as an indicator for Nykaa’s high average order value customer base. Beauty and personal care active users could grow at about 21 per cent annually through FY30, supported by a wider premium device base, higher purchase frequency and increasing average order values.
Quick commerce’s share of online beauty and personal care spending is estimated to rise from about 16 per cent in FY26 to nearly 30 per cent by FY30. Specialist beauty platforms are expected to face less pressure than horizontal ecommerce marketplaces. Nykaa’s share of online beauty and personal care is projected to increase from 27 per cent in FY26 to about 32 per cent by FY30.
Make-up and skincare account for 69 per cent of spending on specialist platforms. Nykaa’s average order value in beauty and personal care stands at Rs 2,373, estimated to be about 3.5 times higher than that of other ecommerce platforms. This higher value could help the company absorb additional fulfilment costs as it expands Nykaa Now.
Nykaa was the first partner for about 55 per cent of the 112 beauty and personal care brands assessed since FY22. The company had more than 4,400 beauty and personal care brands and about 5,700 fashion brands on its platform as of FY26.
According to an Elara Securities report, FSN E-Commerce Ventures’ revenue is estimated to rise from Rs 10,022.4 crore in FY26 to Rs 21,294.3 crore by FY29. Reported profit is projected to increase from Rs 204 crore to Rs 1,421.6 crore over the same period, while earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation are estimated to rise from Rs 752.3 crore to Rs 2,321.9 crore.
The brokerage has retained its Buy rating on the company and raised its target price to Rs 475 from Rs 400, valuing Nykaa’s beauty and personal care segment at 75 times price-to-earnings and its fashion business at four times price-to-sales. a.title: From IPO mockery to Rs 1 lakh crore m-cap: Why investors are still betting on Lenskart’s vision
a.content:
Listen to this article in summarized format
The numbers made the valuation look even harder to digest. Even if Lenskart tripled its profits from that level over the next few years, the valuation would still work out to around 70x.
Retail investors did not hold back. The Rs 70,000-crore valuation quickly became fodder for social media. One X user calculated that with around 2,600 stores in India, each store was effectively being valued at around Rs 27 crore. The punchline: “Are they selling spectacles or diamond lenses?”
Another found the irony impossible to miss: “If Peyush Bansal pitched Lenskart’s valuation to Shark Tank’s Peyush Bansal, then he would have got rejected.”
Another drew comparisons with a familiar list of expensive IPOs: “To all the people who missed the lessons from Mamaearth, Paytm & Nykaa, don’t worry, here’s your latest chance.”
And yet, the market delivered an answer of its own
Fast-forward to 2026. Lenskart shares are up 50% so far this year. The company now commands a market capitalisation of Rs 1.15 lakh crore. The same stock that was mocked for being too expensive has continued to attract investors.
The reason, according to analysts, is increasingly less about the IPO valuation and more about what Lenskart is becoming.
Domestic brokerage Elara Capital believes Lenskart has built one of India’s most differentiated retail models by creating a full-stack eyewear ecosystem spanning the entire value chain. The brokerage draws a parallel with Titan Company Limited’s jewellery business, arguing that Lenskart could steadily compound market share gains and emerge as the category-defining leader in eyewear, much as Tanishq did in jewellery.
And Lenskart’s own numbers suggest that the company is not simply trying to sell more spectacles. It is building an eyewear business that spans everything from a Rs 500 pair of glasses to Rs 30,000 progressive lenses.
In its shareholders’ letter, the company said it had reached its largest-ever number of customers in “Real Bharat” with Rs 500 glasses, including lenses and warranty, sold profitably through Hustlr Club. At the other end of the spectrum, glasses with high-end Rodenstock and Tokai lenses, including progressive lenses priced at Rs 30,000, generated around Rs 250 crore in annual sales.
Then there is Owndays. Lenskart said glasses with premium Owndays lenses generated more than Rs 1,500 crore in annual sales, despite the business not having a presence in India two years ago.
The international story is also beginning to look different. Lenskart said its international business grew 38%, with an EBITDA margin before Ind AS 116 crossing 10%. The company believes the question is no longer whether the international business can work, but how far it can scale.
With Owndays, Lenskart now has one of Asia’s most respected brands. Meller, meanwhile, was a $35 million brand and is on track to become a $70 million brand.
What’s working for Lenskart?
1) Strong business model
At the heart of the Lenskart thesis is a model designed to reinforce itself as it grows. Elara points to revenue productivity of nearly Rs 25,000-30,000 per square foot, high gross margins driven by the company’s private-label-led model and an industry-leading store payback period of around 10-12 months.
But perhaps more important is whether Lenskart can keep bringing customers through the door. It can. The company is reporting same-store sales growth (SSSG) of 20%, which Elara sees as a key differentiator. Revenues across Tier I and Tier II markets are also nearly equal, suggesting that Lenskart’s growth is not dependent solely on India’s largest cities.
2) Full-stack retail infrastructure
According to Elara, Lenskart's advantage extends beyond its stores. The company has built a customer acquisition funnel around free eye testing while continuing to invest in technology to improve the customer experience. Its technology-enabled remote testing capabilities allow it to conduct nearly 600 eye tests per store every month.
The ambition is significantly larger. Lenskart is targeting 100 million eye tests over time, compared to the 23.7 million eye tests conducted in FY26.
Its backward integration has also moved beyond simply cutting costs. Elara Capital sees it as a strategic competitive advantage that gives Lenskart greater control over products, faster inventory turnover and next-day delivery across 78 cities.
That combination matters because it links the company’s stores, manufacturing and technology into one system, strengthening both customer experience and margin resilience.

Buy, sell or hold Lenskart shares?
Jefferies has maintained its Buy rating on Lenskart and raised its target price to Rs 680. The brokerage said Q1FY27 further strengthens the company’s growth and margin expansion story. Market creation remains a key priority, with supply rather than demand emerging as a constraint in India, reflected in around 70,000 daily eye tests.
Lenskart has also strengthened its presence at the lower end with a fully loaded Rs 500 product, while premiumisation is emerging as another growth driver. Jefferies believes improving margins in the international business should address a key investor concern and sees potential for Meller to become the “Ray-Ban of the future.”
Morgan Stanley has an Overweight rating and a target price of Rs 666. The brokerage said Lenskart delivered another quarter of strong performance in Q1, with the beat driven largely by the international business. Strong performance, optimistic management commentary, and higher earnings estimates support its expectation of continued stock outperformance.
Goldman Sachs has an Accumulate rating and raised its target price to Rs 715. The brokerage said the growth and margin flywheel continues to deliver, pointing to significant margin expansion in the international business while SSSG remains elevated.
In India, Goldman Sachs sees volume-led revenue growth and operating leverage-driven margin expansion. It also identifies premiumisation as a new growth vector for the company.
Macquarie has an Outperform rating and raised its target price to Rs 675. The brokerage said India’s Q1 performance was in line with expectations, while the international business beat estimates on stronger margin expansion.
Macquarie remains positive on strong volume growth, continued premiumisation across lenses and frames, the attractive Rs 500 entry-level offering, and the potential for more than 10,000 stores in India. Stronger international margins have led to a 4% upgrade to its EPS estimates and an 8% increase in the target price.
For Lenskart, the market’s biggest shift may not be in its valuation, but in what investors are willing to believe about its future. The company has moved beyond being just an organised eyewear retailer, with a model that now spans value eyewear, premiumisation, eye testing, backward integration, and an expanding international business.

a.title: Nykaa Plans To Boost GMV 2.5-3 Times And EBITDA 4-5 Times By FY30
a.content:
Nykaa Plans To Boost GMV 2.5-3 Times And EBITDA 4-5 Times By FY30
Nykaa targets a 2.5-3x increase in overall GMV and a 4-5x expansion in EBITDA by FY30. Additionally, the company aims to deliver 90% of all orders on the same or next day across India's 19,000 pin codes by FY30, demonstrating its commitment to logistically outpacing competition.
Market snapshot: FSN E-Commerce Ventures (Nykaa) has mapped out an aggressive FY30 strategic roadmap, targeting multi-fold expansion in its key operational and financial metrics. The company aims to leverage its dominant beauty business while scaling its fashion and omnichannel operations to achieve rapid profitability.
Data Snapshot
- Consolidated Revenue from Operations increased 29.10% YoY to ₹2,782 cr in Q1 FY27.
- Consolidated Net Profit (PAT) increased by 226% YoY to ₹80 cr in Q1 FY27.
- Operating EBITDA grew 67.79% YoY to ₹236 cr, with the operating margin expanding by 196 bps to 8.48% in Q1 FY27.
- The company targets overall GMV expansion of 2.5-3 times by FY30.
- The company plans to scale its consolidated EBITDA by 4-5 times by FY30.
- Nykaa aims for 90% of orders to be delivered on the same or following day by FY30.
What's Changed
- Consolidated Net Profit surged to ₹80 cr in Q1 FY27, up from ₹24 cr in the same quarter last year (Q1 FY26).
- EBITDA margin expanded by 196 bps to 8.48% in Q1 FY27 from 6.53% in Q1 FY26.
Key Takeaways
- Nykaa is aiming for a massive scale-up by FY30, targeting 2.5-3x GMV growth and a 4-5x increase in EBITDA, demonstrating a focus on high operating leverage.
- The company's delivery efficiency strategy targets completing 90% of its orders on the same or next day across its entire 19,000 pin code network by FY30.
- Recent quarterly earnings (Q1 FY27) confirm this margin trajectory, with PAT surging 226% YoY to ₹80 cr and operating margins hitting an 8.48% high.
SAHI Perspective
Nykaa's ambitious FY30 roadmap highlights a strong focus on margin expansion and operating leverage. By targeting EBITDA growth (4-5x) that outpaces GMV expansion (2.5-3x), the company plans to transition from a market-share acquisition phase to highly profitable scale. The rapid rollout of 'Nykaa Now' (quick-delivery service) across major cities will be crucial to meeting the 90% same-day/next-day shipping goal without diluting unit economics.
Market Implications
The long-term roadmap provides valuation comfort to institutional investors who have raised concerns over high stock valuations. However, achieving 90% next-day delivery across 19,000 pin codes will require significant capital expenditures in regional warehousing and logistics infrastructure, which could weigh on near-term cash flows if not managed efficiently.

Market Bias: Bullish
Nykaa is exhibiting robust operational strength, as evidenced by a 226% YoY surge in Q1 FY27 PAT to ₹80 cr and an ambitious FY30 roadmap targeting 4-5x EBITDA growth.

FY26 Financial Performance
The beauty and lifestyle retailer demonstrated significant operating leverage in FY26.
