Its portfolio includes milk, ghee, dahi and paneer under Gowardhan, while Go offers products such as cheese, UHT milk, buttermilk, lassi and flavoured milkshakes. The company also operates Pride of Cows, a premium farm-to-home dairy brand.
Avvatar represents its sports nutrition business and focuses on whey protein products. With the addition of popped chips, the company is now extending the brand into everyday snacking.
The move signals Parag Milk Foods’ attempt to build a broader nutrition portfolio where protein can be consumed across different parts of the day, from specialised sports nutrition to convenient snacks.
“Our ambition is to build a holistic protein ecosystem that brings together nutrition, convenience and accessibility across formats and lifestyles,” Shah said.
She added that entering snacking is “a strategic step towards creating a larger, more contemporary food and nutrition business with protein at its core.”
The House of Rare, the company behind fashion brands Rare Rabbit, Rareism, Rare’Z and Rare Ones, is ramping up its growth plans through an aggressive retail expansion strategy, new category launches and a stronger omnichannel presence across India.
The fashion retailer is aiming to achieve revenue of nearly Rs 1,600 crore in the current fiscal year, marking a significant increase from Rs 1,100 crore recorded in the previous year. The growth target comes as the company continues to expand its physical footprint and diversify its product portfolio across multiple fashion segments.
Launched over a decade ago with the introduction of Rare Rabbit, The House of Rare has evolved into a multi-brand fashion platform covering menswear, womenswear, kidswear and sneakers. The company currently operates 210 stores across its portfolio and plans to increase the count to at least 285 stores by the end of this fiscal year. An additional 50 outlets are expected to be added in the following year.
Rare Rabbit continues to be the company’s largest business segment, contributing around 70-72 percent of overall revenue. Womenswear brand Rareism accounts for nearly 20 percent, while Rare’Z and Rare Ones together contribute approximately 8-9 percent.
As part of its diversification efforts, The House of Rare is entering several new product categories, including fragrances, women’s handbags, open footwear, ballerinas, heels, belts and jewellery. The fragrance range is scheduled to launch next month. Meanwhile, its men’s innerwear label, Innerv, already contributes about 3 percent of Rare Rabbit’s menswear business and is being scaled further.
Currently, The House of Rare has a presence across more than 1,100 points of sale. Around 97 percent of its outlets are company-owned and company-operated. Its stores typically span between 1,100 and 1,200 square feet, with capital expenditure averaging Rs 3,400-3,500 per square foot. Metro cities and Tier I markets contribute roughly 60-65 percent of total revenue, though the company sees substantial growth opportunities emerging from Tier II and Tier III cities.
Offline channels remain the primary revenue source, accounting for around 60 percent of total sales, while online channels contribute the remaining 40 percent. The average selling price online ranges between Rs 1,600 and Rs 1,800, whereas the average order value in physical stores stands at approximately Rs 4,500-5,000.
The company has also reported strong customer growth, with its customer base expanding by nearly 50 percent this year. Repeat customers currently account for around 40 percent of total shoppers.
Allied Blenders and Distillers Ltd (ABDL) is planning to enter the single malt whisky segment with an investment of up to Rs 115 crore. The company’s Management Committee has approved the additional capital infusion into its subsidiary, Minakshi Agro Industries LLP (MAILLP).
The investment will be used to set up a malt distillery-cum-maturation warehouse in Aurangabad, Maharashtra. The proposed facility is expected to have an annual production capacity of around 3 million bulk litres and is targeted to be commissioned by the third quarter of FY28.
The proposed facility will support ABDL’s planned entry into the provenance-led single malt whisky category. The company said the investment forms part of its broader strategy to expand its presence in premium spirits.
“The proposed investment is aligned with the Company's long-term strategic vision of expanding and strengthening its premium spirits portfolio through entry into the provenance-led Single Malt Whisky segment,” the company said.
The move comes as Indian consumers have shown growing interest in premium and luxury spirits, with domestic single malt brands gaining greater visibility in recent years. ABDL currently has a portfolio spanning whisky and other spirits and is seeking to add a new category to its business.
Alongside the Rs 115 crore investment, the company has approved an additional capital contribution of up to Rs 10 crore for previously approved projects under MAILLP.
The additional funding will address cost overruns linked to a bottling unit and a distillery. According to the company, the increase in project costs is partly due to higher prices of key metals. A marginal expansion of the bottling hall and mezzanine area is also planned to accommodate longer automated bottling lines.
ABDL is the company behind brands including Officer’s Choice and has operations across the Indian spirits market. The company is also present in international markets and exports to 39 countries, according to the company filing.
The Aurangabad facility is expected to add manufacturing capacity for single malt whisky once commissioned. The investment will also mark ABDL’s entry into a segment that requires longer maturation periods and dedicated production infrastructure.
With the proposed investment and ongoing capacity projects, the company is expanding its manufacturing base while adding premium categories to its spirits portfolio.

a.title: After Nykaa, Zee initiates music copyright fight with Blinkit
a.content:
Zee Entertainment Enterprises Limited has sued quick commerce platform Blinkit for allegedly using its copyrighted content on Instagram, court documents accessed by MediaNama show. The case could have wider implications for the commercial use of music on Instagram, given that Zee and Eternal, Blinkit’s parent company, are both major listed companies in their respective sectors.
What is the dispute about? In a lawsuit filed in the Delhi High Court on July 27, Zee argued that Blinkit created “infringing works” and then uploaded them to its Instagram account.
- Zee also placed on record screen recordings of the alleged infringements posted by Blinkit on social media.
- While Zee’s licensing agreement with Meta allows individuals to use its music in Instagram posts for non-commercial purposes, platforms often use Zee’s licensed music in Instagram Reels to promote their products.
- It is unclear whether Blinkit had secured prior authorisation from Zee to use its copyrighted songs for commercial purposes.
What’s next? The Delhi High Court issued summons to Blink Commerce Private Limited, which operates as Blinkit.
- Justice Jyoti Singh also directed Blinkit to file a written statement within 30 days of receiving the summons, along with affidavits either admitting or denying Zee’s claims.
- The case will next be heard on August 27.
Why this matters: This is at least the third instance this year of a company being accused of infringing Zee’s copyrighted content. In April, Zee sued fashion and beauty retailer Nykaa for allegedly using its copyrighted songs in Instagram Reels to promote its products without permission. The dispute is ongoing, and Zee is seeking damages of approximately Rs 2 crore over Nykaa’s alleged unauthorised use of its music.
Last month, the Delhi High Court passed a John Doe order directing Meta to remove several Facebook URLs hosting Zee’s copyrighted content.
Earlier this year, Zee also filed a commercial suit against rival JioStar in the Delhi High Court, alleging the unauthorised use of its sound recordings across digital platforms and satellite TV channels. The lawsuit alleges that JioStar continued to use Zee’s music content even after the licensing agreement between the two parties had expired.
Zee itself is also facing allegations of copyright infringement. In May, JioStar initiated legal action against Zee Entertainment for allegedly broadcasting 12 Bollywood films to which it holds the rights without permission. In its lawsuit, JioStar accused Zee of being a “habitual infringer”, claiming that it continues to “engage in the unauthorised broadcast and exploitation of the films”.

a.title: Sun Pharma: Credit Rating Reaffirmed at AAA Stable

Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited has announced that CRISIL Ratings has removed the ‘Rating Watch with Developing Implications’ status from the company’s long-term bank facilities. The top-tier rating of ‘CRISIL AAA’ has been reaffirmed with a stable outlook. This follows an earlier communication on May 7, 2026, where the rating was placed under watch. Credit Rating Update for Sun Pharma
Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited today announced an update on its credit rating. Following a review, CRISIL Ratings Limited has removed the ‘Rating Watch with Developing Implications’ status that was previously placed on the company’s long-term bank facilities.
Reaffirmation of ‘CRISIL AAA/Stable’ Rating
The agency has reaffirmed the rating assigned to Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited’s long-term bank facilities at the highest category, ‘CRISIL AAA’. Crucially, the rating now carries a ‘Stable’ outlook. This reassures investors about the company’s robust financial health and its ability to meet its financial obligations.
Background of the Rating Watch
This development is in reference to a prior communication dated 07 May 2026. At that time, CRISIL had reaffirmed the ‘CRISIL AAA’ rating but had placed it on ‘Rating Watch with Developing Implications’. This action was triggered by the company’s announcement on 27 April 2026, the implications of which have now been assessed, leading to the removal of the watch and the stable outlook.

a.title: Nykaa Q1FY27 Net Profit Surges 226% to ₹80 Crore on Strong Revenue Growth
a.content:
Nykaa Q1FY27 Net Profit Surges 226% to ₹80 Crore on Strong Revenue Growth
Nykaa reported a 226% YoY jump in Q1FY27 net profit to ₹80 crore, with revenue up 29% to ₹2,782 crore and EBITDA rising 68% to ₹236 crore at an 8.5% margin — the highest in 12 quarters. The fashion segment turned EBITDA positive, and Nykaa acquired a 51% stake in Aminu Wellness to strengthen its premium skincare portfolio.
*this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only.
FSN E-Commerce Ventures Limited, operating as Nykaa, reported a significant surge in profitability for the first quarter of FY27, driven by accelerated revenue growth and margin expansion. The company's consolidated net profit after tax (PAT) rose 226% year-on-year to ₹80 crore, up from ₹23.3 crore in Q1FY26. This sharp improvement in bottom-line performance reflects enhanced operational efficiency and scale across its beauty and fashion verticals.
Financial Performance Highlights
Nykaa's total revenue from operations grew 29% year-on-year to ₹2,782 crore in Q1FY27, compared to ₹2,155 crore in the corresponding period last year. Gross profit expanded by 33% to ₹1,276 crore, while EBITDA increased by 68% to ₹236 crore. The EBITDA margin widened to 8.5% from 6.5% a year ago, marking the highest level in the past 12 quarters. Consolidated gross merchandise value (GMV) also climbed 34% to ₹5,590 crore.
The improvement in EBITDA margins indicates that Nykaa has successfully scaled its business while managing costs more effectively. Falguni Nayar, Executive Chairperson and CEO, attributed this to disciplined execution and innovation-led consumer experiences.
Business Verticals Update
The Beauty vertical remained the core driver, with GMV reaching ₹4,105 crore and net sales value (NSV) growing 29% year-on-year. Key launches included Rare Beauty, SK-II, and Judydoll, strengthening the premium portfolio. Nykaa Fashion delivered a standout performance with GMV rising 53% to ₹1,471 crore and NSV increasing 54% to ₹451 crore. Notably, the fashion segment turned EBITDA positive, achieving a 0.1% margin compared to a -6.2% margin in Q1FY26.
Acquisition of Aminu Wellness
In a strategic move to expand its House of Nykaa portfolio, Nykaa acquired a 51% majority stake in Aminu Wellness Private Limited. Aminu, a premium dermocosmetic skincare brand founded in 2019 by Prachi Bhandari and Aman Mohunta, has grown revenues eightfold over three years to reach ₹19 crore in FY26. The brand is profitable and known for its science-first approach and proprietary formulations. Post-acquisition, the founders will continue to manage operations, with Nykaa planning to acquire the remaining stake over the next few years on pre-agreed terms. This deal reinforces Nykaa's leadership in the premium skincare segment by integrating Aminu's R&D capabilities with Nykaa's omnichannel reach.
What the Numbers Show
The divergence between revenue growth (29%) and net profit growth (226%) highlights a significant leverage effect from operational efficiencies. With EBITDA margins hitting a 12-quarter high at 8.5%, Nykaa is demonstrating that its scale is translating into meaningful profitability rather than just top-line expansion. The turn to positive EBITDA in the fashion segment further signals improving unit economics across key growth drivers.

a.title: Nykaa says quick delivery isn’t hurting margins as Q1 profit jumps 226%
a.content:
Bengaluru: Nykaa said on Tuesday its rapid-delivery beauty offering Nykaa Now has achieved sufficient scale without hurting profitability, with higher purchase frequency and steady basket sizes offsetting the higher costs of quick commerce, as the company looked to ease investors’ concerns around the economics of the format. The service has expanded to 13 cities from just 3 a year earlier and is expected to reach 25 cities by the end of fiscal year 2027 (FY27), supported by Nykaa's network of 324 stores across 105 cities that serve as hyperlocal fulfilment hubs. Nykaa Now currently offers more than 1,000 beauty and personal care brands, according to the company’s investor presentation. “We don’t think this will be dilutive. The increase in purchase frequency and average order values staying consistent are offsetting the increase in fulfillment costs,” Anchit Nayar, chief executive of Nykaa Beauty, told analysts on Tuesday. “Despite Nykaa Now having become meaningful over the past several quarters, we’ve still shown improvement this quarter.” The comments came as FSN E-Commerce Ventures Ltd, Nykaa's parent, reported a 226% year-on-year jump in consolidated net profit to ₹80 crore in the June quarter, driven by accelerating growth across its beauty and fashion businesses as years of investment in assortment expansion and omnichannel retail began translating into stronger profitability. Revenue from operations rose 29% year-on-year to ₹2,782 crore in the quarter ended 30 June, while gross merchandise value (GMV) grew 34% to ₹5,590 crore. Ebidta (Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization) increased 68% to ₹236 crore, with Ebitda margin expanding to 8.5% from 6.5% a year earlier. Nykaa’s beauty business posted 29% year-on-year growth in net sales value (NSV) to ₹2,371 crore, while fashion grew 54% to ₹451 crore, aided by customer additions, a broader brand portfolio and its partnership with Nike. Fashion also reported positive Ebitda of ₹40 lakh, compared with a loss of ₹18 crore a year earlier, marking its first Ebitda-positive quarter. Beauty Ebitda rose 48% to ₹244 crore, with margin improving to 10.3% from 9%. Management attributed the broad-based growth to a combination of stronger consumer demand and sustained execution. “There’s no single reason. It’s a combination of a good market, strong execution and continuing to build the right platform, marketing and technology,” Nykaa’s founder, executive chairperson and chief executive Falguni Nayar said. Executives said continued customer acquisition, premiumisation, brand partnerships and technology-led improvements in merchandising and personalisation helped Nykaa outpace the broader market. The fashion business also continued to benefit from its strategic partnership with Nike, although management said the underlying platform—not the partnership alone—was driving growth. “We still retain our guidance of growing the fashion business three to three-and-a-half times over the next four to five years. The numbers you are seeing are largely reflective of the underlying platform’s growth,” said Abhijeet Dabas, chief executive of Nykaa Fashion. The company also highlighted improving marketing efficiency, with repeat customers accounting for a growing share of sales. “We are now seeing a higher share of revenue come from repeat customers,” Anchit Nayar said, adding that improved targeting and a stronger assortment had lowered customer acquisition costs, particularly in fashion. During the quarter, Nykaa’s consumer base grew 33% year-on-year to 60 million, while it added more than 160 brands across beauty and lifestyle, taking its portfolio to over 10,000 brands. It also opened 11 new stores, ending the quarter with 324 outlets across 105 cities, while its portfolio of owned brands grew 43% year-on-year. Management said the September quarter is likely to remain the strongest because of festive demand, although beauty remains less dependent on seasonal shopping than many discretionary categories because much of demand comes from everyday-use products. Separately, the board approved the acquisition of a 51% stake in Aminu Wellness Pvt. Ltd. for up to ₹32 crore to strengthen Nykaa’s premium skincare portfolio. The Mumbai-based company said Aminu’s premium dermocosmetic positioning, proprietary formulations and in-house research and development capabilities would strengthen its House of Nykaa portfolio, which currently spans 13 consumer brands. Founded in 2019, Aminu manufactures and sells skincare products across salons, clinics and direct-to-consumer channels. The company reported FY26 revenue of ₹19.4 crore, up from ₹8.4 crore three years earlier, and has built a portfolio of more than 30 products with over 30 proprietary formulations. Nykaa said it would acquire the remaining 49% stake over the next few years under the terms of the transaction, while Aminu’s founders, Prachi Bhandari and Aman Mohunta, would continue to run the business. The transaction is expected to close in the second quarter of FY27, subject to regulatory approvals. The strong top-line performance indicates that consumer spending remained resilient during the quarter, with the company continuing to benefit from its premium product portfolio, growing online customer base and expanding offline presence.

Nykaa delivered a notable improvement in operating performance during the June quarter. Gross profit increased 33% year-on-year to Rs 1,276 crore, while EBITDA rose 68% compared with the same period last year to Rs 236 crore.

As the company continued investing in growth initiatives, its overall expenditure also increased during the quarter. Total expenses stood at Rs 2,662.15 crore, compared with Rs 2,120.56 crore in the year-ago period and Rs 2,535.80 crore in the previous quarter.
The higher spending largely reflects continued investments in expanding retail operations, technology infrastructure, logistics capabilities and customer acquisition as Nykaa scales its omnichannel ecosystem.

The company continued to strengthen its offline presence during the June quarter by opening new retail stores across multiple cities. Nykaa's beauty retail network expanded to 324 stores spread across 105 cities, while its total retail area increased 29% year-on-year to approximately 3.3 lakh square feet.
The expansion forms part of the company's broader omnichannel strategy, which combines its digital platform with a growing network of physical stores to enhance customer experience and improve product accessibility across India.

Nykaa also continued scaling its quick-commerce platform, Nykaa Now, as consumer demand for faster deliveries gained momentum. The service is currently operational in 13 cities, and the company plans to extend its reach to more than 25 cities by the end of FY27.

a.title: Nykaa Q1 Results: Net profit surges over threefold to  ₹80 crore on strong beauty demand
a.content:
Nykaa's parent, FSN E-Commerce Ventures Ltd., reported a more than three-fold jump in its June quarter profit, driven by strong growth in its beauty business and a sharp acceleration in fashion sales, while improved cost efficiencies boosted its operating performance. The company posted a 226% year-on-year (YoY) jump in consolidated net profit to ₹80 crore in the April-June quarter, according to its regulatory filing released on Tuesday. Consolidated revenue from operations rose 29% YoY to ₹2,782 crore during the quarter. At the operating level, EBITDA increased 68% YoY to ₹236 crore, while the EBITDA margin expanded 200 basis points to 8%. The strong quarterly performance was primarily driven by sustained demand for skincare and makeup products. Revenue from the beauty segment rose 27.4% YoY to ₹2,516 crore in the June quarter. The beauty vertical's gross merchandise value (GMV) grew 28% YoY to ₹4,105 crore, supported by continued momentum across its e-commerce platform, offline retail network, and owned brands under the House of Nykaa portfolio. Meanwhile, net sales value (NSV) increased 29% YoY, accelerating from the mid-20% growth recorded over the past few quarters. House of Nykaa continued its strong growth trajectory, achieving an annualised GMV run rate of around ₹3,758 crore, reflecting 39% YoY growth. The portfolio reported NSV of ₹550 crore in the quarter, up 36% YoY, while expanding its customer base to more than 18 million, highlighting strong consumer demand and continued brand adoption. Nykaa's fashion business also delivered a strong performance during the quarter, with GMV rising 53% YoY to ₹1,471 crore, while NSV increased 54% YoY to ₹451 crore. The segment also reported a meaningful improvement in profitability, with the EBITDA margin (as a percentage of NSV) improving to 0.1% from 6.2% in the year-ago quarter. According to the company, the growth was supported by strong customer additions, with the cumulative customer base expanding 34% YoY to 12 million. The company also strengthened its brand portfolio and strategic partnerships, including Nike and H&M, which continued to support the segment's growth. Momentum remained broad-based across both core and emerging categories. Women's fashion grew 40% YoY, while men's fashion surged 83% and kidswear rose 57%. During the quarter, the company said it added more than 130 new brands, including Birkenstock, Debenhams, and H&M Move, further strengthening its product offerings. Meanwhile, its partnership with Nike continued to gain traction, with the Nike app crossing 1.5 million installs within six months of launch, making it one of the top three brands on Nykaa's platforms. a.title: Nykaa Q1 FY27 revenue rises 29%
a.content:
Nykaa Q1 FY27 revenue rises 29%
Nykaa's beauty business remained the company's largest growth engine, with gross merchandise value reaching Rs 4,105 crore during the quarter
Published: Aug 4, 2026 7:05 PM | 4 min read
- Nykaa reported a 29% year-on-year increase in revenue to Rs 2,782 crore and a 226% rise in net profit to Rs 80 crore for Q1 FY27, driven by growth in its beauty portfolio and premium brand launches.
- The company highlighted the success of its AI-led shopping experiences and omnichannel expansion, with significant contributions from new brand launches such as Rare Beauty and SK-II.
- Nykaa's beauty business achieved a gross merchandise value of Rs 4,105 crore, while its fashion segment saw a 53% increase in GMV to Rs 1,471 crore, aided by partnerships with brands like Nike and H&M.
- The retailer expanded its offline presence to 324 beauty stores and announced the acquisition of a 51% stake in premium skincare brand Aminu to enhance its portfolio in the premium skincare segment.
Nykaa began FY27 with its fastest growth in three years, reporting a 29 per cent year-on-year increase in revenue from operations to Rs 2,782 crore and a 226 per cent jump in net profit to Rs 80 crore for the quarter ended June 30. The beauty and lifestyle retailer said the quarter was driven by momentum across its beauty portfolio, premium brand launches, AI-led shopping experiences and omnichannel expansion.
For marketers, the quarter underscored Nykaa's continued focus on premiumisation, exclusive global partnerships, technology-led consumer engagement and offline expansion, while strengthening its portfolio through the acquisition of premium skincare brand Aminu.
Speaking on the results, Falguni Nayar, Executive Chairperson, Founder and CEO of Nykaa, said, "This quarter marked continued acceleration in our growth momentum and EBITDA margins, both reaching their highest levels in the last 12 quarters. Our platform featured exciting new brand launches like Rare Beauty, one of the world's largest celebrity beauty brands, already among the top five premium brands at Nykaa, SK-II, a Japanese high efficacy brand, and Judydoll, among our first Chinese beauty brands which is witnessing strong early traction among consumers. This also marks our first full quarter of operating nike.in in India, which has led to meaningful increase to our already growing fashion business."
She added that the company's AI-led initiatives are beginning to improve customer experiences, with Virtual Closet delivering two-times higher conversion rates while AskNykaa, its conversational search platform, is emerging as a trusted beauty advisor for shoppers.
Nykaa's beauty business remained the company's largest growth engine, with gross merchandise value reaching Rs 4,105 crore during the quarter. The company expanded its premium portfolio through exclusive launches including Rare Beauty, SK-II, Judydoll, K18 and Dr. Reju-All, further strengthening its position as a preferred launch partner for international beauty brands entering India.
The retailer also accelerated its quick commerce strategy. Nykaa Now has expanded to 13 cities and is expected to reach more than 25 cities by the end of FY27, enabling deliveries within 30 to 60 minutes across more than 1,000 beauty and personal care brands.
Offline retail continued to be a key part of the company's omnichannel strategy. During the quarter, Nykaa expanded its network to 324 beauty stores across 105 cities and opened its largest Nykaa Luxe outlet at Ambience Mall, Vasant Kunj, featuring more than 80 premium brands alongside experiential beauty services.
Its owned brands business, House of Nykaa, continued to scale with an annualised GMV run rate of approximately Rs 3,758 crore, supported by strong innovation across Dot & Key, Kay Beauty and Nykaa Cosmetics. New product launches contributed between 20 per cent and 40 per cent of revenues for the company's top three beauty brands during the quarter.
Nykaa's B2B platform, Superstore by Nykaa, also expanded its reach, reporting GMV of Rs 336 crore while growing its retailer network to more than 523,000 registered retailers across over 1,200 cities. The platform added brands including Sebamed, Minimalist, Deconstruct and Yoga Bar during the quarter.
The fashion business also reported strong momentum, with GMV rising 53 per cent year-on-year to Rs 1,471 crore. The company attributed growth to customer acquisition, the addition of more than 130 brands and partnerships with Nike and H&M. Nykaa said Nike crossed 1.5 million app installs within six months of launch and is now among the top three brands on its platform. Meanwhile, Virtual Closet, launched in May, has generated more than 200,000 virtual avatars while delivering two-times higher conversion among users.
Beyond organic growth, Nykaa announced the acquisition of a 51 per cent stake in premium dermocosmetic skincare brand Aminu. Founded in 2019, the brand has grown eight-fold over the past three years and is profitable. Nykaa said the acquisition will strengthen its House of Nykaa portfolio and deepen its presence in premium science-backed skincare, with the founders continuing to lead the business.
Commenting on the acquisition, Adwaita Nayar, Co-founder and Executive Director of Nykaa and CEO of House of Nykaa, said, "At Nykaa, we are building the House of Nykaa, a portfolio of distinctive brands that are redefining beauty for the Indian consumer. Aminu is a natural addition to that vision. Its premium positioning, loyal following, and genuine R&D depth make it more than an acquisition, it's a capability addition to our ecosystem."

Nykaa Q1 profit jumps 227 per cent as revenue nears Rs 2,800 crore
Marketing spend rises to Rs 412 crore as beauty retailer balances growth with profitability
MUMBAI: Beauty may be skin deep, but Nykaa’s latest numbers suggest the real glow-up is happening on the balance sheet. With bigger marketing bets and sharper margins, the beauty retailer is proving that spending to grow doesn’t have to come at the cost of profits.
Nykaa, operated by FSN E-Commerce Ventures Ltd, kicked off FY27 with robust top-line growth and a sharp improvement in profitability, even as it stepped up investments in advertising and customer acquisition to strengthen its position in India’s fast-growing beauty and fashion e-commerce market.
For the quarter ended June 30, 2026, the company reported revenue from operations of Rs 2,782 crore, up 29 per cent from Rs 2,155 crore a year earlier and 5 per cent higher than Rs 2,648 crore in the previous quarter.
Gross profit rose 33 per cent year-on-year to Rs 1,276 crore, with gross margins expanding to 45.9 per cent, compared with 44.6 per cent in the corresponding quarter last year and 45.4 per cent in the March quarter.
Marketing remained one of the company’s biggest areas of investment. Advertising, marketing and selling & distribution expenditure increased 26 per cent year-on-year to Rs 412 crore, up from Rs 328 crore in the year-ago quarter and 8 per cent higher than the Rs 380 crore spent in the preceding quarter.
Despite the increased spending, marketing costs became more efficient relative to revenue. Marketing expenditure accounted for 14.8 per cent of revenue, lower than 15.2 per cent a year ago, although marginally higher than 14.4 per cent in the previous quarter, indicating that revenue growth continued to outpace promotional investments.
Nykaa also delivered stronger operating performance. Contribution profit climbed 37 per cent year-on-year to Rs 589 crore, while the contribution margin improved to 21.2 per cent, compared with 19.9 per cent a year earlier.
EBITDA surged 68 per cent to Rs 236 crore, with EBITDA margin expanding by 196 basis points to 8.5 per cent, up from 6.5 per cent in the corresponding quarter last year. Sequentially, EBITDA increased 3 per cent from Rs 223 crore, while margins edged up from 8.4 per cent.
At the bottom line, profit after tax (PAT) jumped 227 per cent year-on-year to Rs 80 crore, compared with Rs 24 crore in the same quarter last year. Sequentially, profit remained largely stable against Rs 79 crore reported in the March quarter.
Profit before tax nearly tripled to Rs 129 crore, while the PAT margin improved to 2.9 per cent, up from 1.1 per cent a year earlier.
Commenting on the performance, Falguni Nayar, Executive Chairperson, Founder and CEO of Nykaa, said crossing the US$1 billion annual revenue milestone while maintaining profitability and capital efficiency marked a defining moment in the company’s 14-year journey.
She noted that over the past three years, Nykaa has evolved into a multi-engine growth platform, with its Beauty and Fashion businesses doubling their gross merchandise value (GMV), while newer verticals such as Superstore and House of Nykaa have grown four-fold during the same period.
The company now serves more than 55 million consumers, with Nayar highlighting artificial intelligence as a key enabler for improving personalisation, operational efficiency and scalability across its businesses. She also identified wellness as Nykaa’s next major growth frontier alongside its core beauty and fashion operations.
The strong quarterly performance builds on FY26, when Nykaa crossed the US$1 billion annual revenue mark, reporting Rs 10,022 crore in revenue, 59 per cent growth in EBITDA and 183 per cent growth in net profit, making it the company’s strongest full-year profitability performance to date.

a.title: Nykaa To Acquire Majority Stake In D2C Skincare Brand Aminu
a.content: Beauty and personal care (BPC) major Nykaa’s board of directors has approved a 51% stake acquisition of D2C skincare brand Aminu for a cash consideration of up to ₹32 Cr. As per exchange filings, the transaction is expected to be completed by September 15. The company later said that it will acquire the remaining 49% over the next few years. Moreover, the company said Aminu’s founders will continue running the business while Nykaa will support it to scale. Founded in 2019 by Prachi Bhandari and Aman Mohunta, Aminu retails skincare products including serums, cleaners, sunscreen, masks, moisturisers and other body care products across 60 SKUs. The startup also offers free skin consultation services. Its products are priced in a more premium category, a segment where Nykaa is trying to expand in. In a post-earnings call today, Nykaa noted that Aminu’s portfolio products feature a higher price point than existing skincare brands in the House of Nykaa, filling the premium skincare gap. Apart from the seven year old business’ premium positioning, Nykaa also seeks to benefit from its strong R&D to build in-house scientific skincare capabilities, with its over 30 proprietary formulations. Nykaa also highlighted the startup’s omnichannel distribution capabilities as it retails its products on its own website, BPC marketplaces like Nykaa and Clinikally, along with Amazon, Zepto. Notably, it is available at 180 salons across the country, giving Nykaa an entry point into the retail channel. The bootstrapped-startup reported a revenue of ₹19.4 Cr in FY26, up about 50% YoY from around ₹13 Cr earned in FY25. As per Aminu’s website, it sources ingredients for its skincare products from over 40 countries, and features over 250 total ingredients across its product portfolio. It also claims to use only clean, skin friendly ingredients, having eliminated almost 3,000 such popular ingredients from its products. In the past, Nykaa has fully or partially acquired a number of BPC brands to place them under its house of brands strategy. This includes brands like Dot & Key and Earth Rhythm. The company is trying to build portfolios across product categories and price points under the house of brands strategy. Nykaa currently houses 7 BPC and 5 fashion brands, including its own Nykaa Cosmetics brand. The company noted today that it will continue to scale the House of Brands, outlining expansion opportunities in categories like premium fragrances, mid-premium nutraceuticals, derma-led skincare and products for professional make-up artists. Alongside approving the acquisition, Nykaa’s board also cleared the company’s financial performance for the first quarter of FY27. In the quarter, Nykaa reported an over 3X jump in its consolidated net profit for Q1 FY27 to ₹79.8 Cr from ₹24.8 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Meanwhile, its operating revenue jumped 29% YoY and 5% QoQ to ₹2,782 Cr. Shares of Nykaa ended today’s trading session 0.85% higher at ₹344.80.

Nykaa also expanded its premium beauty portfolio with launches including Rare Beauty, SK-II, Judydoll, K18 and Dr Reju-All. “During the quarter, Nykaa also unveiled its largest-ever Nykaa Luxe store at Ambience Mall, Vasant Kunj, spanning over 5,000 sq ft housing 80+ brands, the flagship store features immersive beauty experiences, dedicated shop-in-shop formats for elevated brand representation, and experiential services designed to enhance customer discovery and gratification," the company said. Nykaa Fashion Turns EBITDA Positive Nykaa Fashion sustained its strong growth momentum in Q1 FY27, with GMV surging 53% YoY to ₹1,471 Cr and NSV rising 54% to ₹451 Cr. The business turned EBITDA positive for the first time, reporting an EBITDA margin of 0.1%, aided by a richer brand portfolio, customer acquisition and operating leverage. The company added more than 130 brands during the quarter across categories such as activewear, footwear and kidswear. Nykaa also cited encouraging traction from its partnership with Nike, under which it operates nike.in and the Nike App in India. a.title: Sun Pharma’s premium push cushions US generics pain in Q1, but valuations look full
a.content:
Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd's June quarter (Q1FY27) performance was steady rather than spectacular. Consolidated revenue rose 10% year-on-year to ₹15,183 crore, outpacing the company's high single-digit growth guidance for FY27. Yet management stuck to its guidance.
The quarter highlighted Sun Pharma's continued shift towards higher-margin businesses. Strong growth in India formulations and innovative medicines more than offset weakness in the US generics business.
India formulations, which contributed 36% of Q1 consolidated revenue, was the fastest-growing segment. Sales rose 16% year-on-year to ₹5,475 crore, led by cardiovascular (CVD), central nervous system (CNS) and gastro-ortho therapies. Around 40% of the growth came from higher volumes and 20% from new launches, indicating healthy prescription gains.
Sun Pharma introduced five products in India during the quarter, and strengthened its GLP-1 market position, becoming the second-largest player in generic injectable semaglutide and the only Indian company offering a semaglutide auto-injector.
Its innovative medicines portfolio also maintained strong momentum. Revenue increased 12.8% year-on-year to $351 million, accounting for 21.9% of total sales. Growth was broad-based across the US and international markets, driven Ilumya, Odomzo and Cequa.
The innovative medicines business also supported growth in emerging markets, where revenue rose 15.4% year-on-year to ₹2,945 crore, or 19.4% of consolidated sales. However, in dollar terms, emerging market revenue grew only 4%, slowing from 13.6% in FY26. Management attributed the moderation to geopolitical disruptions and challenging macroeconomic conditions in certain countries.
The US formulations business remained the weak spot. Revenue fell 9.7% year-on-year to $427 million, hurt by lower generic sales following continued erosion in Lenalidomide and increased competition in certain products. Even so, management said Leqselvi continues to gain traction, with prescriptions and the number of prescribing physicians increasing each month.
Margin outlook
Profitability reflected these cross-currents. Consolidated Ebitda margin contracted 133 basis points year-on-year to 28.1%, mainly due to lower foreign-exchange gains, higher spending on new product launches and acquisition-related costs. But for the high lenalidomide contribution in the base quarter, management indicated that underlying Ebitda margin would have improved. Gross margin expanded 95 basis points to 80.5%, led by a richer product mix with a higher contribution from innovative medicines and branded generics.
The Organon acquisition is expected to close in Q4FY27. Management expects only a modest initial contribution given the mature nature of the acquired portfolio.
“Although Sun stands to benefit from Organon’s specialty platform over the medium term, with revenue and cost synergies likely to materialize gradually,” said JM Financial Institutional Securities. “The merger is also expected to enhance annual free-cash-flow generation to 2x by FY29. Beyond the integration, we believe the company's strategy is likely to increasingly focus on inorganic growth, as both businesses have limited organic growth drivers at their combined scale.”
In the domestic market, prescription growth, new launches and the expanding semaglutide portfolio should support market share gains.
“Strong domestic performance, Ilumya approval in psoriatic arthritis, growth in Unloxcyt and Leqselvi and Semaglutide launch in key markets are key growth drivers, before Organon M&A is completed,” said Nuvama Research.
The richer product mix should support gross margins going ahead. However, Ebitda margin could come under pressure from higher R&D spending, investments in innovative products, persistent weakness in US generics, and Organon’s acquisition-related costs.
Sun Pharma shares hit a fresh 52-week high of ₹2,046.90 on Friday, suggesting investors are capturing the optimism, for now. The stock trades at 35.5x its FY27 estimated earnings, as per Bloomberg.

Nykaa will acquire 51% stake in Aminu, a premium dermocosmetic skincare brand for a cash consideration of Rs 32 crore.
Omnichannel beauty and fashion retailer Nykaa has clocked a more than 3x rise in net profit and a 29% rise in revenue for the first quarter of the 2026-27 fiscal year, driven by overall demand.
The company reported a net profit of Rs 79.76 crore for the first quarter of FY27 compared to Rs 24.47 crore in the similar period a year ago. Revenue from operations was Rs 2,782 crore compared to Rs 2154.94 crore registered a year earlier.
Falguni Nayar, Founder, Executive Chairperson, and CEO said, "This quarter marked continued acceleration in our growth momentum and EBITDA margins, both reaching their highest levels in the last 12 quarters.”
Consolidated gross merchandise value (GMV) touched Rs 5,590 crore for the first quarter, at a 34% YoY growth. EBITDA grew 68% YoY to reach Rs 236 crore during the quarter.
The beauty segment, which accounts for 90% of Nykaa’s revenue, grew 27.3% YoY. The fashion segment revenue grew 48% on a YoY basis though on a smaller base.
However, the fashion segment continued to report EBITDA losses, which stood at Rs 8.52 crore for the quarter, while the beauty segment registered a positive EBITDA of Rs 159.10 crore.
Long-term value creation
Meanwhile, Nykaa will acquire 51% stake in Aminu, a premium dermocosmetic skincare brand for a cash consideration of Rs 32 crore. The company said the acquisition is a natural extension of its innovation-led, consumer-first approach.
Founded in 2019 by Prachi Bhandari, Aminu reported a revenue of Rs 19.44 crore for FY26 and is profitable. Nykaa said it will acquire the remaining stake over the next few years on pre-agreed terms.

a.title: Nykaa: Q1FY27 Revenue Grows 29% to ₹2,782 Cr, PAT Surges 226%
a.content:
FSN E-Commerce Ventures Limited (Nykaa) reported robust financial results for Q1FY27, with Net Revenue growing 29% YoY to ₹2,782 Crore. Profit After Tax (PAT) witnessed a significant surge of 226% YoY, reaching ₹80 Crore. The company highlighted strong performance across its Beauty and Fashion verticals, driven by increased GMV, customer acquisition, and strategic initiatives.
Nykaa Reports Strong Q1FY27 Financial Performance
FSN E-Commerce Ventures Limited (Nykaa) has announced its financial results for the first quarter of FY2027 (ended June 30, 2026), showcasing substantial growth across key financial metrics. Net Revenue from operations increased by 29% YoY to ₹2,782 Crore, marking the highest growth in the last 13 quarters. The company’s Profit After Tax (PAT) demonstrated remarkable improvement, surging by 226% YoY to ₹80 Crore.
Key Financial Highlights for Q1FY27
- Net Revenue: Grew by 29% YoY to ₹2,782 Cr.
- EBITDA: Increased by 68% YoY to ₹236 Cr, with an EBITDA margin of 8.5%.
- PAT: Surged by 226% YoY to ₹80 Cr, with a PAT margin of 2.9%.
- Gross Profit: Rose by 33% YoY to ₹1,276 Cr.
- Gross Merchandise Value (GMV): Achieved ₹5,590 Cr, a growth of 34% YoY.
Performance Across Verticals
The company’s business verticals, Beauty and Fashion, both contributed significantly to the growth. The Beauty vertical saw a 29% YoY increase in Net Sales Value (NSV), while the Fashion vertical reported a strong 54% YoY growth in NSV. Nykaa’s strategic focus on expanding its brand assortment, enhancing customer experience, and strengthening its omnichannel presence continues to drive these positive results.
Strategic Initiatives and Future Outlook
The investor presentation also highlighted key strategic initiatives including the expansion of its retail footprint with 11 new stores in Q1FY27, the successful launch of premium brands like Rare Beauty, and advancements in AI initiatives. The company’s acquisition of a 51% stake in Aminu further strengthens its position in the premium skincare segment. Nykaa remains focused on driving sustainable growth and profitability through continued innovation and strategic partnerships.

a.title: How Nykaa is building an owned-media empire
a.content:
ADVERTISEMENT
For most retailers, advertising is a cost centre. For Nykaa, it is increasingly becoming the product itself. Nykaa has assembled one of India's largest consumer-media ecosystems, with an audience that rivals some of the country's biggest digital publishers.
The numbers tell the story. Nykaa's beauty platform attracted 1.89 billion visits in FY26, drew 44.7 million monthly average unique visitors and served 19.7 million annual transacting customers. Its cumulative customer base has crossed 55 million, growing 31% year-on-year.
At that scale, Nykaa is no longer merely an e-commerce marketplace selling lipstick, skincare and fragrances. It is becoming an owned-media company with commerce attached.
Also read: Nykaa partners OpenAI to bring beauty, fashion catalogue into ChatGPT
From shelf space to screen space
Traditionally, beauty brands paid retailers for physical shelf space.
Today, they are paying for attention.
The company constantly refers to the intersection of commerce, content and community—a signal that content is no longer an ancillary function but a core growth engine.
Nykaa's influence extends far beyond transactions. Every product review, tutorial, influencer collaboration and recommendation creates media inventory that brands can tap into.
For global beauty players entering India, Nykaa increasingly offers distribution and access to millions of engaged consumers.
The audience is becoming the moat
Nykaa's business model is beginning to resemble that of a digital publisher.
The company added more than 200 beauty brands in FY26, including luxury labels such as Chanel Beauty, Armani Beauty, Kylie Cosmetics and SK-II. Overall, the platform now hosts more than 10,000 brands across beauty and fashion.
But unlike traditional retailers, Nykaa owns the consumer relationship.
It knows what consumers search for, what they buy, which creators they follow, what trends they engage with and how often they return.
That data advantage is transforming the company into a media platform capable of selling not just products, but discovery itself.
The rise of beauty intellectual property
Nykaa is investing heavily in proprietary experiences that look less like marketing campaigns and more like media franchises.
Properties such as Nykaaland, Nykaa Beauty Awards, Nykaa Luxe Weekender, Get Ready With Nykaa and Nykaa Academy are designed to keep consumers engaged long after a purchase.
These initiatives reveal a fundamental shift in marketing philosophy.
Traditional retailers spend on advertising to drive transactions. Nykaa is building intellectual property that generates recurring attention, engagement and loyalty.
The objective is not simply to sell products; it is to own the cultural conversation around beauty.
Read: Nykaa appoints Ankit Jain to lead quick commerce vertical NYKAA NOW
Creators are replacing commercials
For decades, beauty advertising in India was dominated by television campaigns and celebrity endorsements.
Nykaa is betting on a different future—one powered by creators, communities and experiences.
The company says it is deepening engagement with younger consumers through campus ambassador programmes, experiential activations and community-led initiatives. Consumer discovery is increasingly taking place on Instagram reels, YouTube tutorials and influencer content rather than in front of television screens.
That changes the economics of advertising.
Media budgets are moving away from thirty-second commercials towards creator partnerships, social commerce and immersive experiences.
In the next decade of beauty, the companies that win may not be the ones with the most products. They may be the ones that own the audience.

a.title: Lenskart and Old Chang Kee serve up curry puff-inspired eyewear for National Day
a.content:
Singapore’s National Day collaborations have taken a deliciously unexpected turn this year, with Lenskart partnering with homegrown snack brand Old Chang Kee on a limited-edition eyewear collection. Bringing together contemporary eyewear and one of Singapore’s most recognisable local flavours, the playful capsule collection features three exclusive frame designs, a curry puff-inspired spectacle pouch and a dangling Curry’O charm.
It is a collaboration that sounds unusual on paper, but somehow makes perfect sense. Old Chang Kee’s golden curry puffs have long been part of everyday life in Singapore, while eyewear is an equally familiar daily essential. The collection blends both worlds through subtle references to the heritage snack brand rather than turning the glasses into novelty accessories.
Three designs inspired by local favourites
The Lenskart x Old Chang Kee collection includes three frame styles: the Black Full Rim Square, Black Full Rim Round and Silver Full Rim Geometric.
The Black Full Rim Square features a black frame with gold-lined detailing designed to evoke the warm tones of a freshly wrapped curry puff. It is completed with Old Chang Kee’s Curry’O icon for a small but instantly recognisable finishing touch.
For those who prefer a rounder silhouette, the Black Full Rim Round incorporates etched patterns of the Curry’O and fishball icons across the frame. The design is a light-hearted tribute to the familiar snacks that have been enjoyed by generations of Singaporeans.
The most eye-catching option is the Silver Full Rim Geometric, which comes with a dangling curry puff charm. Inspired by the pleated, hand-folded appearance of Old Chang Kee’s signature snack, the charm transforms the curry puff into a surprisingly wearable keepsake.
While the details are playful, the frames remain practical enough for daily wear. This makes the collection suitable for anyone who wants to mark the National Day season without committing to an overly loud or costume-like accessory.
The curry puff case may steal the show
The frames are not the only reason fans may be tempted by the collaboration. Every pair comes with a specially designed spectacle pouch inspired by the shape and colouring of a curry puff, along with a microfibre cloth. The soft pouch is arguably the collection’s most conversation-starting item and looks more like a plush local-food collectible than a conventional glasses case.
It is a fitting addition for a collaboration built around nostalgia. Rather than simply placing both brand logos on a standard product, the collection uses recognisable details from Old Chang Kee’s visual identity to create something that feels distinctly Singaporean. Each pair from the collection is priced at S$150 and is available at Lenskart stores across Singapore and online.
Catch the roving pop-up across Singapore
To celebrate the launch, Lenskart is also bringing a roving pop-up experience to four shopping malls across Singapore from 31 July to 30 August 2026. The pop-up begins at Lenskart’s newly opened flagship store at Suntec City before moving to VivoCity, Jurong Point and Eastpoint Mall.
The schedule is:
Suntec City: 31 July to 9 August
VivoCity: 10 to 16 August
Jurong Point: 17 to 23 August
Eastpoint Mall: 24 to 30 August
At each stop, visitors can view the collection at a themed push cart, take part in interactive activities and enjoy selected Old Chang Kee treats. Customers who purchase from the collection can also experience a “live cooking” demonstration. Meanwhile, the first 30 customers who complete an eye test each day will receive a complimentary S$2 Old Chang Kee voucher. A lucky wheel offering prizes and additional vouchers will also be available.
A nostalgic way to celebrate Singapore
Food-inspired fashion collaborations are often designed to attract attention, but this one works particularly well because Old Chang Kee is closely connected to everyday Singapore life. Established in 1956, the homegrown snack brand has grown from a single coffeeshop stall into a familiar name with more than 100 outlets across Singapore. Its curry puffs remain an affordable comfort food for office workers, students, commuters and families alike.
By turning those familiar flavours and visual cues into wearable details, the collection offers a cheeky but affectionate celebration of local culture. a.title: Sun Pharma maintains FY27 growth outlook, says Organon deal remains on track
a.content:
5 Min Read
Mumbai-based Sun Pharmaceutical Industries remains confident of delivering high single-digit revenue growth of 6-9% in FY27, with its innovative medicines portfolio, specialty business and new product launches expected to support growth.
Jayashree Satagopan, Chief Financial Officer of Sun Pharma, said it is too early to assess the potential impact of proposed US tariffs on generic medicines, noting that the company will continue engaging with the US administration and industry stakeholders.
She added that Sun Pharma's existing manufacturing footprint in the US provides strategic flexibility should policy changes materialise.
Satagopan also said the proposed Organon acquisition remains on track for completion in the last quarter of the current financial year, subject to regulatory approvals.
On the outlook for its innovative medicines business in FY27, Sun Pharma said it remains focused on expanding the portfolio, although it did not provide a specific growth target. The company expects products launched late last year to make a stronger contribution this year, while noting that growth will vary across markets depending on local dynamics.
In the April-June quarter (Q1FY27), Sun Pharma reported revenue of ₹15,299 crore, net profit of ₹2,894 crore, and a margin of 28.90%.
These are edited excerpts from the interview.Q: The company has maintained its FY27 revenue growth guidance of 6-9%, despite delivering 10% growth this quarter.
A: For the full year, we expect revenue growth to remain in the 6-9% range. One should also factor in the impact of foreign exchange fluctuations. We have seen rupee depreciation compared with last year, and that should be considered while evaluating the full-year performance.
A: We do not provide specific margin guidance. However, our endeavour is always to maximise margins to their fullest potential.
Q: What is the latest update on the Organon acquisition? Shareholders have approved it. Is the transaction still expected to close by early 2027?
A: Yes. Shareholders approved the transaction at their meeting on July 23. All the required regulatory filings across several countries have been completed. We remain on track to receive the approvals in a timely manner, and the last quarter of this financial year remains our target for closing the transaction.
Q: The US is debating tariffs on generic drugs and onshoring pharmaceutical manufacturing. How do you assess this as a risk to Sun Pharma?
A: The announcement came about a week ago regarding the additional tariffs that could be imposed on generics, possibly a couple of years from now. We need to assess the likely impact. There is still a long time between now and then. Sun Pharma will be engaging with the administration independently and along with our partners in the pharma industry. In my view, it is a little too early to comment on it. At the same time, we do have manufacturing facilities in the US for both technical operations and formulations, so we will evaluate the situation at the appropriate time.
Q: How does the Organon portfolio fit into the company's US strategy? Does its manufacturing presence help offset tariff concerns?
A: Organon's manufacturing is primarily in Europe and countries like Brazil and Mexico, not in the US. Therefore, the recent tariff announcement is unlikely to provide any benefit. Having said that, in the US, primarily they are into innovative medicines in the women's healthcare segment and biosimilars. These are complementary to Sun's existing portfolio.
Q: What about Organon's portfolio itself being impacted by Trump's policies on branded drugs and the most-favoured-nation pricing proposal?
A: Organon is still a separate listed company, so we are not in a position to comment on it at this point.
Q: How did the base generics business perform in the US, considering pricing pressure and the absence of Revlimid generic sales? What is the outlook?
A: One of the reasons the US generics business declined this quarter was the absence of Revlimid-related revenue. We launched five new generic products in the US and will continue introducing more products in that market. Pricing pressure remains a reality in the generics business and is expected to continue. We have seen this trend over the past few years, and we do not expect it to change in the coming quarters. Our focus is to introduce newer products while continuing to grow our innovative medicines business in the US.
Q: How did the global innovative medicines portfolio perform? What was the performance of drugs such as Unloxcyt and Leqselvi?
A: The overall business grew 12.8%, driven by both the US and international markets. We launched Leqselvi and Unloxcyt in the US, and both are tracking well in terms of formulary access and prescriptions. Prescriber feedback has been positive, and patient response, particularly for Leqselvi, has been encouraging. As of June 2026, Leqselvi had crossed 1,000 prescriptions. Unloxcyt is also progressing well. Since this is the first year of launch, we expect these products to continue gaining momentum over the coming months and quarters.
Q: Levulan saw an impact during the quarter. What happened?
A: It was a seasonal impact. The decline was quarter-on-quarter rather than year-on-year. Compared with the March quarter, the June quarter saw a slight decline, which is a normal seasonal trend.
Q: What is your outlook for the innovative medicines business in FY27?
A: While I cannot provide a specific growth percentage, our objective is to continue growing the innovative medicines portfolio. Different markets have different dynamics. We also have two products that were launched late last year, and they should contribute more meaningfully this year.

a.title: Sun Pharma voluntarily recalls 11 eyedrops from domestic market, experts seek details
a.content:
Drugmaker Sun Pharmaceutical Industries has undertaken a voluntary recall of 11 of its ophthalmic products in the domestic market. While the voluntary action is appreciated, public health experts are calling for transparency, including specifics on why the eyedrops were recalled, and for regulatory intervention and advisories for those who may have used the drops.
“We have initiated a proactive voluntary withdrawal of some ophthalmic products as a matter of abundant precaution. Product quality and patient safety are important to us and remedial measures have been put in place,” a Sun Pharma spokesperson told businessline. Details were not provided on the remedial measures, the reasons behind the recall, or the locations where the products were manufactured.
Santanu Tripathi, a senior clinical pharmacologist, told businessline, the voluntary recall by the company, “perhaps due to quality/contamination concerns,” was appreciated. However, the company needed “to exercise greater transparency and clearly spell out the specific reason behind this recall decision.”
The recall needs to be supplemented with “in-parallel, pro-active role by the regulators, particularly at the State Drugs Control levels, in regard to enforcing prompt cessation of sale and distribution of the products with specified batch/lot numbers,” he said.
In public interest, he asked, “what about the preparations already sold/dispensed and are being used by the patients at households, at clinics and hospitals? Should this information not be widely circulated among practising ophthalmologists, hospital administrators and hospital stores managers, nurses, and patients at large such that they too stop further use of these products.”
Patients who may have already used these products need to be contacted to check whether they experienced adverse reactions, and if so, whether it has been reported, he said. “In cases there is a causal association with use of such products, the concerned patients must be compensated. Regulators must act promptly, and investigate into the matter,” he added.
Helpline for consumers
An industry insider said the drugmaker had informed the drug regulatory authority, and that a helpline would be instituted for consumers to check their eyedrops. Some Mumbai-based chemists, when contacted, said they had not yet received information on the voluntary product recall.
According to industry tracker Pharmatrac, for the 12 months to June 2026, the ophthalmology segment was pegged at ₹4,721 crore, with the eyedrops segment accounting for a lion’s share at ₹3,521 crore.
Troubled segment
Eye drop concerns appear to be a recurring problem area, said an industry insider, pointing to two Indian drugmakers that recalled their eye drops in the United States (2023) due to quality issues.
In November 2023, Kilitch Healthcare voluntarily recalled 27 eyedrop products from the United States after the US Food and Drug Administration flagged unsanitary conditions. In February 2023, Chennai’s Global Pharma Healthcare voluntarily recalled its Artificial Tears Lubricant Eyedrops, distributed by EzriCare LLC and Delsam Pharma. The action followed the US Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) investigations into drug-resistant infections possibly linked to contaminated eyedrops, they then said.

a.title: Sun Pharma recalls multiple eye drops in India over contamination concerns
a.content:
Sun Pharma recalls multiple eye drops in India over contamination concerns
According to reports, Sun Pharma has recalled multiple eye drop products in India after contamination concerns and has stopped their distribution as a precautionary measure. Experts advise patients not to continue using the affected products or stop treatment without consulting their eye doctor.
According to reports, pharmaceutical maker Sun Pharma has recalled multiple eye drop products in India after contamination concerns emerged during manufacturing. The company has also halted the distribution of the affected products and asked distributors across the country to immediately stop supplying them and return all available stock as a precautionary measure.
The development came to light after a confidential letter issued by Sun Pharma Distributors Ltd to its distributors, accessed by ANI, instructed them to withdraw several ophthalmic products from the market. The company said it had decided to discontinue further distribution and recall all existing stocks of the affected eye drops available in the distribution channel.
The products listed for withdrawal include Depopred 2 ml, Brinolar (BKC Free), Brinzotim Eye Drops 5 ml BKC Free, Lotepred-5 ml, Lotepred 1% Eye Drops, Lotepred LS 0.2%, Lotepred T, Nepalact OD Eye Drops 3 ml, Nepalact-Z, Toba-F and Nepalact Eye Drops 5 ml.
According to the communication, distributors have been directed to immediately stop billing the recalled products, provide details of any remaining stock and return all available units, including those received from other sources, on priority.
Responding to ANI, a Sun Pharma spokesperson said patient safety remains the company's highest priority. The spokesperson said all necessary steps have been taken in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements and that teams are working to restore the availability of the products so patients continue to have access to appropriate treatment options.
The recall has raised concerns among patients who use these medicines for a range of eye conditions, including glaucoma, eye infections, allergies, ocular inflammation and recovery after eye surgery. Since many of these conditions require regular treatment, patients may be worried about whether they should continue using the medicines or stop them immediately.
Experts, however, caution against making treatment decisions without consulting an ophthalmologist. According to the report, patients should neither continue using a recalled eye drop nor discontinue treatment on their own. Instead, they should contact their treating eye specialist as soon as possible so that a safe and suitable alternative can be prescribed without interrupting treatment.
The report also highlights that maintaining sterility during the manufacturing of eye drops is critical because these medicines are applied directly to the eye. Even suspected contamination at a manufacturing facility can pose a serious risk to patient safety, making product recalls an important precautionary measure.
While the recall is precautionary, it serves as a reminder of the importance of strict quality control in the production of ophthalmic medicines. Patients currently using any of the recalled products are advised to check the name of their medication and consult their ophthalmologist before making any changes to their treatment.

a.title: Sun Pharma recalls six eye drop brands from the Indian market as ‘precautionary measure’
a.content:
Sun Pharma recalls six eye drop brands from the Indian market as ‘precautionary measure’
The company has not disclosed the reason for the withdrawal. In a communication to its distributors, the company said the recall was “a precautionary measure”.
Synopsis: Sun Pharma has withdrawn six prescription eye drop brands from the Indian market and asked distributors to stop billing the products and return existing stocks. The company has not disclosed the reason for the withdrawal. The medicines are widely prescribed after eye surgery, particularly cataract procedures, to treat pain and inflammation.
Sun Pharma, the Mumbai-based pharma giant, has withdrawn six prescription eye drop brands from the Indian market. The recalled products are Nepalact OD, Nepalact, Nepalact-Z, Lotepred T, Lotepred LS and Lotepred 1%.
The drugs are routinely prescribed after eye surgery, particularly cataract procedures, which are among the most commonly performed surgeries in the country.
In a communication to its distributors, the company said the recall was “a precautionary measure” and instructed them to immediately cease billing the medicines, share details of existing inventory, and return all available stock, including products sourced through other channels.
The company has not disclosed the reason for the withdrawal. Its communication to distributors does not specify whether the action stems from a quality issue, a manufacturing concern, a regulatory requirement or another reason.
South First emailed Sun Pharma a detailed questionnaire seeking clarification on the withdrawal. The company had not responded at the time of publication.
Nepafenac and loteprednol are prescription medicines that require medical supervision.
The Nepalact range is generally prescribed to control pain and inflammation after cataract surgery. It contains nepafenac, a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) formulated as an ophthalmic suspension.
“Patients usually begin using the drops a day before surgery and continue treatment for two to three weeks afterwards, depending on the surgeon’s advice,” an ophthalmologist told South First.
They added that nepafenac is also prescribed to prevent and treat macular oedema after cataract surgery, especially in patients with diabetes, who face a higher risk of the complication.
The Lotepred range contains loteprednol etabonate, a corticosteroid used to suppress inflammation after eye surgery and in several inflammatory eye disorders.
“Loteprednol is commonly used after cataract and refractive surgeries, as well as in conditions such as uveitis and allergic conjunctivitis. The drops are usually prescribed several times a day for one to two weeks after surgery, with the dosage gradually reduced as inflammation improves,” the ophthalmologist said.
Lotepred T, in particular, combines loteprednol with tobramycin, an antibiotic, allowing doctors to treat inflammation while also providing antibacterial cover where required.
The formulations differ in steroid strength. Lotepred LS contains a lower concentration suitable for milder inflammation, while Lotepred 1% is reserved for more severe cases, enabling ophthalmologists to tailor treatment to individual patients.
“Steroid eye drops such as loteprednol can increase intraocular pressure if used for prolonged periods. Because of this, ophthalmologists periodically monitor eye pressure during treatment to reduce the risk of complications such as glaucoma,” the ophthalmologist said.

a.title: Sun Pharma to Acquire Organon Facility
a.content:
Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited signed a definitive agreement to acquire Organon & Co. in an all-cash transaction valued at an enterprise value of US$11.75 billion. Under the agreement, Sun Pharma will acquire all outstanding shares of Organon. The acquisition is expected to significantly strengthen Sun Pharma’s global presence across innovative medicines, women’s healthcare, branded generics and biosimilars, while expanding its footprint in key international markets.
Strategic Acquisition to Accelerate Global Growth
The proposed acquisition aligns with Sun Pharma’s long-term strategy of expanding its Innovative Medicines business and reinforcing its leadership in the Established Brands and Branded Generics segment. The transaction will enable Sun Pharma to enter the rapidly growing biosimilars market as one of the Top 10 global players. By integrating Organon’s portfolio, manufacturing capabilities and international commercial network, the company aims to accelerate sustainable growth and create long-term value for stakeholders.
Organon Brings Strong Global Portfolio
Organon was established in 2021 following its spin-off from Merck & Co., Inc. (known as MSD outside the United States and Canada). Today, the company operates as a global healthcare leader with a strong focus on women’s health. Its portfolio comprises more than 70 products spanning women’s health, general medicines and biosimilars, which are commercialised in over 140 countries. Organon’s largest markets include the United States, Europe, China, Canada and Brazil. The company also operates six manufacturing facilities across the European Union and emerging markets, providing a robust manufacturing and supply chain platform.
Enhancing Sun Pharma’s Global Healthcare Leadership
With the addition of Organon, Sun Pharma expects to strengthen its diversified healthcare portfolio while expanding access to high-quality medicines worldwide. The acquisition will combine Organon’s strong global brands, customer relationships and healthcare expertise with Sun Pharma’s manufacturing excellence, research capabilities and global commercial network. Together, the combined organisation aims to improve healthcare access, strengthen affordability and deliver innovative treatment solutions across multiple therapeutic segments.
A Transformational Opportunity
Dilip Shanghvi, Executive Chairman of Sun Pharma, said, “The transaction represents a significant opportunity for Sun Pharma to build on its vision of ‘Reaching People and Touching Lives’. Organon’s portfolio, capabilities and global reach are highly complementary to our own, and we believe bringing the two organisations together will create a stronger and more diversified platform. We have deep respect for Organon’s mission and look forward to building on its legacy while driving sustainable long-term growth.”
Kirti Ganorkar, Managing Director of Sun Pharma, described the acquisition as a strategic milestone in the company’s global expansion. “This transaction is a logical next step in strengthening Sun Pharma’s global business. Together, we will become a partner of choice for acquiring and launching new products. Our immediate priorities will be business continuity, disciplined integration and responsible value creation. We also see significant opportunities to leverage Organon’s talented workforce while unlocking meaningful revenue synergies over the coming years,” Ganorkar mentioned.
Organon Board Supports the Transaction
Carrie Cox, Executive Chair of Organon, said the agreement delivers immediate value to shareholders while ensuring long-term continuity for the company’s business. “Following a comprehensive review of strategic alternatives, our Board determined that this all-cash transaction offers compelling and immediate value to Organon stockholders. We believe Sun Pharma is well positioned to support Organon’s businesses, employees and patients globally, while continuing our commitment to delivering impactful medicines and healthcare solutions,” Cox said.
Expanding Global Footprint and Future Opportunities
The acquisition positions Sun Pharma to significantly strengthen its global healthcare business by expanding its presence in women’s health, biosimilars, innovative medicines and branded generics. As per the press release, Organon’s established international footprint, diversified product portfolio and manufacturing infrastructure are expected to complement Sun Pharma’s existing strengths. The combined company is well positioned to accelerate innovation, expand market reach and create sustainable long-term value for patients, healthcare providers, investors and other stakeholders worldwide.

a.title: Sun Pharma Partner Philogen Resubmits EMA Application for Melanoma Therapy Nidlegy
a.content:
Sun Pharma Partner Philogen Resubmits EMA Application for Melanoma Therapy Nidlegy
Mumbai: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited has informed the stock exchanges that its partner, Philogen S.p.A., has resubmitted the Marketing Authorization Application (MAA) for Nidlegy (Daromun) to the European Medicines Agency (EMA). The application seeks approval of the investigational therapy as a neoadjuvant treatment for adult patients with locally advanced, fully resectable melanoma.
According to the company, the resubmission follows the timelines previously communicated by Philogen and incorporates updated clinical evidence generated from the randomized Phase III PIVOTAL study. The revised dossier includes a longer median patient follow-up of 33 months, compared to 21 months in the earlier submission made in June 2024, along with additional post-hoc analyses focusing on event-free survival.
The updated application also contains additional Chemistry, Manufacturing and Controls (CMC) information intended to address questions raised during the previous regulatory review. Supporting evidence further includes efficacy and safety data from a Phase II melanoma study, safety data from the ongoing Phase III NeoDREAM study, and findings from a Phase II study evaluating the therapy in non-melanoma skin cancers.
In the PIVOTAL Phase III trial, Nidlegy demonstrated a reduction in the risk of relapse or death compared with the control arm, while its safety profile was mainly characterized by low-grade local adverse events, according to Philogen.
Commenting on the development, Prof. Dr. Dario Neri, Chief Executive Officer and Chief Scientific Officer of Philogen, said the company remains committed to advancing Nidlegy for melanoma and non-melanoma skin cancers.
Also Read: Sun Pharma Gets Interim Court Relief in Pantocid Trademark Dispute
“Since the previous MAA procedure, our team has worked intensively to address the clinical and CMC questions raised during the review. We are encouraged by the data generated to date and will continue working with our partners and regulators with the aim of bringing this innovative treatment to patients in need,” he said.
Philogen noted that Sun Pharma is its commercialization partner for Nidlegy in Europe, Australia, and New Zealand for the treatment of skin cancers.
Nidlegy is a proprietary biopharmaceutical product comprising two active components, L19IL2 and L19TNF, designed for intralesional administration. The investigational therapy is currently being evaluated in two Phase III clinical trials for locally advanced melanoma and Phase II studies in high-risk basal cell carcinoma and other non-melanoma skin cancers.
Currently, there is no approved neoadjuvant drug for the treatment of locally advanced, fully resectable melanoma, making the regulatory review of Nidlegy a significant development in this therapeutic area.
