Novartis India appoints Vikas Gupta as MD, CEO, signs key brand deals
Novartis India Limited has finalized its leadership transition by appointing Dr. Vikas Gupta as Managing Director and CEO and Bhagwat Singh Deora as CFO. The Board approved critical agreements with Novartis AG, including a royalty-free license for the Tegrital trademark and a five-year distribution deal, securing product continuity post-acquisition by the ChrysCapital consortium.
*this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only.
Novartis India Limited has completed its transition under new ownership by appointing Dr. Vikas Gupta as Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer and Bhagwat Singh Deora as Chief Financial Officer, effective July 29, 2026. The Board of Directors also approved critical commercial agreements with Novartis AG, including a royalty-free license for the Tegrital trademark and a five-year distribution agreement for pharmaceutical products, ensuring operational continuity after the ChrysCapital consortium acquired 70.68% of the equity share capital.
The appointments were made during the company’s 247th Board meeting held on July 29, 2026, in compliance with Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. Dr. Gupta, who initially joined as Additional Director and CEO, was immediately redesignated as Managing Director and CEO, subject to shareholder approval. Mr. Deora, a Chartered Accountant with over 20 years of experience in the pharmaceutical sector, joins from JB Pharma. These leadership changes follow the resignation of six outgoing directors, including former Chairperson Christopher David Snook and CFO Shilpa Shashank Joshi, as part of the governance restructuring triggered by the change in control.
Strategic Agreements and Brand Continuity
To secure its product portfolio post-acquisition, Novartis India executed three key agreements with Novartis entities on July 29, 2026. The most significant is the Tegrital Brand License Deed, which grants the company an exclusive, irrevocable, royalty-free, and non-assignable license to use the 'Tegrital' trademark in India. Under this deed, Novartis AG must automatically assign the trademark to the company at no additional cost, provided there is no material breach by the company. This ensures uninterrupted manufacturing, marketing, and sales of the Tegrital range of pharmaceutical products.
Additionally, the company signed a Distribution Agreement with Novartis Pharma Services AG, appointing it as the exclusive distributor to import and sell certain pharmaceutical products in India. This agreement has an initial term of five years, extendable by another five years subject to mutual consent. Supply prices are fixed for the first year, with subsequent pricing determined by a mechanism outlined in the contract. A separate Trademark Assignment and License Deed transferred ownership of other key brands, including Voveran, Macalvit, and Citromacalvit, to the company on a royalty-free basis.
Leadership and Committee Reconstitution
The new management team includes several senior appointments aimed at stabilizing operations and driving growth. Besides Dr. Gupta and Mr. Deora, the company appointed Jason D'Souza as President – M&A, Business Development & Investor Relations; Rahul Vijayvargiya as Chief Human Resource Officer; Masud Shaikh as Chief Supply Chain Officer; and Sumeet Rajput as President – Business Operations. All appointments took effect on July 29, 2026.
The Board also reconstituted its Risk Management Committee and Stakeholders Relationship Committee to align with the new director lineup. Shashank Sinha chairs the Risk Management Committee, while Ashok Bhatia leads the Stakeholders Relationship Committee. The company has adopted a new corporate email domain (nilpharma.co.in) and website to reflect its rebranding under the new management.
What the Numbers Show
The acquisition of 17,450,680 equity shares by the ChrysCapital consortium (WaveRise Investments Limited and ChrysCapital Fund X) solidifies their control with a 70.68% stake, reducing Novartis AG’s holding below the 10% threshold required for promoter classification. The execution of royalty-free brand licenses and long-term distribution agreements mitigates immediate revenue risks associated with the ownership transition, allowing the new management to focus on operational integration rather than renegotiating core supply chains. The appointment of experienced executives from major Indian pharmaceutical firms signals a strategy to leverage domestic market expertise for future growth.

a.title: Hidden risks of UPI Autopay: Nykaa AVP’s LinkedIn post sparks debate about free trials
a.content:
Lokesh Ahuja, AVP at Nykaa, has shared a cautionary story on LinkedIn. He recently taught his mother how to use UPI payments. He came across something that rang an alarm bell. Scrolling through her phone later, Ahuja spotted several AutoPay mandates. She unknowingly subscribed to multiple services through free trials. These offered zero cost during the initial 30-day period. However, they automatically charged users afterwards unless cancelled promptly. “And most people never notice a ₹79 deduction. Because it quietly disappears inside an account statement with a hundred other UPI transactions. That's the real product behind a free trial. Not the first free month,” he wrote. Lokesh Ahuja reflected on shifting parental concerns across generations. Parents once worried about children crossing roads safely. Now, children worry about their parents navigating the internet safely instead. “Strange how our parents once worried about us crossing the road. Now we worry about them crossing the internet,” he wrote. He later added, “Earlier, the biggest risk was buying the wrong thing. Today, it's agreeing to something you didn't fully understand. AutoPay mandates, app permissions, location access, recurring subscriptions.” According to Ahuja, they're all “tiny decisions” made in seconds. However, such decisions may trigger something for a longer period. “Digital literacy is no longer just about knowing how to use technology. It's also about knowing what you've agreed to,” he added. Lokesh Ahuja's LinkedIn post about hidden AutoPay mandates sparked wide engagement. One user agreed, calling free trials a “silent money drain” nationwide. Another user raised similar concerns regarding debit card charges. “Similarly, how many know that all banks provide debit cards and NOT the ATM cards, just because ATM cards are free, while Debit cards get charged about 800 to 1000 per annum. This is a pure theft, as over 60% of people use Debit Cards as ATM Cards only - they never do online transactions using Debit cards,” the user wrote. One user noted that payment pages would often redirect users to AutoPay. She calls it the “worst part” of the transaction. According to one user, people often notice deductions too late. “Even when people do notice, it's only when the transaction for the next month has already happened,” the user wrote. One user suggests automating reminders before trial periods actually end. Another user stresses the shift in generational trust around financial transactions. “The generation before us, our parents, worked on trust. You genuinely believed people and transacted. Our generation has grown up with mistrust. We are always looking around to see who will take us for a ride,” the user added. a.title: Smart Money Shift: FIIs Raised Stakes in 15 Large Caps as Lenskart Led the Buying
a.content:
Quick Snapshot
- FIIs raised holdings in 41 BSE largecap companies in the June 2026 quarter; 18 of them already have double-digit CY2026 gains, and 15 have full quarter-on-quarter FII disclosure with returns of 15%–49%.
- Lenskart Solutions saw the sharpest jump in foreign ownership, FII holding rose 850 basis points, from 4.26% to 12.76%, between March and June 2026.
- FIIs pumped over Rs 15,157 crore (~$1.8 billion) into Indian equities in the first weeks of July 2026, reversing roughly $30 billion in outflows from January–May, partly driven by money rotating out of AI-led rallies in Korea and Taiwan.
- Adani Power posted the biggest CY26 price gain at 49%, but its FII holding rose just 3 basis points — showing price momentum and institutional accumulation didn’t move together for every stock.
- IndusInd Bank’s Q1 FY27 net profit rose 72% year-on-year to Rs 1,037 crore as FII stake climbed to 29.17%, even as mutual fund holding eased over the same period, per Tijori Finance data.
- Q2 FY27 earnings, due from mid-October 2026, along with the AI-trade rotation and crude oil/rate trends, will be the next test for these flows.
FIIs Widen Bets on 15 Largecaps, but the Accumulation Story Is Elsewhere
FIIs increased their holdings in 41 BSE largecap companies during the June 2026 quarter compared with March 2026, according to ACE Equity data cited by ETMarkets. Of these, 18 companies have already delivered double-digit CY2026 returns, and 15 of them, the ones with full quarter-on-quarter FII disclosure, posted gains ranging from 15% to 49%.
A closer read of the same shareholding data shows the stocks with the biggest share-price rallies were not necessarily where FIIs added the most capital.
NiftyTrader Desk’s analysis of the underlying holding-percentage shifts shows Lenskart Solutions, Billionbrains Garage Ventures (Groww), and Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone (APSEZ) recorded the sharpest increases in FII ownership, a distinction that matters more for tracking institutional conviction than headline price gains alone.
Track live foreign and domestic institutional flows on the FII-DII Tracker.
Where FII Ownership Actually Rose the Most
Lenskart’s FII holding climbed 850 basis points, from 4.26% in March 2026 to 12.76% in June 2026 — the largest jump among the 15 stocks tracked. Independent shareholding trackers, including Kotak Neo, corroborate FII ownership in Lenskart at roughly 12.8% as of June 2026, close to the ACE Equity figure.
Groww’s parent, Billionbrains Garage Ventures, saw FII holding rise 438 basis points, from 2.51% to 6.89%, also broadly confirmed by Kotak Neo shareholding data at 6.9% for June 2026. APSEZ’s FII stake rose 233 basis points, from 13.25% to 15.58%, the third-sharpest increase in the group.
By contrast, Adani Power — the top price gainer at 49% YTD — saw FII holding inch up just 3 basis points (11.73% to 11.76%), and Adani Total Gas, up 15% YTD, saw a 2-basis-point rise. This gap between price performance and institutional stake-building suggests some of the year’s biggest rallies were driven more by retail and momentum buying than fresh FII conviction.
Why FIIs Turned Buyers in This Cohort
FIIs pumped more than Rs 15,157 crore, or roughly $1.8 billion, into Indian equities in the opening weeks of July 2026, according to NSDL data cited by Republic World — a sharp reversal after nearly Rs 2.3 lakh crore, or about $30 billion, in outflows between January and May.
Separate estimates from Jefferies put net FII buying at $1.8 billion through July 15, the first monthly net purchase since February, according to the brokerage’s Global Head of Equity Strategy Christopher Wood.
Wood attributed part of the reversal to money rotating out of AI-driven rallies in Korea and Taiwan and back into undervalued Indian largecaps, noting that a bigger, sustained return of foreign capital would require either the AI trade to cool further or Indian valuations to fall more sharply.
Separately, Republic World reported that blue-chip valuations had corrected 11%–15% from their highs, and that easing geopolitical risk and softer crude oil prices had also improved sentiment, citing Motilal Oswal Financial Services.
Company-specific catalysts played a role too. IndusInd Bank’s Q1 FY27 net profit rose 72% year-on-year to Rs 1,037 crore with improving asset quality, Outlook Business reported, and MD & CEO Rajiv Anand described the quarter as a “clear inflection point” after the bank’s 2025 accounting-lapse crisis, per Business Today.
Adani Ports handled 138.1 million tonnes of cargo in Q1 FY27, up 15% year-on-year, Business Today reported, supporting the stock’s FII accumulation. For Lenskart and Groww, both still within roughly a year of their public listings, rising FII stakes reflect growing institutional comfort with post-IPO earnings visibility.
Where DIIs Stand
Domestic institutional investors, mutual funds, insurers, and pension funds, have broadly continued to act as a buying cushion through 2026 via steady SIP and mutual fund inflows. However, DII behaviour within this specific 15-stock cohort was not uniform.
In IndusInd Bank’s case, mutual fund holding eased to 25.36% in the latest quarter from 27.55% previously, per Tijori Finance shareholding data, even as FII holding rose, pointing to a divergence between foreign and domestic fund managers on the stock’s recovery trajectory.

- Q2 FY27 earnings, due from mid-October 2026, will test whether IndusInd Bank’s recovery and Adani Ports’ cargo growth continue.
- Lenskart and Groww face post-listing lock-in expiries and valuation scrutiny as FII stakes climb from a low base.
- Adani Green Energy’s renewable capacity addition pace and PPA signings remain a watch point for sustaining its 37% YTD gain.

Bottom Line
The June 2026 quarter’s FII data offers more nuance than a simple list of price gainers. Lenskart, Groww, and Adani Ports saw the deepest institutional stake-building, while some of CY26’s biggest rallies, including Adani Power’s 49% run, saw barely any change in FII ownership.
With Q2 FY27 earnings, a still-fragile global rotation out of AI trades, and rate cues ahead, the direction of both FII and DII flows in this cohort will matter more than the headline returns already booked.

a.content:

Sun Pharma partner Philogen resubmits Nidlegy application in Europe
                    The revised application includes additional Chemistry, Manufacturing and Controls (CMC) information intended to address the outstanding questions raised during the previous procedure.
                                    
            
        
                    
                    
                    
                                        Mumbai: Sun Pharma’s supply partner Philogen has announced to have submitted an updated Marketing Authorization Application (MAA) to the European Medicines Agency (EMA). for the approval of onco-derma therapy, Nidlegy (daromun) in Europe.
The company is seeking approval for treatment of adult patients with locally advanced, fully resectable melanoma.
Compared with the MAA submitted in June 2024, the updated dossier carries longer median patient follow-up data of its pivotal Phase 3 trial (PHL19IL2TNF-02/15) of 33 months as opposed to 21 months and includes additional post hoc analyses focused on event-free survival.
Further it also includes additional Chemistry, Manufacturing and Controls (CMC) information intended to address the outstanding questions raised during the previous procedure.
Sun Pharma holds exclusive rights to commercialize the drug across Europe, Australia, and New Zealand. Under the agreement, the two companies will share post-commercialization profit on 50:50 basis..
Philogen is responsible for the product's clinical development, regulatory filings, and manufacturing. The Italy-based drugmaker had retained the drug’s IP ownership and option to explore it for indications other than skin cancers.
Financial terms of the licensing agreement were not disclosed by Sun Pharma at the time of the announcement in 2023.
“Since the previous MAA procedure, our team has worked intensively to address the clinical and CMC questions raised during the review. We are encouraged by the data generated to date and have launched additional registrational studies in non-melanoma skin cancers,” said Prof. Dr. Dario Neri, CEO Philogen.
Nidlegy is a targeted immunotherapy which contains two active ingredients — L19IL2 and L19TNF.
The L19 antibody binds to the Extra Domain B of Fibronectin, a protein expressed in tumors but absent in most healthy tissues and delivers the two pro-inflammatory cytokines— IL-2 and TNF directly to the tumor site to disrupt tumor cells growth and trigger immune response.
In the trial, patients treated with the drug after surgery, demonstrated 41 per cent lower risk of relapse or death compared with those who underwent surgery alone.
Nidlegy is investigated in two Phase 3 clinical trials for the treatment of locally advanced melanoma, and in Phase 2 clinical trials for the treatment of High-Risk Basal Cell Carcinoma and other non-melanoma skin cancers.
According to the Phase2 Duncan study topline results presented at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) in 2025, against basal cell carcinoma (BCC) and cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) – types of non-melanoma skin cancer — the drug reported complete pathological responses in 52.6 per cent of patients.

a.title: Nykaa appoints former Instamart COO Ankit Jain to lead NYKAA NOW
a.content:
Indian beauty retailer Nykaa has appointed Ankit Jain to lead NYKAA NOW, its quick-commerce business, as the company expands its fulfilment and supply-chain operations.

In his new role, Jain will oversee the expansion of NYKAA NOW across key markets and work to strengthen Nykaa’s fulfilment network through AI-led demand forecasting and logistics innovation.
NYKAA NOW promises delivery of beauty and personal-care products within 30 to 60 minutes. The service operates in 13 cities, including Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru and Kolkata.
Nykaa said it also planned to scale Nykaa Next Day and Nykaa Express as part of its wider fulfilment strategy.
Anchit Nayar, executive director and CEO of Nykaa Beauty, said customers increasingly expected “both speed and choice without compromise”.
“At Nykaa, we are building a differentiated fulfilment ecosystem powered by technology, AI and deep execution excellence. Ankit’s experience in scaling complex supply chain and quick commerce operations makes him uniquely positioned to help us strengthen our network, accelerate NYKAA NOW, and deliver exceptional customer experiences at scale,” he said.
Jain said Nykaa had built a strong foundation by combining consumer trust with innovation and technology.
“I am excited to join the company at a pivotal stage of its growth journey and look forward to building resilient, data-driven operations that enable greater speed, reliability and efficiency across the fulfilment network. Together, we have an opportunity to redefine beauty commerce by making the best beauty brands more accessible to customers across the country,” he said.

a.title: IGI Logo
a.content:
At the cusp of a growth inflection
Cyient DLM Ltd (CYIENTDL) is an emerging design-led electronics platform serving Aerospace & Defense, Industrial, MedTech, and Automotive end-markets (with AI data centers and robotics segments expected from FY27 onwards), positioned at the intersection of several technology and manufacturing megatrends. As global OEMs increasingly seek integrated partners capable of supporting products from development through commercialization and lifecycle management, CYIENTDL is well placed to capture a larger share of the electronics value chain.
* CYIENTDL is evolving from a traditional EMS vendor (PCBA+Box-Build) to a Buildto-Spec (B2S mix to increase from 6% in FY26 to double digits by FY28) and a platform-partner model, embedding itself across design, engineering, certification, manufacturing, and lifecycle support. This significantly increases switching costs and extends customer relationships from annual purchase orders to 10-15+ year program partnerships, enabling the company to capture a larger share of value across the electronics product lifecycle.
* Aerospace provides the foundation for this transformation, supported by:
a) record global aircraft backlogs (of 12 years)
b) multi-decade platform lifecycles
c) rising electronics content per aircraft
d) key B2S wins (such as Deutsche Aircraft's D328eco program and Skydrive’s eVTOL project) and platform partnerships (like Boeing 787), which provide long-duration revenue visibility and validate CYIENTDL's ability to participate in high-value, design-led manufacturing programs.
* Additionally, a substantial growth opportunity lies beyond Aerospace, with Industrial and Automotive emerging as the next growth pillars. Exposure to semiconductor equipment, AI infrastructure, clean energy, B2B smart metering, and EV electronics (BMS) positions CYIENTDL to benefit from multiple simultaneous, policy-supported capex cycles and the structural increase in electronics content across industrial and mobility platforms.
* Further, Altek (US acquisition) significantly strengthens CYIENTDL’s growth runway by providing:
a) a North American manufacturing footprint,
b) International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR)-compliant capabilities
c) access to high-value Industrial, MedTech, and Defense customers. Beyond revenue addition, the acquisition creates meaningful cross-selling opportunities and enhances CYIENTDL’s ability to offer global, dual-region engineering and manufacturing solutions.
* Overall, we like CYIENTDL from current levels as the base has normalized following the execution of the large BEL defense order (~32% of FY25 revenue but a low-margin order). Coupled with a strong 1.9x book-to-bill ratio (vs. 1.3x in FY25) and 41% growth in FY26 order inflows, this provides robust growth visibility. We expect CYIENTDL to deliver a CAGR of 27%/40%/67% in Revenue/EBITDA/Adj. PAT over FY26-28 and reiterate our BUY rating with a TP of INR 830, based on 41x FY28E EPS.
Business model transformation
* CYIENTDL's transformation extends beyond the shift from pure EMS to B2S. The company is evolving from a project-based manufacturer to a platform supplier participating across the entire product lifecycle (Product Design → Engineering → Qualification → Manufacturing → Lifecycle Support). The significance lies in transitioning from annual purchase orders to decadelong production programs, a model followed by global aerospace and industrial electronics suppliers (such as Plexus Corp and Sanmina).
* The company's SET (Strengthen-Expand-Transform) framework closely mirrors the evolution path adopted by global aerospace suppliers. The first phase focuses on deepening core OEM relationships (by FY26-27), followed by expansion into automotive, defense, robotics and AI-led opportunities through M&A and integration (by FY27-29). The final phase involves transitioning to a product- and platform-led model (by FY27-32) (Refer to Exhibit 5).
* The key evidence of this transition is the increasing contribution from B2S programs. While B2S contributed ~6% of FY26 revenue, we expect double-digit contribution by FY28. More importantly, several programs are still in the development stage and are likely to contribute materially after 2 years down the line, indicating healthy visibility of the growth pipeline.
* Unlike traditional EMS contracts, where customers can easily switch suppliers, B2S engagements embed CYIENTDL into product architecture, validation, and certification processes. In aerospace and industrial electronics, this often results in supplier relationships lasting for an entire platform lifecycle of 10-15 years (Refer to Exhibit 1).
* The company's recent engineering investments, dedicated testing infrastructure, and B2S labs indicate that management is strategically positioning CYIENTDL to capture a larger share of the growing electronics manufacturing market.
* Our research also indicates that platform-based OEMs globally seek fewer, but more capable, partners that can provide integrated design-to-manufacturing solutions.
* We believe the successful execution of this transformation could gradually shift CYIENTDL's margin profile from the current 9-11% to 13-14%.
Valuation and view
* CYIENTDL’s growth in FY26 was impacted by the execution of the large but lowmargin BEL defense order (32% mix of FY25 revenue). With this order now executed, the base has been normalized. Meanwhile, the company ended FY26 on a strong footing, with its order book increasing 27% YoY to INR24.2b and the book-to-bill ratio improving to ~1.9x (vs. 1.25x in FY25), providing healthy revenue visibility and laying the foundation for the next phase of growth.
* We believe the company’s growth trajectory will remain strong, backed by:
1) increasing contribution from higher-value B2S programs (double-digit contribution by FY28E)
2) a robust order pipeline reflected in a 41% growth in FY26 order inflows and a strong 1.9x book-to-bill ratio repeat above
3) the ramp-up of marquee aerospace platforms and new program wins (such as D328eco, Thales, Honeywell)
4) growing exposure to industrial, AI infrastructure, semiconductor equipment, clean energy, and automotive electronics
5) enhanced customer access and cross-selling opportunities through the Altek acquisition.
* We expect CYIENTDL to deliver a CAGR of 27%/40%/67% in revenue/EBITDA/Adj. PAT over FY26-28 and reiterate our BUY rating with a TP of INR 830, based on 41x FY28E EPS.

a.title: Quote of the day by Nykaa CEO Falguni Nayar: "My mindset was that before I turn 50 I had to start my own business, otherwise..."
a.content:
Falguni Nayar is the founder and CEO of Nykaa. She is a respected business leader and what many find remarkable is that she started the business when she was in her late 40s. For two decades, she worked as a investment banker and she left her high-flying career to finally take the entrepreneurial plunge. Nayar started Nykaa when she was near 50, proving that age is never a barrier to doing bigger and bolder things in life. She's a self-made entrepreneur who inspires so many people out there, especially women looking to take control of their financial and professional futures.
She once said, "My mindset was that before I turn 50 I had to start my own business, otherwise I will never do it. I was 48 at that time. Instead of seeing age as a handicap, I saw it as all the experience that came with it. My professional experience came in very handy. But entrepreneurship is also about learning new things. So I would like to tell women to please educate yourselves and be very open minded." An empowering quote indeed, let's decode what it really means.
What does the quote mean?
A lot of people believe that after a certain age, it is too late to start something new or take big career risks. Falguni Nayar’s quote reminds us that getting older isn't a limitation. An advanced age should actually be seen as a great advantage, for one is more wiser, has more years of real-world experience, wisdom, and skills.
So, instead of waiting for the "perfect time", or feeling intimidated to start something in more advanced stages of life, always remember that one can do anything at any age if there's a will and conviction. Success requires a commitment to continuous learning and self-education, regardless of where you are in life.
How is it relevant today?
Many young and mid-career professionals feel that they must achieve everything in their 20s or 30s. They feel impatient and quite hopeless if they don't see rewards coming soon their way.
Modern career paths are no longer linear; second careers, late-stage startups, and skill resets are becoming common and successful.
Social media often celebrates very young achievers. This explains why people who are older feel that they have been left behind, or are "too late" to the game.
Women in particular often pause, or delay their career ambitions due to family responsibilities, and when they grow older, they make their age an excuse for starting something new.
Continuous learning has become essential today, as industries and technology change rapidly.
Lessons from the quote
Older age should not be seen as a disadvantage. After all, with age comes valuable experience, wisdom, and maturity that young founders often lack.
It is never too late to reinvent yourself or start a brand-new journey.
Prior experience and fresh learning are a powerful combination for success.
Fear of time running out should be used as motivation to act, not as an excuse to give up.
Education and self-belief are the ultimate tools for empowerment, especially for women.

Ahead of the festive season, Amazon India has announced the expansion of its Ashray network with 50 new centres across the country, taking the total number of operational centres to 200. The company said it remains on track to reach 250 Ashray centres by the end of 2026 as it continues to strengthen support infrastructure for delivery drivers.
Amazon India also expanded its mobile Ashray van initiative to Bengaluru, making it the fourth city after Delhi NCR, Mumbai, and Hyderabad to receive the service. Two mobile Ashray vans were flagged off in Bengaluru in the presence of Sandy Gordon, Vice President, Employee Experience and Relations, Amazon, and Brendan Branon, Vice President of North America (NA) Employee Relations (ER).
The move comes ahead of the festive shopping season, a period that typically sees a significant rise in e-commerce orders and last-mile deliveries across India.
Salim R. Memon, Director – Operations, Amazon India said, "With the festive season driving a sharp increase in deliveries, it's more important than ever that drivers across the industry have access to rest on their routes. Ashray was built on a simple idea — that every delivery driver, whether they deliver for Amazon or not, deserves a clean, cool place to rest during their workday. Expanding to 200 centres and bringing mobile vans to more cities means we can reach more drivers in more cities, right when they need it most. This expansion is part of Amazon India's broader investment of over INR 2,800 crore (~USD 300 million) in 2026 to strengthen associate safety, health, and financial well-being across its operations network."
Launched in 2024, the Ashray initiative has grown into one of India's largest delivery driver welfare programmes. The centres are open to all delivery drivers, including those not associated with Amazon. The facilities provide air-conditioned seating, drinking water, mobile charging points, clean washrooms, first-aid support, and designated rest areas. Each centre can accommodate 10 to 15 people at a time and allows free access for up to 30 minutes per visit. The centres operate throughout the year from 9 a.m. to 7 p.m. and are located at high-footfall areas such as petrol pumps and commercial hubs. Their locations are also listed on Google Maps to improve accessibility.
To complement the fixed centres, Amazon's mobile Ashray vans provide similar amenities directly on high-density delivery routes. The fully air-conditioned vans offer seating, drinking water, free Wi-Fi connectivity, and mobile charging facilities, allowing delivery personnel to take short breaks during work hours.
Ashray Expansion Timeline
- 2024: Pilot launched with Ashray centres across Delhi NCR, Bengaluru, and Mumbai.
- 2025: Expanded to 100 centres across 16 cities.
- May 2026: Added 50 new centres, taking the total to 150; mobile Ashray vans launched in Delhi NCR.
- September 2026: Announced 50 additional centres, increasing the total to 200; mobile Ashray vans now operational in Delhi NCR, Mumbai, Hyderabad, and Bengaluru.
- End of 2026 Target: 250 Ashray centres across India.
The latest expansion is part of Amazon India's broader investment in delivery associate welfare, logistics infrastructure, and last-mile operations as e-commerce demand continues to grow across the country.

Toshiaki Nomura, President and CEO, Canon India said, “India is central to Canon’s long-term growth ambitions, underpinned by the resilience of its economy and the emergence of new centres of enterprise and consumption. As education, digitisation and infrastructure reshape demand across Tier lll and Tier IV markets, we see a significant opportunity to unlock the next phase of growth for our printing business. Our ambition to build a network of over 10,000 active retailers across 700 cities by 2027 reflects our commitment to invest ahead of the curve and bring Canon closer to customers through trusted touchpoints that combine first-hand product experience with expert guidance. By combining scale with customer-led innovation and strong channel partnerships, we are positioning Canon to lead and shape the future of printing in India.”
To support the expansion, Canon India is strengthening its omnichannel distribution network across traditional resellers, large-format retail chains, e-commerce, quick commerce and enterprise-focused partners. The company currently operates more than 400 active PIXMA Zones across India and plans to add over 500 PIXMA Zone Lite stores this year. Its Canon eSHOP platform also allows authorised resellers to showcase and sell Canon products digitally.
The wider channel strategy is aimed at giving customers flexibility to research and purchase products across online and offline retail formats while enabling Canon to extend its presence beyond major metropolitan markets. Canon is also increasing investment in retailer engagement and frontline sales capabilities. Its Retail Display Incentive Program currently covers over 1,000 partners and focuses on strengthening product visibility at physical retail outlets.
At the same time, the company plans to scale its RetailChamp Initiative from 400 to more than 1,000 retail sales personnel. The programme focuses on improving product knowledge and customer consultation across the company's retail network. Beyond consumer retail, Canon India intends to expand its System Integrator network to more than 500 partners nationwide. The move is expected to increase its reach across enterprise, education and government segments.
C Sukumaran, Vice President, Canon India said, “Our channel ecosystem will be central to translating Canon’s growth ambition into business impact. As we expand our reach, our focus is on building the capabilities of our partners and frontline teams to understand local needs, create demand and deliver trusted customer experience. Through initiatives such as Canon Passport, RetailChamp and BizBee, we are strengthening partner engagement, knowledge and enablement across the ecosystem. BizBee, in particular, will equip our B2B partners and System Integrators with the training, certifications and business tools needed to unlock opportunities across enterprise, education and government segments. Together, these efforts will help us build a more capable partner network and drive solution-led growth across consumer, SME and institutional markets.”
Canon’s expansion strategy brings together physical retail, digital commerce, reseller engagement and B2B channel development as the company increases its reach across India. The planned addition of retailers, PIXMA Zone Lite stores, System Integrators and trained frontline personnel is expected to support Canon’s consumer printing business across smaller cities while strengthening its ability to serve education, SME, enterprise and institutional customers.
Carlsberg India has received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for its confidential pre-filing of documents for a proposed initial public offering (IPO). The company had submitted its draft IPO papers to SEBI through the confidential route in July 2026. This process allows companies to keep their draft offer documents private during the initial review, before deciding when to make the filing public.
The approval marks a key milestone in Carlsberg India’s proposed initial public offering (IPO). Details regarding the issue size, timeline, and other terms are expected to be disclosed in the offer documents, subject to the necessary regulatory and corporate approvals.
The proposed listing comes amid growing interest among multinational companies in India’s equity markets, as businesses look to unlock value from their investments in the country. The potential IPO would add to the activity in India’s primary market, with anticipated offerings from companies such as Jio Platforms drawing investor attention.
Carlsberg India commenced commercial operations in June 2007 with the launch of Carlsberg Green, entering India’s premium beer segment. Since then, the company has expanded its presence in the domestic beer market through a portfolio of brands, including Carlsberg and Tuborg.
The parent company has also reported positive volume growth across key markets. In its earnings guidance for the six months ended June 30, 2026, Danish brewer Carlsberg reported overall volume growth of 2.8%, while organic volume growth stood at 1.7%. Europe recorded volume growth of 0.1%, while the Central and Eastern Europe and India region registered growth of 6.2%.
The performance highlights the contribution of the Central and Eastern Europe and India region to the group's volume growth during the first half of 2026. With SEBI approval secured, Carlsberg India has taken another step toward its proposed public listing, with further details expected to emerge following the release of the relevant offer documents.
Global apparel retailer UNIQLO has reopened its expanded store at Ambience Mall, Gurugram, strengthening its retail presence in North India and offering customers a larger shopping destination featuring the brand’s latest seasonal collections and customer engagement initiatives.
The reopening was marked by a traditional Taiko drum performance, creating a festive atmosphere that attracted a large number of shoppers to the store. Customers visiting the revamped outlet were introduced to the expanded retail space and a wider assortment of products across key categories.
The enlarged store features UNIQLO’s latest Fall/Winter collection, including seasonal essentials such as Fleece, Knitwear, HEATTECH and PUFFTECH. The expansion is aimed at improving the overall shopping experience while providing consumers with greater access to the brand’s apparel and technology-driven clothing solutions.
In addition to the product showcase, UNIQLO introduced a series of customer-focused experiences designed to encourage participation and community engagement. One of the highlights was the UNIQLO Share Wall, an interactive installation where visitors could share personal stories and experiences about what they appreciate most about the brand.
The company also promoted sustainability through its RE: UNIQLO initiative. A dedicated donation box was installed at the store, encouraging customers to contribute pre-loved clothing that can be redirected to individuals and communities in need. The initiative forms part of UNIQLO’s broader efforts to support responsible consumption and extend the lifecycle of garments.
To celebrate the reopening, UNIQLO has announced a range of special promotional offers, available from October 2 to October 8. The limited-period deals are intended to drive footfall to the newly expanded outlet while giving customers an opportunity to explore the retailer’s latest collections and in-store experiences.
The Ambience Mall store expansion reflects UNIQLO’s continued focus on strengthening its retail footprint in India. By combining a larger retail format, seasonal product innovations, and community-driven initiatives, the brand aims to deepen its engagement with consumers while reinforcing its position in the country’s growing fashion and apparel market.
Reliance-backed online healthcare platform Netmeds reported steady financial performance for FY26, maintaining profitability despite recording only moderate growth in revenue.
Revenue from operations increased 2.3 percent to Rs 44.7 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 43.7 crore in FY25. The digital healthcare and online pharmacy platform posted a profit of Rs 5.5 crore during the fiscal year, continuing its profitable run despite a relatively stable topline.
Netmeds operates across multiple healthcare segments, including online pharmacy, diagnostics, teleconsultation services, and healthcare product sales. In addition to product transactions, the company derives income from healthcare-related services and marketing activities.
Services remained the primary contributor to the company’s business during the year. Gross service income stood at Rs 46.3 crore, largely unchanged from Rs 46.2 crore reported in the previous fiscal. Revenue generated from the sale of goods, however, registered stronger growth, rising 24 percent to Rs 6.03 crore from Rs 4.86 crore in FY25.
Netmeds reported operating revenue of Rs 44.7 crore. The company also earned Rs 3.24 crore from non-operating income, taking its total income to Rs 47.94 crore for FY26.
The company significantly increased spending on brand visibility and customer outreach initiatives during the year. Advertising and promotional expenses jumped 76 percent to Rs 2.9 crore, compared to Rs 1.65 crore in FY25. Additional overhead expenses, including legal, professional, and rental costs, amounted to Rs 12.24 crore.
Overall expenditure increased to Rs 42.4 crore from Rs 41.6 crore in the previous fiscal year. Despite the rise in costs, Netmeds remained in the black, although its profit declined by around 5 percent year-on-year.
The company reported a return on capital employed (ROCE) of 4.5 percent and an EBITDA margin of 5.66 percent. Operational efficiency remained largely stable, with Netmeds spending approximately Rs 0.95 to generate every Re 1 of operating revenue, in line with FY25 levels.
Reliance Industries, through Reliance Retail Ventures Ltd. (RRVL), acquired a majority stake in Netmeds for approximately Rs 620 crore in August 2020 as part of its expansion into the digital healthcare and e-pharmacy sector.
Netmeds competes with major players in India’s online healthcare market, including Tata 1mg, PharmEasy and Apollo 24/7. During FY26, Tata 1mg reported Rs 2,936 crore in revenue while posting a consolidated loss of Rs 287 crore, whereas API Holdings, the parent company of PharmEasy, reported Rs 6,869 crore in revenue.
Cinema exhibitor Cinépolis India has strengthened its presence in Haryana with the launch of a new four-screen multiplex at Amolik’s City Life Mall in Sector 28, Faridabad.
With the latest opening, the company has doubled its footprint in the city to eight screens, less than a year after inaugurating its first Faridabad property at Pacific Mall.
The newly launched multiplex houses 549 seats across four screens and offers recliner seating, Dolby sound technology and the brand’s food and beverage services. The opening comes ahead of the Gandhi Jayanti holiday weekend and the release of Drishyam: The Conclusion on October 2.
The expansion is part of Cinépolis India’s broader growth strategy across the Delhi-NCR cinema market. In recent months, the multiplex chain has added new properties at IREO Grand High Street in Gurugram and Dwarka, taking its regional network to 16 cinemas and 78 screens.
Devang Sampat, Managing Director, Cinépolis India said, "For us, growth is really a catchment question. Sector 28, has settled residential neighbourhoods on every side, and Faridabad is a big city, so there's room here for more than one Cinépolis. The choice of mall matters just as much. Amolik has built City Life as a place where families already come to eat and shop, and a good cinema gives them one more reason to spend the evening there. When a cinema runs well, the businesses around it do well too."
Located in the residential hub of Sector 28, City Life Mall has been developed by Amolik, whose portfolio in Faridabad also includes projects such as Amolik Heights and Amolik Residency.
Canon India has announced plans to expand its consumer printing distribution network to more than 10,000 active retailers across 700 cities by the end of 2027, doubling its current reach as the company looks to capitalize on growing demand for printing solutions across India.
The expansion comes amid sustained double-digit growth in Canon’s consumer printing business and is aimed at increasing product accessibility across Tier II, III, and IV markets. The company expects the initiative to support growth across consumer, SME, education, enterprise, and institutional segments.
Through its planned expansion across 700 cities, the company aims to improve product availability, enhance brand visibility, and provide greater access to consultation and after-sales support.
Toshiaki Nomura, President & CEO, Canon India, said, “India is central to Canon’s long-term growth ambitions, underpinned by the resilience of its economy and the emergence of new centres of enterprise and consumption. As education, digitisation and infrastructure reshape demand across Tier 3 and Tier 4 markets, we see a significant opportunity to unlock the next phase of growth for our printing business. Our ambition to build a network of over 10,000 active retailers across 700 cities by 2027 reflects our commitment to invest ahead of the curve and bring Canon closer to customers through trusted touchpoints that combine first-hand product experience with expert guidance. By combining scale with customer-led innovation and strong channel partnerships, we are positioning Canon to lead and shape the future of printing in India.”
To support the expansion, Canon is enhancing its omnichannel strategy across traditional retail, large-format stores, e-commerce, quick commerce, and enterprise-focused channels. The company currently operates more than 400 PIXMA Zones nationwide and plans to add over 500 PIXMA Zone Lite stores this year. Its Canon eSHOP platform also enables authorized resellers to showcase and sell products digitally.
Canon is further strengthening its partner ecosystem through initiatives such as the Canon Passport Program, which supports more than 5,000 reseller partners, and the newly launched BizBee platform for system integrators and value-added resellers. BizBee will provide partners with training, certifications, incentives, and business tools to enhance solution-led selling.
The company is also investing in retail engagement programs, including the Retail Display Incentive Program and RetailChamp Initiative, which is being expanded from 400 to over 1,000 retail sales personnel to improve product expertise and customer support.
Milky Mist Dairy Food Limited has commissioned a new 10 MW solar power plant at Arasanoor, further strengthening its renewable energy infrastructure and sustainability initiatives. The latest addition comes alongside the 15 MW solar facility already operational at the same location, taking the company’s total investment in the 25 MW Arasanoor solar project to Rs 109.60 crore.
With the commissioning of the new facility, Milky Mist’s renewable energy portfolio has grown to 41 MW. The company’s renewable assets now include 5 MW at Chithode, 9 MW at Kavilipalayam, 25 MW at Arasanoor, and 2 MW of wind power at Kayathar. According to the company, renewable energy sources now meet its entire power requirement across operations.
The solar installations have been developed on arid and open land that is not suitable for agricultural use, allowing the company to utilize such areas for renewable energy generation while supporting its sustainability goals.
The newly operational 25 MW solar facility is expected to generate around 20 million units of renewable electricity annually and supply power to Milky Mist’s integrated manufacturing facility in Perundurai as well as its milk chilling centers. The additional capacity is also projected to reduce dependence on conventional energy sources and help avoid nearly 16,000 tonnes of carbon emissions every year.
Beyond solar and wind energy, the company has invested in steam turbine technology and a methane gas purification plant that generates approximately 15,000 units of electricity daily. Methane produced through effluent treatment processes is purified and converted into compressed natural gas (CNG), while biomass is also used in boiler operations to further reduce reliance on conventional energy sources.
T Sathish Kumar, Chairman and Managing Director, Milky Mist Dairy Food Limited said, “At Milky Mist, our approach to growth has always been guided by a long-term vision of building a business that is responsible in its use of resources and conscious of its impact on the environment. We believe that sustainability must be embedded in the way an enterprise is built, operated and scaled, rather than viewed as a standalone initiative. Our investments in renewable energy, resource-efficient technologies and alternative sources of power are a reflection of this philosophy. The commissioning of our new 10 MW solar power plant is another significant step in this journey, taking renewable sources to over 90% of our total power requirements. As we continue to expand our operations, our endeavour is to strengthen energy self-sufficiency, advance more sustainable manufacturing practices and create enduring value for our business, our stakeholders and the environment.”
The latest investment aligns with Milky Mist’s broader strategy of building a technology-driven and resource-efficient manufacturing ecosystem, while continuing to explore opportunities to enhance energy efficiency and expand the use of renewable power across its operations.
Amazon India has expanded its ultra-fast delivery service, Amazon Now, to more than 120 cities across the country, doubling the service’s reach within two weeks. The expansion brings the quick-commerce offering to several new markets, including Amritsar, Abohar, Jalandhar, Ambala, Mangalore, Manipal, Visakhapatnam, Kochi, Changanassery, Bhubaneswar, and Karwar.
Amazon Now enables customers to receive deliveries within minutes and offers access to a broad assortment of daily essentials. The service covers categories such as groceries, including fresh fruits and vegetables, frozen foods, personal care products, beauty items, fashion, small appliances, home essentials, and kitchen products.
To support the growing network, Amazon is leveraging nearly 800 micro-fulfilment and urban fulfilment centres across India. The infrastructure is designed to facilitate rapid deliveries while expanding product availability in both metropolitan and emerging markets.
Harsh Goyal, Vice President – Everyday Essentials, Amazon India said, "We are delighted to take ultra-fast deliveries with Amazon Now to India’s hinterland – from Amritsar & Abohar in the north to Kochi & Changanassery in the south – ahead of the Amazon Great Indian Festival. Amazon Now continues to be the fastest-growing ecommerce business unit in Amazon India's history with orders doubling every quarter. This accelerated rollout underscores our commitment to making fast & reliable delivery accessible to customers across the country. We look forward to continue scaling up and offering the widest selection of products at the fastest delivery speeds this festive season.”
The announcement follows Amazon’s recent disclosure that Amazon Now achieved an annualized gross sales run rate of $1 billion in India over the past three-month period. The company plans to further scale the service to more than 300 cities as it works toward building one of the country’s largest delivery-in-minutes networks.
Ahead of the Amazon Great Indian Festival, which begins on October 8, customers using Amazon Now will have access to deals across multiple product categories. Amazon will also offer a 10 percent instant discount on SBI Credit Cards, Debit Cards, and EMI transactions, while Prime members will be eligible for additional savings on select purchases.
Acerpure India, a part of the Acer Group, has introduced its new Nitro QLED TV range in India. The smart TV lineup is now available on Flipkart and includes 75-inch, 85-inch, and 100-inch screen variants, targeting consumers seeking large-screen home entertainment and gaming experiences.
The new Nitro QLED TVs combine QLED display technology with a 120Hz HSR refresh rate, aimed at delivering smoother visuals for gaming, sports broadcasts, and high-motion content. The televisions also support Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos, offering enhanced picture quality and audio performance. The range runs on Google TV 5.0 Ref+, providing access to streaming platforms, smart TV features, and connected entertainment services.
In terms of audio, the 75-inch and 85-inch models come equipped with 40W box speakers, while the 100-inch variant features a 65W box speaker system. The televisions also include a built-in karaoke feature, expanding their entertainment offering for family and group viewing.
Vasudeva G, Director, Acerpure India said, “The way consumers experience entertainment at home is evolving rapidly, and we see a growing desire for experiences that are not just bigger, but genuinely more immersive and engaging. With Nitro, we are bringing the scale of the big screen into the living room and creating a proposition that is as much about the experience as it is about the technology behind it. The 75-inch, 85-inch, and 100-inch formats reflect our ambition to make larger-than-life entertainment more accessible to Indian consumers. Our association with Akshay Kumar as the brand ambassador for Acerpure further strengthens this vision of connecting technology with contemporary lifestyles and entertainment. Through our partnership with Flipkart, we are excited to take this proposition to consumers across the country.”
The launch comes as demand for premium smart TVs, large-screen displays, connected home entertainment devices, and gaming-focused televisions continues to grow in India. With larger display options and advanced audio-visual features, Acerpure is expanding its presence in the consumer electronics and smart TV market. The Acerpure Nitro QLED TV range is available on Flipkart, with prices starting at Rs 59,999.
ICA-GemLab, an international organisation specialising in diamonds, coloured gemstones, and jewellery testing, is set to open its first laboratory in India this October. The new facility will be located in Surat, Gujarat, a major global hub for diamond processing, jewellery manufacturing, and gemstone trade. The laboratory will offer testing, certification, and reporting services for diamonds, coloured gemstones, and jewellery, providing manufacturers, traders, retailers, jewellery brands, and consumers with access to gemological analysis within India.
The Surat facility marks ICA-GemLab’s first laboratory in the Indian subcontinent and forms part of the organisation’s expansion strategy to strengthen its presence in key global gems and jewellery sourcing markets. The laboratory will operate in coordination with ICA-GemLab’s headquarters in Bangkok and its existing offices in Dubai and Hong Kong.
As one of the world's leading centres for diamond cutting, polishing, and jewellery production, Surat plays a critical role in the global gems and jewellery supply chain. The new laboratory aims to provide testing and reporting services closer to the manufacturing and trading stages before products enter retail channels. ICA-GemLab is affiliated with the International Colored Gemstone Association (ICA), a global trade body representing the coloured gemstone industry. The Surat laboratory will follow the reporting standards, analytical procedures, and professional practices adopted across the ICA-GemLab network.
Kalpesh Desai, who will lead ICA-GemLab India as Director said, “India has a significant share of the world’s diamond processing, with Surat being one of its key centres. Our aim is to provide direct access to our internationally established analytical methods and reporting standards to manufacturers, traders, retailers, designers and consumers. We are working with a long-term plan. We aim to provide reliable gemological information, documented methodologies and analysis that can help traders and consumers make decisions based on appropriate information.”
Amira Hatta, Managing Director, ICA-GemLab Global said, “India is one of the most important markets in the global gems and jewellery industry. Opening a laboratory in Surat will bring our analytical capabilities directly to this market, so that customers will have access to our services closer to where they operate.”
The laboratory will issue three categories of reports: Diamond Reports, Coloured Gemstone Reports, and Jewellery Reports. These services will cater to jewellery manufacturers, wholesalers, gemstone traders, retailers, jewellery designers, industry professionals, and end consumers.
Headquartered in Bangkok, ICA-GemLab currently operates offices in Dubai and Hong Kong. The organisation also works with Sri Lanka’s National Gem and Jewellery Authority to provide gem testing services in the country. The launch of the Surat laboratory represents the latest step in its international expansion within the gems, diamonds, and jewellery certification sector.
ITC Ltd has acquired the remaining 52.5 percent stake in Sproutlife Foods Private Ltd for approximately Rs 645 crore, taking full ownership of the health foods company and making it a wholly owned subsidiary. According to a regulatory filing, the FMCG major purchased 13,445 equity shares of Sproutlife Foods through a secondary cash transaction. Following the acquisition, ITC's shareholding in the company has increased from around 47.5 percent to 100 percent.
The transaction was completed on September 28, and Sproutlife Foods became a wholly owned subsidiary of ITC with effect from the same date. The company stated that no regulatory approvals were required for the acquisition. The move is aligned with ITC's strategy to strengthen its presence in the packaged foods, health foods, nutrition products, and FMCG segments while expanding its future-ready food portfolio.
Sproutlife Foods owns and markets products under the Yoga Bar brand, which operates in the healthy snacks, breakfast cereals, protein products, and nutrition-focused food categories. Founded in February 2015, the company has reported steady growth over the past three financial years.
The company recorded a turnover of Rs 452 crore in FY2025-26, up from Rs 200 crore in FY2024-25 and Rs 108 crore in FY2023-24, reflecting strong growth in India's health and wellness food market. The acquisition further strengthens ITC's position in the fast-growing health foods and packaged nutrition category, where consumer demand for better-for-you food products continues to rise.
Pepperfry has entered into a strategic partnership with Imaginest, a home interiors and modular solutions company promoted by the founders of Capstone Life, to strengthen its presence in the modular furniture and home interiors segment. The collaboration will combine Imaginest's design, manufacturing, and project execution capabilities with Pepperfry's omnichannel retail network, consumer reach, and home category expertise. The companies aim to offer customers an integrated experience covering design, customization, manufacturing, delivery, installation, and after-sales support.
The partnership is intended to simplify the home interiors journey by addressing common challenges such as dealing with multiple vendors, pricing transparency, and project execution timelines. Through the association, customers will be able to access modular home solutions through selected Pepperfry store locations.
Umesh Sangurmath, Founder, Capstone Life said, "The home interiors journey continues to be fragmented, particularly as customers look for reliable partners who can manage the journey from design to execution. Imaginest was created to bring thoughtful design and quality execution together. Our partnership with Pepperfry allows us to bring this proposition to customers in key markets, combining our capabilities with Pepperfry’s strong consumer presence and making the process of creating a home simpler and more predictable."
Balavender Singh, CEO, Imaginest added, "Our partnership with Pepperfry is about creating a better modular home experience for customers in major markets. By combining Imaginest’s design and execution capabilities with Pepperfry’s consumer connect and Store ecosystem, we can bring greater transparency, accountability and speed to the journey from the first design conversation through to installation and after-sales support. Together, we see an opportunity to build a differentiated modular proposition in the markets that matter most to today’s urban homeowner."
Ashish Shah, Co-Founder and CEO, Pepperfry said, "Modular furniture and home interiors are important growth areas for Pepperfry. Partnering with Imaginest strengthens our design and execution capabilities and enables us to deliver a more integrated modular experience to customers in key markets. Together, we aim to combine greater choice and transparent pricing with dependable execution and long-term product support."
The rollout will initially cover selected Pepperfry stores in major cities and key markets, with plans to expand the partnership's footprint over time. The collaboration comes as demand for modular kitchens, wardrobes, storage solutions, and customized home interiors continues to grow in India's home improvement and furniture retail market. Industry players are increasingly focusing on end-to-end solutions that combine design expertise, execution capabilities, and omnichannel customer engagement.
Flipkart has announced a major expansion of its supply chain and logistics infrastructure ahead of The Big Billion Days and the upcoming festive shopping season. Through its logistics arm Ekart, the company has added 14 million cubic feet of warehousing space across India, increasing its storage capacity by 50 percent. The e-commerce company said technology and automation upgrades have also increased peak processing capacity by more than 30 percent, enabling faster order fulfilment and delivery during the high-demand festive period.
To strengthen last-mile delivery capabilities, Ekart has added more than 900 delivery hubs across the country. The expansion is aimed at increasing same-day and next-day deliveries as online shopping demand rises during the festive season. With these additions, Ekart's network now includes more than 8,200 facilities, comprising fulfilment centres, sortation hubs, and last-mile delivery operations. The company also operates nearly 1,200 Flipkart Minutes micro-fulfilment centres across more than 150 cities.
As part of its efforts to support MSMEs, small businesses, artisans, weavers, and marketplace sellers, Flipkart has pre-positioned more than 2.5 crore product units in Ekart fulfilment centres ahead of the festive sale. The company has also opened 70 additional pick-up stations in key seller clusters to reduce fulfilment timelines and improve inventory movement.
Ekart's third-party logistics (3PL) franchise network has grown to 600 locations within two months of launch, enabling businesses beyond the Flipkart marketplace to access logistics and delivery services during the festive season. The company has also expanded its delivery footprint by adding more than 750 new PIN codes. The expansion includes regions such as Leh in Ladakh, Kargil in Jammu and Kashmir, parts of Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh, and several locations across the Northeast, including Kamalanagar and Zamuang in Mizoram, Turacity, Resubelpara and Rajabala in Meghalaya, and Bomdila and Tezu in Arunachal Pradesh.
Hemant Badri, Senior Vice President and Head, Supply Chain, Flipkart Group said, "Every year, The Big Billion Days raises the bar for what customers expect: faster deliveries and wider reach. This year, a customer in Leh or Kargil will experience Big Billion Days for the first time. Across Ekart and Flipkart Minutes, we now operate over 8,200 facilities, allowing us to take the festive experience to more customers while helping sellers reach buyers they could not reach before."
To support increased operational demand, Flipkart has announced the creation of more than 2.5 lakh direct and indirect employment opportunities during the festive season. Of these, nearly 75,000 roles are expected to be filled by first-time workforce entrants. Around 60 percent of the new opportunities will be focused on last-mile delivery operations, reflecting the company's emphasis on faster deliveries and the continued expansion of Flipkart Minutes across Tier ll and Tier lll cities.
The company also highlighted measures for delivery personnel, known as Wishmasters. These include term life insurance, personal accident coverage, mediclaim benefits, access to a Doctor on Call service, festive-season bonuses, referral incentives, and AI-enabled onboarding through the Flipkart Delivery Partners app. The expansion underscores Flipkart's focus on strengthening its e-commerce logistics network, supply chain capabilities, seller ecosystem, and quick commerce operations ahead of one of India's largest online shopping events.
The Adie Broswon Group has entered the whisky segment with the launch of Kingpin Whisky, expanding its spirits portfolio across Delhi, Punjab and Chandigarh. The launch comes as India’s whisky market continues to record growth, with brands increasingly catering to consumers across different price points and consumption occasions.
According to IWSR data cited by the company, India recorded 4 percent growth in beverage alcohol volumes in 2025, while Indian whisky volumes also increased by 4 percent during the year. Against this backdrop, Kingpin has been introduced with a focus on combining a distinctive whisky profile with accessible pricing.
Kingpin is made using a blend of malts and Indian grain spirits. The product is designed to combine the character of malt whisky with the smoothness and versatility associated with grain spirits.
The whisky undergoes maturation and filtration, with the resulting profile featuring smoky notes alongside hints of tobacco and honey. The company said the product has been developed to offer a balanced drinking experience while retaining a pronounced character.
The brand is positioned around the philosophy “Live Bold. Drink Bold.” Its packaging uses a royal blue and gold colour scheme, with a crown-inspired insignia forming part of the visual identity.
Kingpin is being introduced in seven pack sizes: 1,000 ml, 750 ml, 500 ml, 375 ml, 180 ml, 90 ml and 60 ml. The range is intended to address different consumption occasions and price points across its initial markets.
The 750 ml bottle is priced at Rs 500 in Delhi, Rs 530 in Chandigarh and Rs 750 in Punjab. The varied pricing reflects differences across state markets, where alcoholic beverage taxation and pricing structures can vary.
The launch is part of the Adie Broswon Group’s broader focus on developing its own alcoholic beverage brands alongside its existing brewing and distillation operations.
Headquartered in Delhi NCR, the Group has interests across sugar, brewing, distillation and renewable energy. Its integrated 170-acre agro-industrial complex in Kiri Afgana, Batala, includes a sugar mill, three distilleries and a brewery.
The facility is supported by more than 6,000 professionals, according to the company. The Group operates under the philosophy “Victory in Every Field” and continues to expand its presence across its businesses under the leadership of Mrs. Jasdeep Kaur Chadha.
With its initial launch across Delhi, Punjab and Chandigarh, Kingpin marks the Group’s latest move into the consumer-facing whisky category, adding another offering to India’s competitive Indian Made Foreign Liquor (IMFL) market.
Food brand Kkhavo, known for its heritage Kala Namak Rice, has entered the cookware segment with the launch of Kkhavo Kitchen, a premium range of Tri-Ply Mini Cookware designed for smaller portions, quick meals, reheating and serving.
The new range comprises four products—Mini Kadahi, Mini Fry Pan, Mini Sauce Pan and Mini Square Pan—with individual pieces priced between Rs 699 and Rs 799. The Mini Kadahi, Mini Fry Pan and Mini Sauce Pan are also available as a three-piece set priced at Rs 1,749. As part of the festive launch, the brand is offering introductory discounts of up to 40%.
With Kkhavo Kitchen, the brand is expanding its food-focused portfolio into cookware, bringing together its existing food proposition with the manufacturing experience of Co-founder Mudit Goel.
Before founding Kkhavo, Goel built a stainless-steel business with experience spanning manufacturing, operations, supply chains and exports to international markets. The new cookware business draws on this background, with the brand positioning the range around quality, functionality and contemporary design.
“Kkhavo Kitchen brings together two journeys that are deeply connected to my experience. Having built a stainless-steel exports business and worked across international markets, I have always understood the importance of quality, functionality and precision in manufacturing,” said Mudit Goel, Co-founder, Kkhavo.
The Mini Cookware range features a three-layer construction comprising 304 stainless steel, an aluminium core and 430 magnetic stainless steel. According to the brand, the construction is designed to support even heat distribution and reduce hot spots.
The cookware is available in 12 cm to 15 cm formats, with capacities ranging from 550 ml to 600 ml. The pieces feature a brushed stainless-steel finish, silicone-grip handles and a stainless-steel cooking surface without an applied non-stick coating.
The range is compatible with induction and gas cooktops and follows a “Cook • Reheat • Serve” proposition, allowing consumers to use the same vessel across different stages of food preparation and serving.
Kkhavo Kitchen is positioning the mini-sized formats for smaller portions, quick meals, reheating and direct serving. The brand said the compact format is intended to offer versatility while taking up less space in the kitchen.
The cookware comes with a five-year warranty and is ISI certified. Its design combines a brushed-steel finish with subtle branding and silicone-grip handles.
The range allows Kkhavo to extend its positioning around food quality from ingredients into the cooking and serving process, while also entering a broader kitchenware market. The cookware range is being introduced ahead of the festive season, with discounts of up to 40% intended to support initial consumer trials.
Ranbir Kapoor has entered India's fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) sector with the launch of Flux Theory, a new personal care brand focused on the body wash category. The venture was founded in partnership with Advay Jhunjhunwala and venture-building platform Think9. Launched in Mumbai, Flux Theory enters the shower and personal care market with a range of body wash products designed around different consumer preferences, combining skincare benefits, fragrance profiles, and personality-led positioning.
The brand's initial portfolio includes five body wash variants: Sage, Sport, Lover, Dreamer, and Rebel. Each product has been developed with a specific fragrance profile and targeted skin-care benefits, including hydration, deep cleansing, exfoliation, brightening, and moisturisation. The range features fragrances such as bergamot, mint, santal, leather, and oud. According to the company, the products are intended to offer consumers a wider set of choices within the body wash segment beyond traditional functional attributes.
Flux Theory enters a category that continues to see growth in India. According to Euromonitor International, India's bath and shower market grew 4 percent in value during 2025 to reach retail sales of Rs 35,370 crore. Research by Mintel found that 65 percent of Indians were not using body wash in 2024, highlighting opportunities for category expansion. The company said its strategy is focused on attracting first-time body wash users while also encouraging existing consumers to explore alternatives within the shower care segment. The brand plans to build an omnichannel presence across digital and physical retail channels as it expands its reach.
As Founder, Ranbir Kapoor has been involved in developing the brand's proposition, product experience, creative direction, and visual identity from the early stages.
Kapoor said, “I have always been drawn to the idea that there is more than one side to each of us. As an actor, I experience that through the characters I play; in everyday life, we all move between different moods, roles and versions of ourselves. That was the thought behind Flux Theory. The shower is an everyday moment, but it can mark a shift in how you feel and what you are ready for next. That became the space in which we wanted to build Flux Theory. We have built each product around a distinct personality, fragrance and skin benefit, so people can choose what feels right for them in that moment. I’m excited to see Flux Theory start a new conversation in an everyday category and become a brand people return to as part of their routine.”
Advay Jhunjhunwala, Co-Founder, Flux Theory said, “The shower category has traditionally been led by function, familiarity and scale. While those remain important, consumers are increasingly looking for products that address specific skin needs and offer a more distinctive experience. Flux Theory brings together function, fragrance and personality in a way that gives consumers a new reason to choose body wash. Our ambition is to grow the category, bring more first-time users into it and give existing consumers a reason to switch. Ultimately, a daily-use brand earns its place through the product and the repeat purchase and that is what we are building towards.”
The Flux Theory product range is currently available through the brand's website as well as major e-commerce, beauty, and quick commerce platforms including Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra, Tira, Zepto, and Instamart. With the launch of Flux Theory, Kapoor joins a growing list of celebrities entering India's FMCG and personal care sector, as brands increasingly target younger consumers through differentiated products and omnichannel distribution strategies.
Rapido has expanded its food delivery business with the launch of Ownly in Hyderabad, making the city the platform’s second market after Bengaluru. The move marks the next phase of Ownly’s growth as it seeks to strengthen its presence in India’s food delivery sector. The food delivery app is now operational across Hyderabad, a city known for its strong food culture and large consumer base.
Through Ownly, Rapido is introducing a zero-commission model under which restaurants do not pay platform fees, while customers are charged a delivery fee based on the cost of the service. As part of the launch, Ownly highlighted the role of Rapido Captains, who will support food deliveries across the city alongside their existing responsibilities within Rapido’s mobility network. The company said the expansion is expected to create additional earning opportunities for Captains by enabling them to participate in food delivery demand.
To mark the launch, Ownly organised a gathering for Rapido Captains in Hyderabad. The event brought together delivery partners from across the city and was attended by Telugu actor Nani, who interacted with members of the Captain community.
Aravind Sanka, Co-Founder of Rapido and Ownly said, “Hyderabad is one of the most passionate food cities in the country, especially when it comes to biryani; and that makes it a natural next home for Ownly. Our model is simple: restaurants keep what they earn, customers pay only for their food and delivery, and nobody pays for anything in between. Bengaluru showed us that people respond to honesty in pricing, and we expect Hyderabad to hold us to it just as closely. It felt right to begin here with our captains, because they are the ones who carry this promise to every doorstep in the city.”
The company said its Captain network will continue to play a key role as Ownly scales operations across Hyderabad and expands its customer reach. Ownly's entry adds another player to Hyderabad’s food delivery market and reflects Rapido’s efforts to diversify beyond mobility services.
The platform is positioned around transparent pricing, affordability, and direct engagement with restaurants. With Hyderabad becoming its second operating city, Ownly is looking to expand its food delivery network while offering restaurants an alternative operating model and increasing delivery opportunities for Rapido Captains.
Mount Everest Breweries Limited (MEBL), an Indore-based beer manufacturer, has filed its Draft Red Herring Prospectus (DRHP) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for an Initial Public Offering (IPO). The issue comprises a fresh issue of up to 11.5 million equity shares with a face value of Rs 10 each. According to the DRHP, the company may also undertake a pre-IPO placement before filing the Red Herring Prospectus with the Registrar of Companies (RoC). Any amount raised through the pre-IPO placement will be adjusted against the fresh issue size.
The company plans to utilise Rs 230 crore from the fresh issue proceeds towards capital expenditure for a proposed brewing facility with a capacity of 1 million hectolitres per annum (HLPA). Another Rs 70 crore will be used for repayment or pre-payment of certain borrowings, while the remaining funds will be allocated for general corporate purposes.
The IPO is being offered through the book-building process, with up to 50 percent of the net offer reserved for qualified institutional buyers, while non-institutional investors and retail individual investors will receive at least 15 percent and 35 percent of the allocation, respectively.
Founded in 1999, Mount Everest Breweries is a beer brewing company with operations spanning brewing, packaging, sales, and distribution across economy, core, and premium beer categories. The company held a market share of nearly 36.3 percent in Madhya Pradesh by production volume in FY 2026 and currently operates across 16 states and three union territories.
MEBL currently operates two brewing facilities. Its Simrol facility in Indore was established in 2008, while its Mysuru facility was acquired in 2025. The company is also involved in contract brewing and contract manufacturing for other beer brands and has a brewing arrangement in Assam to serve the North-East market. Its proprietary beer portfolio includes Mount’s 6000, Lemount, Mount’s Lager, Dabang, and Stok, catering to multiple consumer segments. As of August 31, 2026, the company's products were available through 22,229 retail outlets and touchpoints across India.
Mount Everest Breweries is part of the Associated Kedia Group, which also includes Associated Alcohols and Breweries Limited (AABL). While MEBL focuses on beer production and distribution, AABL operates in the Indian-Made Foreign Liquor (IMFL), Indian-Made Indian Liquor (IMIL), Extra Neutral Alcohol (ENA), and ethanol segments. Both companies function independently under a non-compete agreement signed in April 2026.
The company operates two key business verticals. The first is its proprietary beer brands business, which focuses on brewing, packaging, sales, and distribution of its owned brands. The second is its contract brewing business, where it manufactures and packages beer for third-party brand owners.
